results.name: Agentic Attacks in the Wild: ARTEX & Offensive AI Frameworks
results.description: Between late September and November 2026, cloud environments experienced a surge in automated intrusions driven by agentic offensive frameworks, particularly ARTEX and its variants including Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, and HexStrike. These attacks leverage AI-driven automation to conduct noisy, vector-agnostic campaigns that spray credentials, probe endpoints, and abuse multiple access methods including stolen cloud keys, OAuth flows, and CI/CD trust relationships. Operators route attacks through residential proxy networks making IP-based blocking ineffective. Once initial access is achieved, agents systematically harvest credentials, explore lateral movement opportunities, and exfiltrate sensitive data including API keys and secrets. Poor operational security by attackers has resulted in exposed command-and-control panels revealing both attacker prompts and AI reasoning, providing unprecedented visibility into these machine-speed operations targeting cloud infrastructure and AI platform credentials.

results.name: Vmcloudoor: a stealthy backdoor targeting the Chinese cloud
results.description: A sophisticated Linux implant called Vmcloudoor has been discovered targeting virtual machines hosted on Chinese cloud platforms, specifically Alibaba, Tencent, and Huawei. The backdoor disguises itself by mimicking legitimate cloud service processes and adapts its concealment profile based on the detected environment. It establishes command-and-control communications through Alibaba Cloud infrastructure and Gitee, using time-constrained beacons with machine fingerprinting. The implant features command execution, file transfer capabilities, and system inventory collection. It actively detects security products including EDRs and AVs, adjusting its behavior accordingly. Analysis of the infrastructure suggests development by a Chinese pentester, potentially for red team operations, with evidence pointing to structured development practices and OPSEC failures revealing internal domains and GitHub accounts.

results.name: MoldyRoost: A Malvertising Machine Built to Deliver iOS Exploits
results.description: MoldyRoost represents a large-scale malvertising operation delivering nation-state-grade iPhone exploit chains through programmatic advertising. Between May and November 2026, over 480 ad domains across six sub-clusters targeted 47 countries, with particular focus on Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, the UK, and Turkey. The operation deploys four exploit kits (Coruna, DarkSword, SilkPath, and GhostWave) through cloaked landing pages that execute drive-by attacks requiring only loading the page on vulnerable iPhones. These kits target iOS versions 13.0 through 26, exploiting multiple zero-day vulnerabilities to exfiltrate cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases, keychain data, messages, and photos. The attackers combine sophisticated cloaking techniques with device fingerprinting to deliver exploits exclusively to iOS devices while showing benign content to others. A leaked repository revealed the operation's infrastructure, including version routers and channel-based attribution systems for stolen credentials.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: The extension you never installed: KREMLIN forges Chrome's own integrity checks to steal banking sessions
results.description: Brazilian banking malware operation REF9334 has been deploying KREMLIN toolkit since May 2025, targeting Brazilian financial institutions through malicious browser extensions. The operation uses multi-stage JavaScript loaders, custom C++ installers, and exploits Chromium integrity mechanisms by manipulating Secure Preferences and regenerating required HMACs. Infrastructure leverages Ethereum smart contracts as dead-drop resolvers for dynamic C2 configuration. Seven distinct campaigns over 15 months show evolution from PULSAR RAT to REMCOS RAT delivery. Attackers impersonate twelve Brazilian banks through Portuguese-language lures, with transaction patterns clustering during São Paulo working hours. The malicious extensions intercept credentials, session tokens, and sensitive banking data through keylogging and request interception capabilities. Over 1,500 infections have been temporarily disrupted through network canary registration, with 98.75% of victims located in Brazil.

results.name: RevStealer Malware: A Hidden Data Heist Behind the Promise of Free AI
results.description: RevStealer is an infostealer first identified in September 2026 targeting Windows systems through trojanized Electron applications disguised as legitimate software, particularly a fake Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop lure. Distributed via GitHub repositories and game-cheat sites, the malware employs sophisticated evasion techniques including anti-debugging, anti-sandbox, anti-VM capabilities, and AES-256-CBC encryption. It conducts comprehensive data theft, harvesting browser credentials, session cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, VPN configurations, Windows Credential Manager data, password managers, messaging applications, and user documents. The malware features encrypted command-and-control communications with blockchain-based fallback using Polygon smart contracts, performs streaming exfiltration of stolen data, and self-deletes to minimize forensic traces rather than maintaining persistence. This rapid theft-focused execution model creates immediate compromise risks with minimal detection windows.

results.name: From Phishing Email to Azalea Agent: Uncovering a Multi-Stage Attack on Ukrainian Government Bodies
results.description: A sophisticated spear-phishing campaign targeted Ukrainian government bodies in October 2026, using a fraudulent email about financial assistance for military unit A1836. The attack employed a RAR archive containing a malicious LNK file that initiated a five-stage infection chain. The sequence began with a curl-based downloader, progressed through multiple encrypted stages including HIODropper and StageLoader, and culminated in the deployment of Azalea Agent 1.21.3, a .NET-based remote access trojan. The campaign utilized a C2 server at 151.244.30.176, historically associated with Iranian ISP Shatel before transitioning to a Canadian ASN. The infrastructure exposed multiple services including OpenSSH, NGINX, RDP, and potentially FRP-based tunneling capabilities. Despite thorough analysis, no definitive attribution to known threat groups was established, as Azalea Agent is a commercially available Malware-as-a-Service tool accessible to multiple operators.

results.name: CLoader Bot Campaign Targets Thai Organizations Through LuaJIT-Based Malware Delivery
results.description: A sophisticated campaign targeting organizations and individuals in Thailand has been identified, utilizing spear-phishing emails to deliver CLoader bot malware through a multi-stage infection chain. The attack begins with an obfuscated JavaScript file disguised as a PDF document using double-extension techniques. This JavaScript drops a LuaJIT executable along with an obfuscated Lua script, which serves as the malware interpreter. The payload employs multiple anti-analysis techniques including UPX packing, resource section obfuscation, and dynamic filename generation. The final payload establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry modifications while masquerading as legitimate Windows services. It communicates with command-and-control infrastructure via Pastebin-hosted configurations and supports remote code execution, PowerShell commands, and Windows Defender exclusion manipulation to evade detection and maintain operational capabilities.

results.name: Lost in relocation: analysis of a new loader distributing CASTLESTEALER
results.description: A previously undocumented Windows loader tracked as OXLOADER delivers the CASTLESTEALER infostealer through malicious Google Ads campaigns. The loader employs sophisticated evasion techniques including control-flow flattening, mixed Boolean-Arithmetic obfuscation, and abuse of the Windows .reloc section to stage shellcode. It incorporates five anti-VM and language checks, self-modifying decryption stubs, and masquerades as legitimate software like Node.js or API Monitor. CIS-region and Russian-language exclusions suggest a financially motivated, Russian-speaking threat actor. The loader achieves low detection rates across static engines and sandboxes, with victims redirected through intermediary domains to Storj-hosted batch scripts that download and execute the payload. The final stage uses DonutLoader to deliver CASTLESTEALER in-memory, targeting credentials and sensitive information.

results.name: Bazuka: The Fraud Framework That Can Do It All
results.description: In late October 2026, a new mobile threat called Bazuka was discovered while investigating an NFC card relay application. Unlike typical banking trojans with simple architectures, Bazuka is a comprehensive modular framework designed for fraudulent operations. The framework consists of a dropper/downloader, core component, and 23 specialized modules covering overlays, keylogging, SMS and 2FA interception, remote control, and cryptocurrency address swapping. Notable features include LLM integration within the control panel to help operators manage infections and identify high-value victims, plus ADB bridging capabilities for covert privilege escalation. Distribution occurs through traffers using lures like adult content, with plans for potential Google Play deployment using minimal permissions to bypass review processes. The control panel, partially in Russian, reveals sophisticated victim management tools and AI-assisted targeting capabilities.

results.name: Rotating Storefronts: Inside a Fake-Shop Network Gearing Up for Black Friday 2026
results.description: A sophisticated fake-shop operation has been identified preparing for Black Friday 2026, utilizing a Chinese-developed SaaS store builder platform called oemcart. The network operates 4,660 domains, with 3,415 observed between October and November 2026, rotating an average of 91 new domains daily. A single storefront was linked to 75 short-lived domains impersonating well-known retailers, primarily targeting Central and Eastern European, UK, and US shoppers. Aldi and Lidl are the most impersonated brands. The operation collects shopper contact details before payment attempts, while payment endpoints are supplied dynamically at checkout to evade detection. Infrastructure rotates between Cloudflare, Tencent Cloud, and Alibaba Cloud. A parallel network of 372 domains impersonates premium fashion brands using WordPress/WooCommerce. The operation employs multiple evasion techniques including daily domain rotation, server-side payment delivery, and CDN usage to hamper traditional detection methods.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: October 2026 Infostealer Trend Report
results.description: During October 2026, multiple infostealer families including Lzveil, StealC, Remus, DarkCloud, and AgentTesla were distributed through various channels. Distribution methods included SEO poisoning, file-hosting services, cloud storage platforms like Mega and Mediafire, and spear-phishing emails. Malware was frequently disguised as software cracks and keygens, with Microsoft Corporation being the most impersonated entity. EXE files constituted 98.4% of execution types, while DLL side-loading accounted for 1.6%. The newly identified Lzveil infostealer was distributed alongside Remus in password-protected archives. Email-based campaigns involved DarkCloud impersonating laboratory equipment companies and AgentTesla impersonating shipping firms. Both collected extensive system information, credentials, and sensitive data using SMTP and FTP exfiltration methods respectively.

results.name: October 2026 APT Attack Trends Report (Domestic)
results.description: During October 2026, multiple APT campaigns targeting South Korea were observed, primarily utilizing spear phishing and malicious HWP documents. Seven distinct attack types were identified, predominantly leveraging LNK files with PowerShell commands to deploy various payloads. Attackers employed cloud services like Dropbox, GitLab, and GitHub for command-and-control infrastructure and payload delivery. Common tactics included registry persistence, scheduled tasks, and DLL side-loading. The campaigns deployed remote access tools including XenoRAT, Xctdoor, and custom .NET-based RATs, alongside information stealers targeting browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and system information. One campaign specifically targeted defense industry personnel using weaponized Hangul documents. Post-compromise activities focused on reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and establishing persistent remote control capabilities through various backdoors and legitimate remote management tools like MeshAgent.

results.name: An AI-Augmented Cybercrime Operation
results.description: A French-speaking operator with minimal technical skills conducted a nine-day campaign in November 2026 targeting European banks, insurers, payment providers and municipalities using a jailbroken AI agent. The operator issued 1,801 plain-language commands in misspelled French while the AI agent autonomously wrote scanners, exploits, parsers and exfiltration scripts. The campaign exploited an exposed staging server containing prompt logs, stolen data, and operational tooling. More than 50 organizations across Belgium, France and Switzerland were targeted, resulting in successful breaches at an insurer and multiple municipalities through exposed analytics tools, weak passwords and unauthenticated endpoints. Standard security controls including MFA, IP allowlisting and server-side validation stopped exploitation attempts. The operation ceased when the model API key was revoked on November 14, 2026.

results.name: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com's High-Profile Heists
results.description: Multiple threat actors affiliated with Com have conducted persistent vishing campaigns targeting data-rich organizations since August 2026, leading to data theft and extortion attempts. The operations primarily focused on financial services, healthcare, and legal sectors in the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia. Attackers employed social engineering techniques, posing as IT support to direct victims to adversary-in-the-middle proxies that captured credentials and MFA tokens. Following initial access, threat actors established persistence through unauthorized MFA device enrollment, exfiltrated data using scripted methods and native cloud utilities, and sent extortion demands via internal communication channels. Two newly identified activity clusters, CL-CRI-1264 and CL-CRI-1274, demonstrated advanced techniques including malicious browser extensions with keylogging and remote control capabilities. These cybercriminals have shifted away from encryption-based extortion, enabling faster operations w...
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Inside a Gentlemen Ransomware-Linked Intrusion
results.description: A deception alert revealed a multi-week intrusion initiated through compromised credentials on an internet-facing Citrix VDI environment lacking MFA enforcement. The threat actor, whose credentials appeared in stealer-logs five days prior, systematically mapped Active Directory, executed large-scale account enumeration exceeding 41,000 queries, and accessed files containing plaintext passwords and tokens. The intrusion escalated to domain-level compromise when the operator reset and re-enabled a disabled Domain Admin account, modified privileged passwords, and added a service identity to Domain Admins group. Tools including SoftPerfect Network Scanner and FileZilla were staged and masqueraded. Approximately 270 SFTP connections to external servers were observed, indicating potential data exfiltration. The case demonstrates how stealer-log exposures combined with absent MFA and insecure credential storage enable rapid privilege escalation to domain administrator control.

results.name: Suspected DPRK Campaign staging PHP2Shell Targeting against Global PHP infrastructure
results.description: A Korean-speaking threat actor, tracked as the June 2026 Minjun campaign and linked with moderate confidence to North Korea's Lazarus Group, is actively planning targeted exploitation of two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that enable unauthenticated remote code execution. The campaign prioritizes government agencies, financial institutions, manufacturing, logistics, aviation, and trading platforms across the US, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the EU. Operators are using AI-assisted reconnaissance to rank public exploit code and plan sector-specific attacks. Exploitation attempts have been observed globally since 17 October 2026, with 17 suspected source IPs identified conducting web shell deployment and session poisoning. The vulnerabilities affect all internet-facing PHP installations below version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, with Apache mod_php at highest risk.

results.name: Infostealer riding the AI Train
results.description: Aokigahara is a newly identified infostealer with traditional data theft capabilities targeting browsers, VPN clients, cryptocurrency wallets, FTP/SFTP clients, password managers, and email applications. Its distinguishing feature is dedicated targeting of AI applications and development tools, including Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI. The malware collects authentication files, session data, and configuration files from these AI services, alongside developer credentials such as Git files, SSH private keys, and AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud credentials. Stolen AI credentials could enable unauthorized access to paid services, account resale, or data extortion. The stealer employs anti-analysis techniques including language checks, virtual machine detection, and control-flow flattening, and uses AES-256 encryption with X25519 key exchange for command-and-control communications.

results.name: VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability
results.description: VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-premises versions contain a critical SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with minimal privileges to escalate to superuser operator access. Any user with Enterprise Read Only role can exploit this flaw to access privileged internal functionality, potentially compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and managed data. The vulnerability is actively exploited, with specific malicious IP addresses identified. Affected versions include VCO 5.2.x prior to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.x prior to 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.x prior to 6.4.2.12. Hosted and dedicated VCO instances were already patched. Immediate upgrade to fixed releases is recommended, along with restricting web interface access and monitoring for suspicious activity.

results.name: 2026 Year End Phishing Lures
results.description: As organizations approach year-end and fiscal close periods, employees face increased administrative activity in finance, HR, and IT departments. This heightened legitimate communication creates ideal cover for phishing campaigns. Attackers exploit year-end business processes by impersonating compensation adjustments, Q4 financial documents, access reviews, invoice follow-ups, and benefits statements. Multiple campaigns have been observed targeting organizations across sectors including aviation, telecommunications, manufacturing, real estate, technology, and financial services, with concentration in the Middle East. Attackers leverage SharePoint, Docusign, and Microsoft 365 themes, employing credential harvesting pages disguised as document-sharing portals. Generic protected-message lures prove effective by requiring minimal customization while appearing legitimate during busy periods when employees expect increased document requests and administrative deadlines.

results.name: ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
results.description: Throughout October 2026, an actor utilizing ARTEX, an autonomous AI penetration-testing agent, targeted multiple IT and software vendors with attacks focused on identity providers including Okta, Entra, and Cognito. The activity overlaps with Storm-0940, a Chinese-state aligned actor involved in supply-chain attacks. Observed methodologies included mapping applications through JavaScript bundles and source maps, probing authentication mechanisms, manipulating OAuth callbacks, password-spraying corporate environments, abusing account recovery endpoints, and testing tenant isolation. Sessions lasted 24-30 hours with automatic IP rotation when blocked. The agent demonstrated agentic behavior through automated step chaining, output-based adaptation, and relentless iteration. Attacks featured coordinated bursts with unique user agents, one-second intervals between attempts, and targeting of software engineers across hundreds of users.

results.name: SEO Poisoning Campaign Delivers New Armorsteal Malware
results.description: In September 2026, an SEO poisoning campaign distributed Armorsteal malware through fake websites impersonating Chocolatey package manager and Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS) tool. Victims searching for software installation commands were presented with malicious PowerShell scripts that deployed Python-based malware protected by Pyarmor. The malware consists of three main components: a remote access module that communicates with command-and-control servers and verifies RSA-2048 signatures on received tasks; a surveillance module that logs keystrokes, monitors clipboard activity, hijacks cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and captures screenshots; and an information stealer targeting browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, passwords, and SSH keys. The campaign employed anti-analysis techniques including cloud provider detection and code obfuscation, with infrastructure changes observed throughout the monitoring period.

results.name: StealC Is Back, and This Time It's a RAT
results.description: Four months after Operation Endgame dismantled StealC in June, its seller returned in October with Stadia, a full-featured remote access trojan that incorporates StealC's code verbatim. Unlike its predecessor, Stadia offers comprehensive remote administration capabilities including hidden desktop control, live command shell, file explorer, process manager, and in-memory loader, with the original StealC stealer functioning as one of six modules. The operator targets former StealC customers by offering a free month on the top-tier subscription priced at $900 monthly. Analysis reveals the binary shares byte-for-byte code with StealC version 3.5, particularly the Chromium App-Bound Encryption helper. The agent communicates via plain HTTP to three hardcoded IP addresses, uses RC4 encryption with Base64 encoding, and establishes persistence through hidden scheduled tasks under C:\ProgramData\ with randomized directory names impersonating legitimate updaters. The transformation from simple infostealer to full RAT...

results.name: MythicRatatoskr: An Yggdrasil-enabled backdoor deployed in a UAC-0099-Sandworm collaboration
results.description: On July 16th, 2025, UAC-0099 conducted a spearphishing attack against a Ukrainian grain logistics company, deploying the MATCHWOK backdoor. The following day, attackers introduced MythicRatatoskr, a previously undocumented Go-based backdoor utilizing the Yggdrasil mesh network for command and control communications. This decentralized network enables end-to-end encrypted IPv6 traffic between nodes, complicating detection efforts. Approximately two months later, on September 17th, 2025, Sandworm executed a destructive data-wiping attack using the SDelete utility deployed via Active Directory Group Policy. This incident represents documented cooperation between UAC-0099, acting as an initial access broker, and Sandworm, responsible for the destructive phase. The MythicRatatoskr backdoor supports standard backdoor functionality including command execution, file transfer, screenshot capture, and SOCKS5 proxying capabilities, marking the first documented case of state-aligned actors exploiting Yggdrasil infrast...

results.name: Hunting Leaked PHP2Shell RCE Across Open Directories (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
results.description: Two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, leaked before their scheduled patch on October 21, 2026. The flaws involve out-of-memory corruption in PHP core through multipart/form-data parsing, exploitable via session.upload_progress without authentication. Scanning began approximately 20 minutes after the patch release, with activity traced to a Mirai-style IoT botnet. Analysis of attacker infrastructure revealed approximately ten workspaces staging php2shell tooling, targeting WooCommerce, WHMCS, and Magento platforms. Despite widespread exposure affecting over 683,000 IPs running vulnerable PHP versions, no successful in-the-wild exploitation was confirmed as of October 21, 2026. The technical difficulty of achieving reliable code execution on systems with address-space randomization limited successful compromises.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: M365 Token Spray and Replay Campaign Compromises Business Email Accounts
results.description: Between July and September 2026, a sophisticated campaign targeted Microsoft 365 accounts through adversary-in-the-middle attacks and token replay techniques. The operation captured sign-in sessions via AiTM relays and replayed stolen tokens from IP addresses controlled by German hosting provider 1337 Services GmbH. Over ten weeks, 79 organizations were compromised with 497 successful sign-ins against over 200,000 failed attempts. Attackers registered 48 rogue Entra devices, replaced victim MFA methods, and created hidden inbox rules to conceal malicious communications. The campaign evolved through four distinct phases, rotating through different IP addresses and employing both scripted token replay and browser session replay techniques. In one case, compromised accounts were used to send payroll-related emails to external contacts, demonstrating business email compromise objectives.

results.name: Inside SiriusQT: A Seriously Skilled RAT
results.description: SiriusQT is a Windows Remote Access Trojan advertised on dark web forums since April 2026, offering capabilities beyond remote administration including HVNC, credential theft, cryptocurrency wallet collection, clipboard monitoring, keylogging, process injection, and persistence mechanisms. Distributed via Malware-as-a-Service by a reseller named GhostKernel, at least 30 users purchased licenses ranging from monthly to lifetime access. The malware was observed targeting victims in the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, and the Netherlands. SiriusQT employs custom encrypted command-and-control traffic, multiple process injection techniques, and features both native C++ and .NET loader variants. The threat actor Amonus is referenced as the alleged developer, though GhostKernel appears to be the primary distributor through underground forums and Telegram channels.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: INC and The Gentlemen Ransomware: Exposed AI Infrastructure
results.description: Threat researchers discovered an AI-driven intrusion ecosystem operated by affiliates of INC Ransomware and The Gentlemen Ransomware groups through seven exposed command-and-control servers. The operators integrated commercial AI models via OpenCode and OpenRouter, logging over 8,000 messages across 133 sessions with recorded spending exceeding $23,000. They exploited edge devices at scale including FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, and cPanel systems, compromising thousands of targets. The infrastructure contained 46 custom INC encryptor builds staged for October 1, 2026 deployment, evidence of live victim encryption, and a custom arsenal including the Phantom autonomous framework, Ghost C2, and various exploitation tools. The campaign targeted 62 named organizations, predominantly in the United States, with focus on industrial manufacturing and healthcare sectors. OPSEC failures in late September 2026 exposed source code, credentials, AI session logs, and complete victim knowledge bases.

results.name: Inside a Global AI-Assisted Hacking Campaign
results.description: In October 2026, a Chinese-speaking threat actor conducted widespread AI-assisted cyberattacks combining the ARTEX penetration testing framework with multiple AI coding assistants including Claude Code, Codex, and Grok. The attacks, initially reported as targeting South Korean financial institutions, affected organizations globally across multiple industries including finance, retail, education, cryptocurrency, and telecommunications. Custom synchronization scripts maintained investigation context across AI sessions, while specialized agents divided reconnaissance and exploitation tasks. Prompts revealed requests for bulk personal data, transaction records, and mobile phone numbers, alongside questions about selling stolen information on underground markets. The workflow incorporated peer review between AI models, with GLM instructed to audit DeepSeek findings. Targeting spanned over 20 countries across Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America, indicating financially-motivated opportunistic attacks.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Recent AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks in Japan: Investigating Attack Infrastructure and Techniques
results.description: In October 2026, multiple organizations in Japan experienced unauthorized access incidents resulting in personal information leakage. Investigations revealed that attackers leveraged artificial intelligence to scan for known vulnerabilities and execute attacks through APIs. The threat actors analyzed Android application packages to identify and exploit APIs, testing for vulnerabilities including server-side request forgery. Multiple attack servers were identified containing tools for reverse engineering Flutter applications, analyzing Android apps, and targeting web applications, MySQL databases, Jenkins servers, and email gateways. Evidence suggests attempts to evade endpoint detection and response systems and deploy web shells for internal network access. The attacks also targeted web services beyond Japan, demonstrating a broader scope of malicious activity.

results.name: PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
results.description: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, collectively named PHP2Shell, were disclosed on October 21, 2026. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory handling corruption that can interrupt PHP while internal request data is partially initialized, leading to invalid data treatment. CVE-2026-109619 exploits stale global state where request-owned internal state survives after memory is freed. Both vulnerabilities can be exploited successfully on ARM64 systems and x86 systems without ASLR. Fixed versions include PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Over 2.6 million internet-facing hosts running PHP were identified as vulnerable, with 42% on end-of-life branches receiving no official patches. Early exploitation attempts were observed from multiple sources, including scanning activity and webshell deployment attempts targeting the upload-progress vulnerability path.

results.name: Stray Cat, Open Doors: How k0t Wanders Through the Network Edge
results.description: Group-IB and NyxLab uncovered a large-scale campaign by threat actor k0t exploiting FortiGate, FortiWeb, and Palo Alto GlobalProtect edge devices to harvest credentials and establish persistent access. The operation involves exploiting CVE-2025-64446 in FortiWeb and CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect, alongside brute-forcing attacks using custom tools. Over 70,000 exposed credentials were discovered, with victims spanning multiple industries globally. Post-compromise activities include credential theft, Active Directory enumeration, and data exfiltration via Rclone to cloud storage. Persistence is maintained through MeshCentral, AdaptixC2, and various RMM tools including Atera and AnyDesk. The campaign shows overlaps with Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware groups, suggesting k0t may operate as an Initial Access Broker, though direct affiliation remains unconfirmed.

results.name: "Next Exploit Opportunities": How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
results.description: A financially motivated threat actor operating under the handle BUGSTER leveraged jailbroken AI assistants, specifically the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4, to conduct multiple cybercrime operations across India. The actor, demonstrating limited technical skills but relying heavily on AI-generated scripts and reconnaissance, successfully exfiltrated over 5,200 personal records from a university database, conducted WordPress brute force attacks, and planned VoIP telecommunications fraud. Additional activities included Wi-Fi password cracking requiring physical proximity to targets, cryptocurrency whale reconnaissance, and development of credential scanning toolkits. The actor configured specialized AI bot profiles providing step-by-step criminal guidance, including fraud traffic ratios and carrier evasion techniques, demonstrating how AI lowers the skill barrier for cybercrime operations.

results.name: Amazon-Themed ClickFix Campaign Serves Up Finger-Licking Malware
results.description: Attackers leveraged a sponsored Google search result for 'amazon business' to redirect victims to a spoofed Amazon login page hosted on Google Sites. The page presented a fake CAPTCHA (ClickFix) that tricked users into executing a malicious command using Windows' finger utility, an obsolete network tool repurposed as a living-off-the-land binary. This initiated a complex infection chain downloading IronPython, executing obfuscated Python scripts, and deploying multiple payloads including Doina malware, Lumma Stealer via a Node.js package, and a pirated NetSupport Client RMM tool. The attack infrastructure predominantly used barbecue-themed domains for command and control. The campaign affected multiple organizations and demonstrates cross-platform capabilities, with alternate payloads prepared for macOS users. Attackers employed sophisticated obfuscation techniques including Base64 encoding with Cyrillic character substitution, XOR encryption, and RC4 decryption throughout the infection stages.

results.name: Uncovered and Disrupted BADBOX 3.0, the Largest Ad Fraud Operation by Bid Volume Ever Publicly Disclosed
results.description: BADBOX 3.0 represents the largest ad fraud operation ever disclosed, generating approximately 40 billion bid requests daily and comprising over 4% of all connected TV traffic. The operation primarily targets low-cost consumer devices infected with backdoors delivering fraud modules linked to TXCZ, a Chinese electronics manufacturer. These modules render invisible video ads while impersonating legitimate applications and enroll devices as exit nodes in eleven residential proxy networks, including PXYEDGE, the successor to IpMoYu from BADBOX 2.0. The operation also employs spoofed server-side ad insertion traffic. The campaign's volume exceeds the previous record holder VASTFLUX by three times and surpasses the combined volume of five years of prior investigations.

results.name: Device Code Phishing in Microsoft 365: Attack Analysis
results.description: In November 2026, a resurgence of device-code phishing campaigns targeted Microsoft 365 accounts using payment-themed emails and fake SharePoint workspaces. Attackers delivered obfuscated HTML and SVG attachments that redirected victims through verification gates to counterfeit document-sharing pages. These lures instructed recipients to enter attacker-supplied codes into genuine Microsoft authorization pages, exploiting the device-code authentication flow. When victims completed authentication, including MFA, attacker-controlled clients received access tokens with granted permissions. The campaigns employed sophisticated obfuscation techniques including fragment reversal, Base64 substitution, and XOR encoding. Session-status checks and heartbeat mechanisms coordinated the phishing pages with backend infrastructure. The attacks combined legitimate business correspondence pretexts with Microsoft's authentic sign-in infrastructure to deceive users into authorizing malicious access requests.

results.name: UAT-12643: Suspected North Korea-aligned actor blends blockchain resilience with targeted infostealing
results.description: A financially motivated threat group designated UAT-12643 has been discovered operating malicious infrastructure targeting cryptocurrency holders, gaming platform users, and VoIP software operators. The actor deploys multiple payloads including the Overlord RAT, Python-based Good Game infostealer, and a multi-cryptocurrency clipboard hijacker. The Overlord RAT employs an innovative command-and-control resilience technique by embedding encrypted server URLs in Solana blockchain transaction memos. Potential victims are located primarily in Europe based on file harvesting capabilities targeting English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese documents. The campaign demonstrates overlaps with known North Korean APT tactics, particularly through the use of Overlord RAT and Solana blockchain techniques previously attributed to Lazarus Group and UNK_DeadDrop cluster. Lure themes suggest targeting of finance staff, VoIP operators, and cryptocurrency users across multiple sectors.

results.name: N0N Ransomware Group: Victims, Leak Site, TTPs & IOCs
results.description: N0N is a financially motivated cyber extortion group that emerged in September 2026, employing data theft and extortion tactics without using traditional encryption methods. The group leverages compromised credentials obtained from third-party infostealer campaigns to infiltrate corporate networks. Once inside, they exfiltrate sensitive information including Active Directory mappings and legal documents, then threaten public disclosure via dark web leak sites to coerce ransom payments. N0N targets multiple sectors including investment services, telecommunications, retail, education, and pharmaceuticals across 54 countries. Their approach avoids conventional file encryption, instead manipulating victim data through administrative tools, making detection more challenging for traditional security controls.

results.name: Inside the 'Party' Panel: How Fraudsters Rent Android Banking Trojans to Target Indian Bank Customers
results.description: A multi-tenant malware-as-a-service platform enables fraudsters to deploy fake Google Play pages and branded Android banking trojans targeting Indian financial institutions. The operation, discovered via an unprotected server, hosted 50 tenant accounts with 34 active paid licenses targeting customers of six Indian banks and card issuers. Victims are lured through convincing fake Play Store pages that harvest card details, CVV, and personal information before delivering a two-stage malware. The dropper bypasses Android 13+ security by impersonating the Play Store installation process, while the hidden payload steals SMS-based OTPs, uploads sensitive photos, and redirects phone calls using call-forwarding codes. The infrastructure leverages Firebase and Telegram for command-and-control, with all indicators pointing to an India-based operator exploiting Indian hosting providers and targeting domestic financial customers and government service users.

results.name: Unsolicited audits: how AuditTeam masks ransomware
results.description: AuditTeam is an active threat group operating since January 2026, using the sophisticated OpsAgent framework to compromise organizations across multiple countries including Russia, Italy, Philippines, Hong Kong, Senegal, Finland, and China. The group demands an 'Audit & Consulting fee' for vulnerability reports, masking ransomware operations as security consulting. OpsAgent evolved from C++ to Rust implementation, providing extensive capabilities including file system management, process injection, privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, and network pivoting. The framework uses AWS CloudFront subdomains for command-and-control, discovered via GitHub repositories. Two specialized modules extend functionality: an AV/EDR killer using a signed Beijing Jiangmin Antivirus driver to terminate security products, and a cryptor module encrypting files with AES-CBC or ChaCha20 while targeting database processes. The transition to Rust and evidence of LLM-assisted development suggests evolving toolchain ...

results.name: Attackers Exploit Optimizely Flaw To Inject Malicious JavaScript
results.description: On November 16, 2026, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation account signup flow, allowing unauthorized modification of the Project JavaScript field. This enabled injection of malicious JavaScript into customer projects, which was then delivered to website visitors through legitimate Optimizely snippets served from their CDN. The malicious payload was designed to replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Litecoin, Toncoin, Bitcoin Cash, and Dogecoin. It also performed payment card skimming, cookie theft, screen capture functionality, and delivered iOS exploit kits (Coruna and DarkSword) targeting iPhones and iPads. ThreatLabz identified over 450 unique domains and 3,000 URLs serving the malicious script, affecting multiple industries including airlines, automotive, banking, e-commerce, insurance, media, real estate, retail, telecommunications, and technology sectors. Optimizely blocked the vulnerable path, removed injected code, and rese...

results.name: One Phishing Kit, 29 Fake Banks
results.description: Since late September 2026, a phishing campaign has been deploying fake online banking websites using a single template kit. The operation created 29 unique fake-bank domains with professional-looking pages designed to harvest credentials and personally identifiable information. Each site features identical artifacts including the same tagline, bank routing number, and support phone number, with only bank names swapped. Domains use cheap TLDs and are registered on disposable infrastructure. Victims were primarily located in North America, followed by Europe and Asia, with finance and banking organizations representing nearly half of affected targets. One-third of domains had zero antivirus detection at discovery time. The campaign uses a purchased PHP banking-scam kit, originally branded as EMENDY INVEST. Operators build fake business ecosystems around these domains to appear in search results and enhance legitimacy.

results.name: Major African Stock Exchange Targeted in AI-Assisted Attack
results.description: Attackers deployed a sophisticated 41-module PowerShell toolkit against an African stock exchange, exhibiting strong indicators of AI-assisted development. The toolkit operated for just over three minutes in September 2026, systematically hunting credentials and testing them against the exchange's investment API and securities depository gateway. Each module utilized identical scaffolding and hex-encoded DNS exfiltration to unique subdomains of a public out-of-band testing service. Six persistence implants attributed to China-linked group Witchetty were discovered on the same server, with earliest activity dating to April 2026. The toolkit targeted cloud credentials, database connections, SharePoint, SCCM, and TFS servers, focusing on systems close to financial operations. While Witchetty is traditionally an espionage group, the financial targeting suggests possible cybercrime motivation, though espionage cannot be ruled out.

results.name: Inside Turla's Cereal: 12 Exchange loaders, older traces and new ways to hunt
results.description: In November 2026, researchers disclosed Cereal, a modular espionage toolset deployed by the Russia-aligned Turla group against Microsoft Exchange servers at government organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania. The operation targeted email communications involving NATO and European Union institutions through stealthy components that avoided traditional detection methods. CerealNeuron listened for specially crafted web requests on compromised servers, while CerealBox intercepted selected emails within Exchange's transport pipeline without registering new agents. Analysis identified 12 related loader files, with evidence dating back to 2022. The toolset employed DLL side-loading, impersonated legitimate Windows files, and operated within trusted infrastructure to avoid outbound beacons. Multiple naming conventions across security vendors complicated detection efforts, requiring defenders to correlate file metadata, structural hashes, and behavioral analysis rather than relying on single indicators.

results.name: US Bank, IRS, and Social Security Logins Stolen by a Russian-Speaking Operation
results.description: A Russian-speaking credential-theft operation compromised 603 Windows systems between October and November 2026, stealing US bank credentials and federal identity logins from victims' own machines. Operating from a Netherlands VPS, the attackers deployed three parallel command-and-control frameworks (HavoX, Phantom53, Kraken Bridge) and bypassed Chrome app-bound encryption, cracked LastPass, 1Password, and KeePass vaults offline, and replayed cookies to bypass Microsoft 365 MFA. At least 46 victims had ID.me or Login.gov accounts exposed, providing access to IRS, Social Security, and VA portals. The operation also targeted 35 AI developer products, 44 cryptocurrency platforms, and deployed RMM tools for persistent access. All traffic was fronted through 12 Cloudflare Workers domains. A complete exposed directory containing 1,692 operational files, including loot archives, post-exploitation scripts, and Russian-language operational logs, revealed the infrastructure and tooling used.

results.name: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits vSphere
results.description: In September 2026, the suspected PRC-nexus threat actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited CVE-2026-123890, a zero-day vulnerability in VMware vCenter Server, following their initial exploitation of CVE-2026-102764 in BeyondTrust Remote Support. The group demonstrated sophisticated post-exploitation capabilities by deploying five newly identified malware families: BONESAW (a Golang exploitation utility), SAWSNAKE (a SAML authentication bypass tool), SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH (webshells), and BEARBONES (a backdoored SSH server). ARMORY CASTLE leveraged these tools to conduct reconnaissance targeting VMware infrastructure, escalate privileges, establish persistence, steal credentials including vCenter master keys and PostgreSQL passwords, and ultimately extract sensitive data from ESXi guest VMs. The campaign showcases the threat actor's deep platform expertise across multiple appliance types and substantial resource backing, utilizing two zero-days and three specialized malware sets in a single operation.

results.name: Autonomous LLMjacking: 'Skynet' Agent Hijacks Exposed AI Models to Run Attacks
results.description: Attackers have developed an autonomous offensive agent that scans the internet for exposed large language model endpoints and hijacks them to execute attacks. The agent is equipped with 74 offensive tools covering reconnaissance, exploitation of web frameworks including VS Code, Django, Jupyter, Laravel, Supabase, Next.js, Flask/Werkzeug, database theft through Prisma, credential harvesting, and cryptocurrency mining. Once connected to an unprotected model, it operates unattended for up to 100,000 steps without human approval. The operators use jailbreak techniques to bypass safety controls, redefining credential theft as routine development work. Victims include model owners who pay for computing power and compromised servers stripped of data and used for Monero mining. The activity was captured through an AI honeypot that recorded the complete instruction set, revealing a self-directed cybercrime operation targeting internet-facing AI services without authentication.

results.name: The Gentlemen: A closer look at a not-so-gentle ransomware-as-a-service operation
results.description: The Gentlemen is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in mid-2025 after operating as an affiliate of LockBit and Qilin. The group offers affiliates up to 90% of ransom revenue and has claimed over 800 victims across multiple regions and sectors. The ransomware targets Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD systems using a double-extortion model that encrypts files and exfiltrates data. Written in Go, the ransomware employs ChaCha20 encryption with multiple speed modes, terminates security processes using vulnerable drivers, and spreads laterally through networks via PsExec. A May 2026 infrastructure breach exposed internal communications, affiliate information, and connections to the Qilin ecosystem. Organizations in the United States and Europe are most frequently targeted, particularly in manufacturing, technology, healthcare, professional services, and retail sectors.

results.name: From Phishing to LLMjacking: Threat Actors Targeting Cloud Billing Accounts for LLM Usage
results.description: Threat actors are conducting sophisticated campaigns targeting Google Cloud Platform environments through phishing attacks via sponsored search ads. Attackers compromise privileged user credentials using fake login pages, then manipulate organizational policies to disable security guardrails. They create service accounts with Gemini API access, invite external attacker-controlled accounts, and assign administrative billing roles. The attackers link their external GCP projects to victim billing accounts, enabling them to execute large-scale AI workloads while hiding activity from victim monitoring. This results in unauthorized charges reaching tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars within 24-48 hours. The campaigns employ evasion techniques including geographic IP blending and demoting legitimate administrators to prevent detection and remediation.

results.name: Ukraine's State Data-Exchange System Targeted by Russian-Speaking Operator via Graylog Log4Shell
results.description: Between May and September 2026, a Russian-speaking operator systematically targeted Ukraine's state data-exchange infrastructure by exploiting Log4Shell vulnerabilities in Graylog servers. The attacker swept 9.1 million Ukrainian IP addresses, filtering 7,576 live hosts to identify systems running UXP Verifier, a component of the national data-exchange platform. Using a two-stage CommonsBeanutils2 deserialization chain delivered through Graylog's sessions API, the operator gained access to at least two organizations, including a logging server containing 6.8 million documents from Ukraine's state data-exchange system. The operation was exposed when the attacker accidentally served their working directory over HTTP for 17 hours, revealing reconnaissance tools, shell history, exploit code, and access logs. While the operator queried transaction indices and demonstrated prior knowledge of the system's schema, no data exfiltration was directly observed. The campaign also included failed exploitation attempts a...

results.name: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257
results.description: Active exploitation of PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 has been observed, targeting GlobalProtect portal and gateway components. The authentication bypass flaw allows unauthorized attackers to circumvent security controls and establish VPN connections. Ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc), along with Settra ransomware actors, are exploiting this vulnerability to gain initial network access. Following successful exploitation, threat actors bypass multi-factor authentication, conduct internal reconnaissance using remote monitoring tools, move laterally via RDP and SMB, and stage additional tooling for credential harvesting and ransomware deployment. A sophisticated tactic observed involves pivoting directly to the virtualization layer, accessing vCenter management appliances, disabling security controls on ESXi hypervisors, and performing offline credential dumping against domain controller virtual disks. Multiple industries have been impacted including educa...

results.name: Active Exploitation of CVE-2026-110936 in Siemens Software Center
results.description: A DLL side-loading vulnerability in Software Center version 3.5.8.7 is being actively exploited by attackers. The threat actors distribute a genuine, digitally signed copy of the application alongside malicious DLL files through unofficial channels. When executed, the vulnerable version loads the attacker-supplied DLLs without validation, enabling malicious code execution. The attack vector involves ClickFix social engineering tactics, tricking users into executing commands. The campaign uses specific infrastructure for payload hosting and command-and-control operations. Version 4.0.9.8 patches this vulnerability, with automatic updates applied upon application restart. No official systems or distribution channels were compromised during this campaign.

results.name: Behind the Power Outage: Unmasking a New Intrusion Vector in Enterprise Infrastructure Tools
results.description: An attacker exploited CyberPower PowerPanel Business (PPB), a UPS management software, to execute malicious code on a Windows domain controller. The threat actor uploaded custom scripts through the web console's file-upload endpoint on TCP port 3052, leveraging PPB's legitimate feature that runs scripts during power events. These scripts executed with SYSTEM privileges through the trusted ppbed.exe service. The attacker downloaded tools using certutil, loaded .NET assemblies into memory, and extracted Active Directory data using ntdsutil and esentutl against ntds.dit. Through iterative script development, the adversary refined their collection process until successful. Finally, they deployed a persistent implant, upnpcont.exe with malicious atl.dll, using DLL side-loading. The operation demonstrated interactive human engagement, utilizing primarily built-in Windows utilities to maintain stealth while compromising critical infrastructure.

results.name: GravityRAT Mobile Cyber-Campaign Targets Defense Personnel
results.description: An active cyber-surveillance campaign has been uncovered deploying GravityRAT malware against defense industry and military personnel, primarily targeting individuals from India seeking positions at foreign defense contractors. The campaign utilizes fake recruitment portals and software utility websites that mimic legitimate services to distribute malicious payloads. These sites display logos of major defense contractors like Airbus, BAE Systems, Thales, and Lockheed Martin to build credibility. GravityRAT is a multi-platform surveillance framework active since 2015, attributed to Pakistan-aligned threat actors including SpaceCobra and Cosmic Leopard. The malware conducts extensive data exfiltration including contacts, call logs, SMS messages, GPS location, documents, WhatsApp backups, and device identifiers, uploading collected information to command and control servers at regular intervals.

results.name: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Distributes Malware Across Global Brands
results.description: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform on November 16, 2026, compromising 188 JavaScript snippets across 178 organizations including BBC, CNN, Zoom, GitLab, IKEA, and HSBC. The exploit targeted the optional Project JavaScript field in Optimizely's A/B testing service, allowing malicious code injection through trusted infrastructure. Visitors to affected websites were exposed to cryptocurrency wallet address clippers that replaced legitimate addresses with attacker-controlled ones, payment card skimmers, and iOS-specific exploit kits. The attack leveraged encoded JavaScript modules that intercepted clipboard operations, monitored page content through MutationObservers, and delivered platform-specific payloads. Optimizely patched the vulnerability, removed injected code, revoked tokens, and reset affected accounts by November 16 at 23:11 UTC.

results.name: Behind the Power Outage: Unmasking a New Intrusion Vector in Enterprise Infrastructure Tools
results.description: Threat actors exploited CyberPower PowerPanel Business (PPB), a UPS management software, as an execution channel on a Windows domain controller. The attackers leveraged PPB's legitimate feature that runs scripts during power events by uploading malicious .cmd files through the web console on TCP port 3052. Commands executed through the PowerPanel service (ppbed.exe) ran with SYSTEM privileges. The intrusion involved iterative script development to dump Active Directory credentials using ntdsutil and esentutl, downloading tools via certutil, and deploying a persistent implant through DLL side-loading. This technique allowed attackers to hide within trusted infrastructure management software, making detection challenging as activities appeared to originate from legitimate power-management processes.

results.name: Open by Default, Already Occupied: Threat Actors are Renting your Compute
results.description: Analysis of 11,891 IP addresses reveals that over half of exposed Ollama servers show evidence of unauthorized access. Approximately 65% of affected hosts reside in cloud or hosting networks, with Germany, China, and the United States most impacted. The investigation identified 106,938 model entries across exposed servers, with 24% showing models pulled from raw IP addresses and 22% using free tunneling services. Evidence suggests attackers are exploiting unauthenticated Ollama instances to access paid cloud model subscriptions, conduct server-side request forgery, and attempt path traversal attacks similar to the Probllama vulnerability. Model lists contain Base64-encoded strings targeting sensitive files like /etc/shadow and SSH keys, with some malicious artifacts persisting for five months. The exposed infrastructure primarily consists of rental compute resources that lack proper authentication, egress controls, and organizational ownership.

results.name: Fake FMCSA, DAT, and TIMOCOM Portals: 3 Cyberattacks Targeting US Logistics
results.description: Three distinct campaigns are actively targeting American trucking and logistics companies through digital platforms used for routine business operations. HelloFriends employs fraudulent carrier verification portals impersonating SAFER and Motus to harvest credentials, personal identification data, and fuel card information via sophisticated phishing infrastructure. NodeRemote distributes malware through fake broker documents and onboarding pages, deploying Node.js backdoors with rotating command-and-control infrastructure that maintains persistent remote access to compromised endpoints. The Fake Freight Portals campaign impersonates TIMOCOM and DAT, using malicious WebDAV shortcuts to install MeshCentral and CastleRAT remote access tools, while attempting to extract BitLocker recovery keys and weakening endpoint defenses. These campaigns exploit familiar business workflows including carrier verification, broker onboarding, and freight booking to compromise operational systems and sensitive business data.

results.name: agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2: PyPI credential stealer
results.description: Microsoft's Agent Framework meta-package on PyPI was compromised with versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, published on November 17, 2026. Both versions deployed a .pth startup hook that executed credential-stealing code every time Python launched, requiring no package import. The stealer harvested Azure, Azure DevOps, and GitHub Actions tokens from environment variables across 300 running processes, credential files, and cloud metadata services. It collected tokens from Azure CLI caches, pip, npm, Docker, git, and Hugging Face credentials, then minted fresh cloud tokens via Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions OIDC endpoints and Azure Instance Metadata Service. All stolen data was compressed, Base64-encoded, and exfiltrated to a webhook.site endpoint. The compromise was detected within six minutes and removed within hours, but any host running these versions should be considered fully compromised.

results.name: ROMULUS Campaign: CNCMachineRMS RAT Analysis
results.description: Starting in late September 2026, widespread ClickFix activity was observed involving multiple malware delivery chains impersonating legitimate software. The ROMULUS platform distributed both CNCMachineRMS and LegionLoader through separate infection chains, utilizing ChatGPT Custom GPTs and DLL sideloading techniques. The investigation recovered a final RAT from a malicious Stardock installer employing encrypted payloads and a proprietary storage format. Analysis revealed strong similarities to CNCMachineRMS, previously documented in a separate BabaDeda infection chain, including family-specific identifiers and a custom scripting engine. The RAT supports persistent remote access, surveillance, system reconnaissance, and additional payload execution. ROMULUS operates as a delivery service platform, likely continuing to evolve as ClickFix techniques prove effective for initial access across cybercriminal ecosystems.

results.name: IronWorm eBPF Rootkit: How GhostMap Hides on Linux
results.description: GhostMap is a Linux eBPF rootkit shared across IronWorm and Atomic Arch malware payloads that manipulates kernel data to conceal malicious processes, files, and network sockets from user-space applications. The rootkit uses eBPF programs attached to kernel events to modify directory entries by overwriting a single byte in application memory, forcing readers to skip hidden files. While process concealment proved effective against standard enumeration tools, socket hiding failed completely against ss, leaving listeners visible despite removal from /proc/net/tcp. The malware establishes persistence through systemd services and stores collected data in extended file attributes. Runtime security monitoring successfully detected the rootkit's eBPF attachments and memory-writing capabilities, demonstrating that while GhostMap can manipulate system views, underlying runtime behavior remains observable through alternative detection methods.

results.name: Fake Conad Plus App: A Promise of 10× Loyalty Points Conceals Android Malware
results.description: A fraudulent campaign targeting users in Italy impersonates Conad, a retail brand, by offering multiplied miPREMIO loyalty points through a fake application called Conad Plus. The malicious website conad-plus[.]shop distributes an Android malware family identified as Koktevrat. The installation chain involves two APK files with RC4-encrypted assets containing operational code. Once installed and granted Accessibility permissions, the remote access trojan can capture screenshots, intercept keystrokes, collect form data, enumerate installed applications, display overlay screens, and execute interface interactions. Commands are received via WebSocket connection to a static command-and-control server, supplemented by Firebase Cloud Messaging for signaling. The malware employs a domain generation algorithm for fallback infrastructure and uses multiple obfuscation techniques including dynamic code loading, reflection, and encrypted assets to hinder analysis.

results.name: Customer Advisory: Guidance Following the Optimizely Supply Chain Incident
results.description: On November 16, an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely Web Experimentation, injecting malicious JavaScript into customer projects. The malicious code, active from 04:21 to 23:11 UTC, could swap cryptocurrency addresses, skim payment card details, steal screenshots and cookies, and deliver exploit kits to vulnerable iOS devices. Analysis identified 188 infected snippets belonging to 178 organizations. The altered scripts were served from Optimizely's content network and customer domains, making detection difficult. Optimizely fixed the vulnerability and removed injected code, though one snippet was re-infected during cleanup. Organizations may be affected through vendor websites visited during the incident window, particularly authentication and payment pages loading Optimizely scripts.

results.name: Microsoft's agent-framework Hijacked on PyPI via Silent .pth Startup Hook
results.description: A supply chain attack targeted Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, affecting versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 released on November 17, 2026. The attacker repacked legitimate wheels locally and injected a .pth startup hook that executes a credential stealer every time Python starts, regardless of whether the package is imported. The malicious code harvests environment variables containing Azure, AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, and other cloud credentials, reads configuration files from multiple locations, queries Azure metadata services for OAuth tokens, and exfiltrates compressed data to a webhook.site endpoint. Both versions were quarantined within 40 minutes but automated dependency bots had already begun propagating updates. The stealer targets 31 credential patterns, reads up to 80 files, and on Linux scans running processes for secrets.

results.name: OPTIMJACK: When Trusted JavaScript Becomes a Supply Chain Attack
results.description: On November 16, 2026, attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into 188 snippets affecting 178 organizations including Zoom, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA and HSBC. The payload replaced cryptocurrency wallet addresses, captured payment card details from first-party forms, collected non-HttpOnly cookies and screenshots, and attempted to deliver exploit kits to iOS devices. Researcher Scott Helme identified the compromise, which lasted approximately 16 hours before cleanup was completed. The attack demonstrated how trusted third-party JavaScript providers can become supply chain attack vectors, bypassing traditional security controls. Organizations with restrictive Content Security Policies blocked some malicious activity, while others remained fully exposed. The incident highlights the need for continuous monitoring of third-party code rather than relying solely on initial vendor assessments.

results.name: PHP2Shell Exploited by AI Agents from Day One: Inside a Credential-Harvesting Campaign
results.description: A credential-harvesting campaign exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities within days of public disclosure on October 21, 2026. The operation utilized attacker infrastructure at 206.245.153[.]56 serving as command-and-control, payload hosting, and data collection. An AI-agent system orchestrated exploitation using a custom job dispatcher with DeepSeek V4.1 endpoints, processing targets from a Shodan dataset of 68,198 hosts. The campaign compromised 404 systems across 57 countries, establishing persistence through SSH keys, webshells, cron beacons, and Dropbear tunnels. Operators exfiltrated cloud credentials, database backups, application secrets, OAuth tokens, and source code. Evidence suggests an initial-access-broker model, with attempts at financial fraud against payment platforms that failed to complete actual theft. The pattern indicates a financially motivated actor using AI-augmented operations to compress exploitation timelines from weeks to days.

results.name: Brain Cipher Ransomware Group: Victims, Leak Site, TTPs & IOCs
results.description: Brain Cipher is a financially motivated cybercriminal group operating since the early 2020s, specializing in sophisticated ransomware attacks against large organizations. The group employs double extortion tactics, threatening to release stolen data if ransom demands are not met, with payments typically ranging from $150,000 to $8 million in Monero cryptocurrency. They utilize a modified variant of LockBit 3.0 ransomware and conduct extensive network infiltration and data exfiltration before deployment. Their attack methodology incorporates zero-day vulnerabilities and social engineering techniques to maximize effectiveness. The group has targeted critical sectors including healthcare and finance, demonstrating willingness to disrupt essential services for financial gain, with 76 documented victims across 51 countries.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Helix Ransomware Group: Victims, Leak Site, TTPs & IOCs
results.description: Helix is a financially motivated cybercrime group that emerged in July 2026, specializing in data extortion through sophisticated identity theft techniques. The group combines voice phishing with Microsoft OAuth Device Code Flow abuse to bypass multi-factor authentication and compromise enterprise environments. They target high-value Microsoft 365 cloud infrastructures, specifically SharePoint data repositories, primarily in North America. Using two compromised accounts, Helix conducts stealthy data theft through automated scripts and shared cloud infrastructure, exfiltrating sensitive information without deploying custom malware. Extortion demands are delivered through corporate collaboration tools such as Microsoft Teams and email. Their operations demonstrate advanced social engineering capabilities combined with cloud service abuse for large-scale data theft and extortion.

results.name: Eclipse Ransomware Group: Victims, Leak Site, TTPs & IOCs
results.description: Nightmare Eclipse, also known as Chaotic Eclipse and Dead Eclipse, is a rogue threat actor that emerged in April 2026, operating from Russian-geolocated infrastructure. This individual conducts high-impact zero-day disclosure campaigns against Microsoft products driven by personal vengeance rather than financial motivation. The actor utilizes zero-day exploits targeting Windows security subsystems, including CVE-2026-50656 for privilege escalation, and weaponizes Microsoft Defender Antivirus to gain administrative control over enterprise networks. Primary targets include public administration, healthcare, and finance sectors, with a focus on Windows enterprise endpoints. Initial access is achieved through exploitation of VPN gateways, followed by defense impairment and data encryption activities.
