results.name: Cyberleek Ransomware Group: Victims, Leak Site, TTPs & IOCs
results.description: CyberLeek is a newly emerged extortionist and data leakage group that employs a novel monetization strategy based on public engagement rather than traditional ransom demands. The group gained attention for leaking proprietary content from Rockstar Games and primarily targets major software publishers in the gaming industry. They utilize a Solana-based cryptocurrency token called $CYBERLEEK to drive audience engagement and funding. Their operations combine elements of hacktivism with financial motivations centered on cryptocurrency profits. The group stages data exfiltration from internal development environments using compromised credentials, publicly releases gameplay footage, and conducts decentralized voting to determine which content to leak next. They communicate through unconventional channels like Telegram to facilitate interactions with their audience.

results.name: NetScaler intrusions chaining CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88779
results.description: In early October 2026, analysts investigated a compromise of a Citrix NetScaler ADC appliance running an affected 14.1 build. Attackers chained two vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-88771 (pre-authentication log-poisoning/RCE) and CVE-2026-88779 (SAML-parsing crash) to achieve root code execution. The intrusion deployed multiple persistence mechanisms including PHP web shells with cookie-based command channels, setuid shell modifications, cron entries, and boot hooks. Attackers installed TCP session managers, HTTP tunnels, and outbound reverse agents for command-and-control. A dedicated Go reconnaissance tool mapped internal infrastructure including DNS, LDAP/Active Directory, management services, and VMware vCenter systems. HA-aware persistence logic synchronized implants across appliance pairs and forced failovers. The campaign exfiltrated NetScaler configurations, historical data, and key material, demonstrating evolution from initial foothold to persistent platform for internal reconnaissance.

results.name: MCH and Caishen: supply chain poisoning pushes iOS exploits
results.description: On November 16, 2026, compromised third-party scripts delivered card skimmers and cryptocurrency clippers to visitors of major websites including BBC, Zoom, and CNN. An unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Experimentation product to inject malicious JavaScript, though other libraries like Kissmetrics, StorifyMe, and minute-ly were also affected. The campaign utilized an iOS exploitation toolkit branded Caishen, delivering exploits to mobile users while desktop visitors received card skimmers, cryptocurrency clippers, and page-data theft mechanisms. Infrastructure analysis revealed connections to MCH control panels and cryptocurrency energy rental storefronts, with over 140 instances of related panels observed. The operation's infrastructure went offline within hours of public disclosure on November 17, 2026, but new control panel hosts quickly emerged on alternative networks. Stolen cryptocurrency was rapidly moved through commercial services.

results.name: URGENT: iOS Exploits Are Being Actively Deployed via Poisoned JavaScript on BBC, Zoom, CNN and Other Major Websites
results.description: Research reveals that threat actors have compromised third-party JavaScript providers including Optimizely, Kissmetrics, StorifyMe, and Minute-ly to deliver iOS exploits through at least 21 major websites. The attack routes Mobile Safari users to Coruna and DarkSword exploit-kit infrastructure without any user interaction. Affected sites span multiple sectors including BBC, CNN, Fox News, Zoom, GitLab, and Salesforce. Instead of targeting website backends directly, attackers poisoned widely-used analytics and content provider scripts, which then loaded malicious payloads that executed zero-click exploit chains. The compromised scripts operated via hidden iframes, leaving no visible indicators while exploiting vulnerabilities in Mobile Safari. This supply-chain attack bypasses traditional security measures as the malicious code originates from legitimate, trusted infrastructure that enterprise filters cannot block without disrupting business operations.

results.name: US Logistics Cyber Threats: 3 Campaigns & Defense
results.description: Three distinct campaigns are actively targeting the US trucking and logistics sector through fraudulent business portals and malicious documents. HelloFriends uses fake FMCSA carrier verification portals to harvest credentials, SSNs, EINs, and fuel card information through phishing emails. NodeRemote distributes backdoors disguised as broker onboarding documents, establishing persistent access through scheduled tasks and rotating C2 infrastructure. Fake Freight Portals impersonate TIMOCOM and DAT platforms, delivering MeshCentral and CastleRAT through malicious WebDAV shortcuts while attempting to extract BitLocker recovery keys. These attacks exploit routine logistics workflows including carrier verification, broker onboarding, and freight booking. The campaigns demonstrate sophisticated social engineering, infrastructure rotation, and multi-stage infection chains that combine credential theft with persistent remote access capabilities.

results.name: agent-framework Compromised: Credential Stealer Targets Azure and CI Pipelines
results.description: On November 17, 2026, two malicious versions (1.26.1 and 1.26.2) of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package were published to PyPI for approximately 50 minutes before removal. The compromised packages deployed credential stealers through Python .pth files that executed automatically on interpreter startup. The malware targeted Azure and CI/CD environments, extracting environment variables containing secrets, credential files from Azure CLI, Docker, Git, and package managers, plus Azure managed-identity and OIDC tokens. Version 1.26.2 enhanced capabilities to steal GitHub Actions OIDC tokens from workflows with federated credential access. Stolen data was exfiltrated via a hardcoded webhook.site URL. The root cause appears to be unauthorized direct upload to PyPI outside the normal release process, though this has not been confirmed.

results.name: Active DGA Phishing and Polymorphic WebView Trojans Targeting Romanian Users - NACE Exchange / TroveX
results.description: A sophisticated financial fraud campaign is actively targeting Romanian users through fake cryptocurrency exchange platforms branded as NACE Exchange and TroveX. The operation employs domain generation algorithms to rapidly rotate phishing domains that mimic legitimate crypto exchanges, harvesting credentials and personal data. Malicious Android APK files and iOS provisioning profiles are distributed as fake trading applications, functioning as WebView wrappers with embedded tracking infrastructure. These trojans request extensive permissions including GPS location tracking, clipboard access, contacts, and storage to exfiltrate sensitive data. The campaign has been documented across multiple European countries and utilizes personas like Professor Herbert Phillip. Infrastructure endpoints are frequently rotated to evade detection, making this a persistent transnational threat.

results.name: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Silently Run Malware on MSP Technicians' Computers
results.description: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical vulnerability in ScreenConnect with a CVSS score of 9.9, to execute malicious files on managed service provider technician workstations without user confirmation. The flaw allows malicious guests to send files during remote support sessions and trigger execution with elevated privileges. In a documented November 12 incident, attackers installed a rogue remote access client in approximately nine seconds. Researchers identified over 688,000 delivery attempts across 42 MSP servers between October and November, originating from 29 IP addresses. The attack chain involves batch scripts, PowerShell commands, and installation of disguised ScreenConnect clients connecting to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Affected organizations must update technician clients to version 26.6.5 or later and investigate suspicious file transfers and executions.

results.name: Microsoft’s agent-framework PyPI package Compromised with Credential Stealer
results.description: Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI was compromised on November 17th, with versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 containing malicious code. Both versions install Python startup hooks through .pth files that silently execute on interpreter initialization. The malicious code collects Azure, GitHub Actions, and various CI/CD credentials, including environment variables, configuration files, and cloud identity tokens. It actively requests fresh Azure managed-identity and GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. The stolen data is compressed, base64-encoded, and exfiltrated to a webhook.site endpoint. The attack targets credential-related environment variables, processes, Azure and Azure DevOps credentials, GitHub Actions tokens, and configuration files from various tools including pip, npm, Docker, and Git.

results.name: Amazon job offer promises $5,000 a month, but it has got all the signs of a scam
results.description: Multiple fraudulent websites are advertising fake remote assistant positions using Amazon-like branding and domain names, promising up to $5,000 monthly. These sites, registered between July and October through the same registrar, collect personal information including names, addresses, and employment history through forms. Despite advertising remote work, applications ask about vehicle access and package delivery capabilities, indicating potential reshipping or parcel-mule fraud schemes. The operations target job seekers looking for flexible work during Amazon's legitimate holiday hiring season. Sites use identical icons and connected infrastructure, with domains like amzssapplication[.]com and applyamazonsp[.]com. Victims risk identity theft, involvement in fraud operations using stolen payment details, and financial losses through fake check schemes.

results.name: AI Agents Targeted Through Malicious GitHub Repositories
results.description: A sophisticated malware campaign has been discovered that targets developers using AI coding assistants through compromised GitHub repositories. The attack exploits configuration files and instruction documents that AI agents use to understand projects, such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Twenty-two malicious repositories have been identified containing a concealed payload (setup.js) that steals credentials from platforms including GitHub, GitLab, AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. The malware validates stolen tokens, modifies repositories, infects software packages, and propagates by injecting malicious instructions into AI-agent configuration files. It can also spread through victim accounts by committing malicious files to repositories with sufficient permissions, affecting npm, PyPI, RubyGems, and JFrog package ecosystems.

results.name: Optimizely Attack Hits Zoom, BBC, CNN With Skimmer, iOS Kits
results.description: On November 16, 2026, attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Experimentation product to inject malicious JavaScript into 188 customer projects, affecting major organizations including Zoom, BBC, CNN, IKEA, HSBC and Equifax. For nearly 19 hours, visitors to these sites received code that swapped cryptocurrency addresses, skimmed payment card data, and delivered iOS exploit kits to iPhone and iPad users. The payload included cryptocurrency clippers for multiple blockchains, a card skimmer targeting first-party checkout forms, context theft capturing cookies and screenshots, and iOS exploit chains (Coruna and DarkSword kits) targeting devices running iOS 13 through 18.6. Attackers collected approximately $7,150 in cryptocurrency, though the full extent of stolen card data and compromised iOS devices remains unknown. All infected files were cleaned by 23:11 UTC on November 16.

results.name: Threat Researcher’s Notebook: BubbleLoader
results.description: BubbleLoader is an evolving loader actively used in recent attack campaigns to deliver secondary malicious payloads. It hijacks common benign software such as WinRAR, x64dbg, Windows Media Player, Firefox Launcher, and virtiofs by patching entry points and adding two PNG files that serve as delivery mechanisms. The loader operates in four stages: the entry point patch allocates memory and copies PNGs, a fake PNG houses shellcode and XOR-encrypted third stage, shellcode decrypts the third stage using the first PNG as a rolling XOR key, and the third stage performs reflective loading with anti-analysis features. BubbleLoader leverages runtime polymorphism to change in-memory payload hashes for every execution, complicating forensic analysis. Two activity clusters observed in mid-September and early October indicate active deployment by adversaries.

results.name: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer
results.description: Multiple Plex Media Server vulnerabilities announced in September 2026 are being actively exploited to deploy cryptominers and proxy software. The exploitation chains together four CVEs to achieve remote code execution on vulnerable Plex servers. A honeypot deployment captured exploitation attempts from multiple IP addresses starting October 17, 2026. Attackers deployed XMRig cryptominer and myawesomeproxy software on compromised systems. The proxy tool potentially enables threat actors to utilize residential IPs for accessing corporate VPNs and email systems. Exploitation was observed from IP addresses 45.194.92.222, 91.92.40.202, and 176.65.139.228, with malicious payloads downloaded from 217.60.194.116. The vulnerabilities affect Plex Media Server version 1.43.2 and earlier, with proof-of-concept code publicly available through the plex2shell project.

results.name: ConnectWise (SkyKick) Vendor Credentials Abused in M365 Attacks
results.description: A Microsoft 365 API credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) was compromised and used to gain unauthorized access to customer M365 environments. The threat actor authenticated from IP address 144.172.64.128 on October 15, obtaining Microsoft Graph access tokens across hundreds of tenants. The attacker moved through tenants in sorted GUID order, suggesting automated targeting. In one instance, the ConnectWise Cloud Management MS Teams application elevated itself to Global Administrator and added credentials to other applications, including security tools. The activity began with password spraying against law firms on October 13-14, followed by role assignments in approximately 50 tenants, and culminated in widespread credential abuse. Nearly 1,000 Entra tenants showed sign-in activity from the malicious IP, with over 300 successful authentications. A second targeted wave focused on 16 tenants in policy, national security, trade, and critical mineral sectors.

results.name: Operation ShadowCloud: initial infection and the GitDoor backdoor
results.description: A sophisticated cyber intrusion campaign dubbed Operation ShadowCloud has been identified targeting government entities across Asia and Africa. Adversaries deploy two novel backdoors, GitDoor and GraphDoor, through the legitimate MeshAgent utility. These implants conceal command-and-control communications by leveraging cloud platforms including Microsoft SharePoint, GitHub, and Ably messaging services, effectively evading network detection mechanisms. The modular toolset supports on-demand plug-in downloads and in-memory shellcode injection, enabling capabilities such as keylogging, screen capture, credential theft, and proxy deployment. The operation employs DLL sideloading techniques with legitimate executables to deliver malicious loaders that decrypt and execute encrypted payloads. Multiple GitHub repositories, created since late 2024, serve as infrastructure for data exfiltration and command distribution. The campaign demonstrates advanced obfuscation including control flow flattening and multi-stage ...

results.name: World's Largest Brands Infected With Malware Via Optimizely
results.description: On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was distributed to 178 organizations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform, affecting major sites including Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, and HSBC. The multi-purpose malware swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and deployed Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits targeting iPhones and iPads. Attackers injected their code into customer Project JavaScript fields within Optimizely snippets, which were then served from trusted cdn.optimizely.com domains. Verified cryptocurrency theft totaling approximately $7,040 occurred within nine hours, with funds moved to exchanges. The payload was rebuilt 26 times throughout the day, adding features including card skimming capabilities. Most malicious code was removed by 21:52 UTC, though Content Security Policy protections could have prevented the attack on properly configured sites.

results.name: XaocMail ClickFix Campaign Drops Phantom53 and HavoX Across Latin America, Asia, and Europe
results.description: A Russian-speaking threat actor operates a sophisticated multi-stage campaign utilizing XaocMail phishing platform, Phantom53 DNS-over-HTTPS command-and-control framework, and Havoc post-exploitation toolkit. The operation leverages Cloudflare Workers infrastructure and ClickFix social engineering lures to deliver malicious MSI payloads. Phantom53 implements stealthy beaconing through public DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers, employs a week-keyed SHA256 domain generation algorithm for resilience, and uses scheduled tasks with Python virtual environments for persistence. The campaign shows evidence of AI-assisted development using Claude Code for automated testing and rapid iteration. Targets span Latin America, particularly Brazil and Peru, followed by entities in Asia and Europe across technology, finance, education, government, logistics, and manufacturing sectors. The attackers demonstrate advanced operational security through legitimate infrastructure abuse, reflective code loading, and sophisticated anti-sandb...

results.name: Lotuslite V2: The Evolution of Mustang Panda's .NET Backdoor
results.description: This analysis identifies Lotuslite V2 as a .NET successor to LOTUSLITE malware, attributed to Mustang Panda (Earth Preta). The campaign targets Thailand through a public Zoho WorkDrive link delivering an assessment-themed ZIP archive. The infection chain leverages a signed PDFgear executable for DLL side-loading, establishes registry persistence, and initiates TCP connections to command-and-control infrastructure. The evolved variant introduces the PRO1 protocol marker (0x50524F31) and implements application-layer AES-256-GCM encryption. Key modifications include a transition from C++ to managed .NET/C# architecture, enhanced cryptographic protection beyond transport-layer security, and refined command routing through bitwise MSB masking. The operational tradecraft maintains consistency with previous Mustang Panda campaigns, including signed binary abuse, ProgramData staging directories, and registry-based persistence mechanisms targeting government and diplomatic entities in the ASEAN region.

results.name: Detected Exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center, N-able N-central also Exploited
results.description: On November 6, 2026, the Apache Software Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-90436, a critical unsafe reflection vulnerability in Apache Axis 1.x that enables unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability affects certain versions of Atlassian Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central when configured with non-default settings. Active exploitation in the wild was detected on November 13, 2026, targeting both products. Affected Confluence versions range from 1.x through 9.x when Remote API is enabled, while N-central requires Legacy API to be active for exploitation. Apache Axis 1.x has reached end of life with no official patches planned. Organizations must apply emergency patches or disable vulnerable APIs immediately, prioritizing internet-accessible instances and investigating exposed systems for compromise indicators.

results.name: Fake Prime Gaming x FC 27 reward site harvests EA passwords and 2FA codes
results.description: Football fans seeking free player packs for EA SPORTS FC 27 are targeted by a sophisticated phishing campaign mimicking Prime Gaming reward pages. The fake site, styled as an official promotion, directs victims to a fraudulent EA sign-in page that captures email addresses, passwords, and two-factor authentication codes. The stolen credentials are sent to attacker-controlled servers that validate entries before proceeding, potentially allowing immediate account takeover. The phishing kit includes tracking capabilities for social media traffic sources and masquerades as an internal authentication tool. Compromised EA accounts may contain valuable virtual assets, purchased games, and payment information. The operation demonstrates advanced credential harvesting techniques specifically targeting the gaming community following FC 27's September launch.

results.name: Typosquatters Copy Big Brands' New Domains Within a Day of Registration
results.description: An ongoing typosquatting campaign has been targeting clients of brand-protection registrars CSC and MarkMonitor by monitoring their new domain registrations. Malicious actors registered 25 lookalike domains using one-character modifications within 24 hours of authentic domains being registered. The campaign targeted major brands including Abbott Laboratories, Bayer, CarMax, McDonald's, Procter & Gamble, and Sanofi. Most authentic domains were designed for marketing campaigns like patient-savings programs, sweepstakes, and legal settlements. The lookalike domains served parked pages, deceptive search portals, and brand-themed blogs containing advertisements routing visitors to scam sites. Registration occurred through China-based registrars Cloud Yuqu LLC and Chengdu West Dimension Digital Technology. Activity continues with new lookalikes detected as recently as November 11, 2026.

results.name: CVE-2026-84869 in ScreenConnect Exploited to Run Malicious Files on MSP Technician Accounts
results.description: A critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE-2026-84869, CVSS 9.9) allows malicious guests in remote sessions to push files to technician workstations and execute them with elevated privileges without authorization. Between October and November 2026, attackers conducted a massive spray campaign across 42 MSP ScreenConnect servers, issuing 688,000 malicious file-transfer requests. One successful exploitation achieved full compromise in nine seconds, deploying a rogue ScreenConnect client branded as Windows Update and connected to attacker infrastructure at masterdarky[.]com. Attack techniques included worm-like propagation, path traversal to inject startup scripts, and strategic targeting of MSP technician workstations that hold RMM consoles and customer credentials. Additional campaigns planted unauthorized crypto-exchange-named guest sessions as lures, while test runs used canary files to verify exploitation success before deploying actual payloads.

results.name: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
results.description: On November 13, 2026, a coordinated high-volume phishing campaign targeted organizations worldwide across multiple sectors. Threat actors disguised emails as legitimate Microsoft 365 service-health notifications, claiming emails were held during a service disruption and would be deleted within 24 hours unless recipients took action. The campaign used specific sender domains including moments-notice[.]com, planetmaison[.]com, and newbooker[.]com, with randomized outage subjects and recipient-specific tracking links leading to reallifeaccounting[.]com. The activity was assessed as credential phishing, though no credential capture, malware delivery, or post-compromise activity was directly observed. Microsoft Defender blocks malicious domains used in this campaign, and Defender for Office 365 quarantines phishing emails.

results.name: QUIC and Covert: Novel HTTP/3-Powered RATs Target Southeast Asian Governments
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage cyberespionage campaign has been targeting Southeast Asian government entities since July 2025. The activity features two previously undocumented custom remote access Trojans: PerfectPioneer RAT and its successor KUKURAT. These tools demonstrate advanced capabilities including covert HTTP/3 over UDP for command and control communications that bypass traditional TCP-based detection, an operational safety mechanism preventing operators from executing forensics-heavy commands, and multi-vector heuristic camouflage generating synthetic benign activity to obscure malicious operations. The attackers leverage server exploitation and phishing for initial access, manipulate domain log-on scripts for lateral movement, harvest credentials through LSASS dumping and DCSync attacks, and exfiltrate sensitive documents and emails. The campaign exhibits high operational stealth with consistent refinement of capabilities over nine months, characteristic of advanced persistent threat operations fo...

results.name: Fake crypto-wallet downloads used to deploy ScreenConnect remote access software
results.description: A sophisticated attack campaign is targeting cryptocurrency users, particularly those utilizing hardware wallets. The attackers employ deceptive ZIP files containing malicious BAT scripts, masquerading as legitimate wallet updates for Coldcard, Ledger, Pera Algorand Wallet, Revolut, and Xaman. The primary objective is deploying ConnectWise ScreenConnect, a legitimate remote-support application, which grants attackers complete remote access to compromised devices. Once installed, the ScreenConnect client connects to attacker-controlled infrastructure at fjksdjfdtitive[.]net on TCP port 8041, enabling command execution, data exfiltration, and potential theft of cryptocurrency credentials, wallet recovery phrases, and private keys. Affected users must immediately isolate their devices, block malicious domains and IPs, remove ScreenConnect installations, reset all credentials from clean devices, and consider moving cryptocurrency assets to new wallets generated on uncompromised systems.

results.name: Beyond Optimizely: Malicious Scripts Traced Across Four Web Services
results.description: An investigation documents malicious JavaScript delivered through four web services: Optimizely, Kissmetrics, StorifyMe, and minute-ly. Optimizely confirmed attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation signup workflow to inject malicious code into customer projects, affecting 188 snippets across 178 organizations including BBC, Zoom, GitLab, HSBC UAE, CNN, Fox News, Salesforce, Equifax, and Ledger. Archived evidence shows poisoned responses began November 13, 2026, before the main November 16 wave. The malicious code substituted cryptocurrency addresses, monitored card details in accessible forms, and established a mobile delivery path linked to Coruna and DarkSword operations. Later-stage iOS modules targeted keychain databases and private keys, though successful exploitation remains unproven. The shared infrastructure used routing channel 02111110 and collection domains at 1688360[.]cc and webshell[.]lol. Optimizely patched the vulnerability and removed injected code, but access paths for t...

results.name: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
results.description: Beginning November 11, 2026, threat actors gained unauthorized access to cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances belonging to managed service providers. The attackers abuse ScreenConnect, a legitimate remote-support application, to install unauthorized remote-access clients and deploy SCKit, a malicious worm, on customer-managed endpoints. The toolkit establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry entries, deploying RelayTrap to deliver malicious payloads to connecting technicians. SCKit targets IT support technician workstations using hijacked authenticated ScreenConnect sessions and uses victim management consoles to distribute payloads to other managed devices. The attack chain includes PowerShell decoders, encrypted bundles using device-specific key material, and browser-access components targeting authenticated ScreenConnect sessions. The worm's deployment enables threat actors to remotely administer affected endpoints, execute commands, and deploy additional tools independently...

results.name: WardenStealer Malware: Turning AI Access into an Underground Commodity
results.description: WardenStealer is a Rust-based Windows infostealer first observed in November 2026 that specializes in stealing credentials, authentication tokens, cookies, API keys, and local AI application files targeting platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor. Distributed through ClickFix lures, malicious advertisements, cracked software, and fake game cheats, it enables session hijacking that persists even after password resets. The malware operates as malware-as-a-service and captures OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, and configuration data from AI desktop applications. Stolen credentials are monetized in underground markets through discounted subscriptions and API credit reselling, supporting LLMjacking activities. Successful infections expose developer repositories, cloud services, build pipelines, and internal systems, while generating unexpected charges against victim accounts through unauthorized API usage.

results.name: Analysis of NodeLinkRAT, a New North Korea-Linked RAT Abusing Public Note Services as C2
results.description: Between September 12 and 18, 2026, a threat actor impersonating a South Korean National Assembly aide conducted spearphishing attacks against seminar attendees using honorarium payment forms as lures. The attacker deliberately omitted attachments in initial emails to elicit victim replies, then delivered malicious LNK files through webmail. The multistage fileless attack chain involved obfuscated PowerShell scripts, free web hosting, and abuse of aNotepad as a command channel. The actor dynamically changed payloads by updating public note page contents, deploying XenoRAT, information collection scripts, document exfiltration tools, and ultimately NodeLinkRAT—a JavaScript-based remote access tool running on legitimate Node.js runtime. Exfiltration channels rotated among Dropbox, MEGA cloud, and free hosting services. The campaign employed living-off-the-land techniques, polymorphic scripts, and legitimate infrastructure abuse to evade detection while conducting cyberespionage operations targeting South Kore...

results.name: The Retadup USB worm is back to spread CoffeeLoader
results.description: In August 2026, a new CoffeeLoader malware variant was identified, utilizing an NSIS-based installer that drops a patched 7z.dll file containing malicious shellcode. This version employs the Armoury packer, which has been updated to use OpenGL instead of OpenCL for GPU-based decryption. The malware establishes persistence through registry modifications and downloads its main payload from hardcoded C2 servers over HTTPS. The infection vector traces back to the Retadup worm, originally discovered in 2017 and neutralized by French authorities in 2019 after disinfecting 850,000 systems. Since 2024, threat actors have re-registered Retadup's former C2 domains to distribute malware, initially SmokeLoader and later CoffeeLoader, primarily affecting systems in Peru, Angola, Russia, and Bolivia.

results.name: Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework
results.description: ARTEX is an open-source, large language model-driven autonomous penetration testing framework that threat actors have weaponized to automate cyber intrusions from reconnaissance through data exfiltration. Since August 2026, various malicious actors have used ARTEX to conduct global campaigns across multiple sectors, significantly reducing intrusion timeframes with some attacks progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours. Notable incidents include attacks against South Korean financial institutions affecting approximately 67,000 individuals and a supply chain compromise of ConnectWise Cloud Backup impacting over 2,250 downstream customers. Despite the original developer removing the GitHub repository in October 2026, ARTEX continues to proliferate through community forks, archived copies, and a commercial version. The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously at machine speed, fundamentally acc...

results.name: Attackers use Crypto Exchange Names to Disguise Unauthorized Sessions on 100+ ScreenConnect Servers
results.description: Between November 3 and November 13, 2026, threat actors enrolled over 2,200 fake guest sessions across 118 ScreenConnect servers belonging to 109 MSPs and organizations. The unauthorized sessions masquerade as legitimate computers using crypto exchange-themed names like KUCOIN-SRV and BACKUP-PROBIT, displaying screenshots of trading desktops. The majority of connections originated from a single IONOS-hosted IP address. While no malicious activity has been directly observed, investigators suspect these sessions serve as bait to exploit CVE-2026-84869, a critical ScreenConnect vulnerability that could allow malicious guests to execute files on unpatched technician workstations with elevated privileges. The sessions maintain persistent connections every 151 seconds to appear online, potentially waiting for technicians to connect and expose their systems to exploitation.

results.name: GeoVision Camera Software Abused to Deploy XMRig Cryptominer
results.description: Widespread malicious activity was observed targeting GeoVision webcam software between November 8 and November 10, affecting ten accounts and 13 organizations across various industries. Attackers exploited publicly exposed GeoVision devices to execute commands through GeoStartupAgentService.exe under SYSTEM privileges. The attack chain involved PowerShell download cradles retrieving malicious scripts from a remote server, deploying a vulnerable driver for BYOVD attacks, and configuring IFEO Debugger hijacks to disable Windows Defender components. A custom Golang loader utilizing BitTorrent DHT and PKARR resolver was deployed to maintain dynamic command and control infrastructure. The campaign ultimately delivered XMRig cryptominer to hijack computing resources. The incident highlights risks associated with internet-exposed camera management systems and demonstrates sophisticated defense evasion techniques.

results.name: TypoPrompting: From AI Typos to Malware
results.description: Attackers leveraged 186 typosquatting domains across 27 AI brands including Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Midjourney, and ElevenLabs to distribute malicious payloads. Simple typing mistakes lead users to ClickFix lures executing hidden PowerShell commands, Microsoft Store-signed browser-hijacking applications, or search-hijacking extensions. One Claude typo delivered commands from decimal-encoded IP addresses, while others served Net Guard, a Store-signed application containing browser control capabilities. Additional routes deployed search-hijacking extensions affecting 972,000 users. The infrastructure spans 211 entry domains including lookalikes of banks, insurers, and enterprise software, with traffic distribution systems profiling visitors before serving platform-specific lures. This TypoPrompting pattern exploits legitimate workflow interruptions, turning routine AI tool access into malware delivery opportunities through parked domains and sophisticated redirect chains.

results.name: 56 AWS API calls in 141 milliseconds: Inside an AI-run intrusion
results.description: Between September 30 and October 16, 2026, a CyberStrikeAI server executed a sophisticated AWS intrusion spanning four accounts using eight compromised identities. The attack featured machine-speed credential harvesting, with one role executing 56 EC2 user data requests in just 141 milliseconds. The adversary systematically validated stolen credentials, extracted secrets from Secrets Manager, pulled EC2 user data scripts containing sensitive information, and executed remote commands via SSM SendCommand. The attack displayed automated tooling characteristics with intermittent activity across 16 days, including a deliberate 14-day gap that evaded time-based correlation rules. All 78 alerts generated were medium or low severity individually, becoming significant only when correlated by source IP. The intrusion originated from infrastructure in Hong Kong associated with the open-source CyberStrikeAI offensive security platform.

results.name: CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability
results.description: On September 27, 2026, Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771, a critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting NetScaler Application Delivery Controller and NetScaler Gateway with a CVSS score of 9.8. The vulnerability enables unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands without requiring optional features. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed worldwide exploitation. Attackers employ a staged exploitation chain involving access-log poisoning, where malicious Base64-encoded payloads are staged in HTTP User-Agent headers, followed by authentication log poisoning using forged PPE failure messages containing shell commands. A vulnerable Perl diagnostic script then executes the poisoned commands with elevated privileges. Observed activities include web shell deployment, PHP enablement, and delivery of FreeBSD implants from infrastructure overlapping with CVE-2026-75650 exploitation targeting Adobe Commerce systems.

results.name: YuanKong RAT: the Android remote-control service that stamps its operators' names into every build
results.description: YuanKong is a multi-tenant Android remote access trojan whose dropper stores decryption keys in cleartext configuration files. The malware uses a two-key XOR scheme to unpack payloads signed with a shared certificate across all operator builds. Each build embeds operator account identifiers as hardcoded string constants, including account IDs, operator handles, and enrollment codes that are transmitted to command-and-control servers. Analysis of 110 dropper samples revealed 57 distinct payloads belonging to 42 different operator accounts. The RAT steals credentials through screen capture, accessibility service abuse, and overlay attacks while escalating privileges by self-pairing with the device's own ADB daemon to obtain shell access. It communicates via Socket.IO over WebSocket with a shared set of C2 domains.

results.name: Inside Help TDS: Hotejka, Cloudflare Pages and Predictive Detection
results.description: Since April 2017, a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, believed to be a rebrand of ROI777, has operated the Help Traffic Distribution System (TDS), delivering tech support scams to victims. The operation uses browser fingerprinting and geolocation to redirect users through compromised websites, malvertising, social media, and spam to fake Microsoft security alerts that lock browsers and display fraudulent phone numbers. When victims call, operators from call centers guide them to install remote desktop tools like UltraViewer, granting complete system access for ongoing exploitation. Since April 2026, Hotejka has created over 20,000 disposable domains on free Cloudflare Pages infrastructure, generating approximately 300 new domains daily. Affiliates including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay drive traffic to the TDS. Infoblox developed predictive detection algorithms that identify malicious domains approximately seven days before deployment, reducing customer exposure from 4% to 0.5...

results.name: BREAK THE SILENCE: Tracking Silent Lynx Through Exposed Infrastructure
results.description: Silent Lynx, a persistent cyber espionage threat actor, has conducted targeted intrusion campaigns against government ministries, diplomatic missions, and civil society organizations across Central Asia since 2024. The group focuses on high-value public sector organizations in Commonwealth of Independent States countries, leveraging spear-phishing campaigns through compromised government email accounts and malware staging via GitHub. Operations from late 2024 through 2026 reveal extensive infrastructure including exposed open directories, newly registered domains, and GitHub repositories. The actor employs lightweight reverse shells, PowerShell scripts, proprietary tools, and commodity utilities. Recent activity shows adoption of exploit-assisted delivery via CVE-2025-8088, expanding focus on Linux systems, and interest in FortiWeb vulnerability CVE-2025-25257. Attribution indicators point to Russian-speaking operators likely based in Kazakhstan, with targeting concentrated on water resources, environmenta...

results.name: AI-Powered Espionage Campaign Targets Government Linux Infrastructure
results.description: An espionage campaign tracked as CL-UNK-1211 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure between October 2025 and April 2026, utilizing AI-generated payloads containing conversational annotations suggesting LLM or automated AI agent involvement. Attackers focused on Linux environments deploying web shells, custom cross-platform backdoors including SysGoRAT malware, and open-source tools to maintain persistent access. Operations included extensive reconnaissance, database dumping, mailbox enumeration targeting social media accounts linked to government emails, and sophisticated defense evasion techniques such as disabling endpoint protections, erasing system logs, and planting deceptive red-team markers to disguise malicious activity as legitimate security assessments.

results.name: KGB RAT: A Fully Undetectable Windows Trojan Built to Spy, Steal, and Terrorize
results.description: KGB RAT is a Windows Remote Access Trojan actively promoted on underground forums since late 2025, marketed deceptively as a legitimate administration tool. Sold through a Malware-as-a-Service model with pricing from $150 to $800, it features credential theft, keylogging, hidden desktop takeover, ransomware capabilities, and psychological harassment functions including screamers and forced blue screens. The tool ships with a built-in FUD crypter updated daily to evade Windows Defender, requires no port forwarding for C2 connectivity, and delivers Telegram-based notifications. Evidence suggests development began in early 2022. Based on NjRAT foundation, it targets multiple operators sharing a common builder, with at least one deployment featuring an active CryptoClipper module for cryptocurrency wallet address swapping.

results.name: Inside a PaperCut Attacker's AI Toolkit: Agent Instructions, Exploit Code, a Second RCE, and Victims Across 45+ Countries
results.description: Three exposed directories on infrastructure at 45.142.193[.]132 revealed an AI-orchestrated campaign targeting PaperCut NG/MF print management software. The exposed workbench contained AI-agent instructions, exploit code, operational logs, and post-exploitation tooling. Attackers exploited CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 through a Tapestry vulnerability chain, and developed a second RCE path via XML-RPC API abuse. The campaign deployed automated exploitation at scale using hundreds of AI agents running through OpenAI Codex and DeepSeek models. Post-exploitation activity included Windows credential harvesting, LSA secret extraction, reverse SOCKS5 pivoting using chisel, Metasploit automation, and Active Directory domain compromise. The actor's files documented 1,005 hosts across 45 countries in their reconnaissance pool, with 46 confirmed Active Directory domain compromises and 45 targets maintaining live internal access pivots at time of discovery.

results.name: DragonForce Ransomware Profile: From Affiliate Program to Cybercrime Cartel
results.description: DragonForce is a financially motivated ransomware operation that emerged in August 2023, initially using leaked LockBit 3.0 code and later transitioning to Conti v3-based variants. Operating as a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, they offer affiliates an 80% revenue share and comprehensive management tools. By March 2025, they evolved into a 'cartel' structure, providing white-label services. Their attacks primarily target organizations in the US and UK, spanning multiple sectors including manufacturing, professional services, retail, healthcare, and technology. The group actively recruits developers and reverse engineers while offering specialized data analysis services to help affiliates maximize extortion pressure. Notable incidents include a major MSP breach in May 2025 exploiting SimpleHelp vulnerabilities, cascading compromise across multiple client networks.

results.name: How AI Agents Turned One Exposed Endpoint into a Server Takeover
results.description: An investigation revealed the first confirmed incident where large language model-driven AI agents executed substantial portions of an attack. Within 24 hours, attackers exploited an exposed job-submission feature on an Apache Tomcat server running Spring Batch, requiring no authentication, zero-days, or new malware. The attacker used Cairn, an open-source AI agent orchestration platform, identified on the attacking infrastructure. Commands were executed through JavaScript via Nashorn engine, with results extracted through error messages in 1,800-byte chunks across hundreds of sequential requests. The attacker recovered plaintext database credentials from configuration files, enabled xp_cmdshell, and escalated privileges using PrintSpoofer and GodPotato tools to achieve SYSTEM access. Registry hives were extracted, administrator accounts created, and artifacts deleted. Machine-driven execution was evidenced by rapid command timing, programmatic job naming, structured output formatting, and automated error ...

results.name: PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization in September 2024 exploited CVE-2024-47575 on a FortiManager appliance, exfiltrating configurations and cryptographic material for over 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Attackers then exploited CVE-2025-61624 to deploy PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 malware that leaves no disk artifacts or network traces. The implant operates by patching running processes, creating covert inter-process communication channels between system daemons, and intercepting network traffic. Additional attack vectors included weaponizing Apache mod_md for reverse shell command and control, impersonating the FortiManager platform to compromise downstream devices, and deploying extensive anti-forensic measures. The intrusion demonstrates advanced tradecraft consistent with nation-state actors, highlighting the critical risk of centralized edge management platforms.

results.name: Beyond the clipboard: The evolving tradecraft of ClickFix
results.description: Threat actors continue to evolve ClickFix tactics, moving beyond simple clipboard-based social engineering to more sophisticated attack chains. Recent campaigns leverage malvertising through typosquatting, SEO poisoning, and compromised websites to deliver fake verification prompts. These attacks now employ elaborate PowerShell scripts with animated progress bars to mimic legitimate security checks. Observed payloads include Node.js-based RATs like DuskDesk, lateral movement techniques targeting domain controllers via WinRM and SSH tunnels, and steganographic delivery chains hiding executables within PNG files. Some campaigns utilize browser-cache-seeded attacks that detect the victim's browser and retrieve staged payloads from cached files. Defense requires user training to recognize social engineering, application control policies, and behavioral monitoring for suspicious command execution patterns and persistence mechanisms.

results.name: Ivanti CVE-2026-104935: Zero-Day Chain Exploited in Operation Innovate
results.description: Ivanti has released emergency security updates after attackers exploited a chain of three zero-day vulnerabilities in Connect Secure VPN appliances to gain root-level access without authentication. The attack began on October 3, targeting an appliance running version 22.8R2.4. Two vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-104935 with a CVSS score of 8.6, involving an authentication bypass and remote code execution through manipulated CGI requests and malicious file uploads. A third unpatched vulnerability allows privilege escalation to root by manipulating a privileged service through memory modification. While patches address the authentication bypass and RCE, the privilege escalation flaw remains unresolved. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog with an October 16 remediation deadline for federal agencies.

results.name: Hirudo: From Fake Updates to Patched Banking Apps
results.description: A new Android banking remote access trojan named Hirudo has been identified, combining credential theft with live remote control. It is delivered through shopping and entertainment apps that act as droppers, installing the trojan as a separate package behind fake update prompts. The malware replaces legitimate banking applications with patched versions that disable security checks from within the app itself. Eight Indonesian banking apps covering seven banks have been targeted with purpose-built replacements embedding a hooking engine. The campaign uses real advertising infrastructure including Amazon CloudFront for distribution, with targeting extending beyond Indonesia to China, India, Mexico, Morocco, Thailand, and Malaysia. Backend data from August 2026 revealed thousands of stolen credentials and device records.

results.name: ClingSTUN Turns Vulnerable Edge Devices Into Attacker Infrastructure
results.description: An evolving Linux malware campaign deploys ClingSTUN, a back-connect proxy backdoor exploiting known vulnerabilities in Internet-facing IoT and network devices. The malware establishes persistent access and converts compromised systems into remotely controlled proxy nodes. Supporting multiple Linux architectures, ClingSTUN combines boot persistence, process termination, watchdog manipulation, process concealment, remote command execution, and self-propagation. It abuses legitimate public STUN infrastructure for NAT traversal. The campaign has expanded the number of vulnerabilities and device vendors it targets over time, affecting products from D-Link, EnGenius, Realtek, TP-Link, AVTECH, Ivanti, Tenda, Lantronix, and others, highlighting the continued risk posed by unpatched, unsupported, and unnecessarily exposed Internet-facing devices.

results.name: Stolen webcam clips of 900+ victims feed North Korea's $400 million fake Zoom scheme
results.description: North Korean state-sponsored hackers have stolen over $400 million in cryptocurrency during the past 18 months through a sophisticated social engineering operation known as FaceStealer. The attackers compromise legitimate accounts on platforms like Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack, and Discord to invite targets to fake Zoom or Teams meetings. These fraudulent calls display stolen webcam footage of previous victims, creating the illusion of legitimate participants. During the calls, attackers claim audio issues and instruct victims to run malicious scripts that install cookie harvesters, keyloggers, screen capturers, and backdoors. Each successful attack records new victims whose footage is then used in subsequent operations. The scheme primarily targets cryptocurrency wallet holders, web3 workers, and open-source maintainers, with hackers sometimes waiting months or over a year before stealing cryptocurrency funds.

results.name: ESXi ransomware: why it is dangerous and how to defend against it
results.description: A recent investigation revealed how adversaries systematically destroyed an organization's virtualization estate over ten days by compromising four ESXi hosts, all virtual machines, both vCenter Server Appliances, and backup infrastructure. The attackers, identified as BlackNevas, exploited legitimate VMware management interfaces without using vulnerabilities. They gained access through compromised credentials from non-virtualization systems, established persistence using MeshAgent and Ligolo-ng on vCenter appliances, then leveraged Host Profiles to enable SSH on ESXi hosts. The payload was delivered via SFTP and executed selective overwrites of virtual disk files while backup systems were disrupted first. This demonstrates how hypervisor compromise through valid credentials and administrative features poses severe risk, requiring architectural defenses including treating vCenter as Tier 0 assets, separating virtualization identities from enterprise administration, implementing independent logging infrastr...

results.name: Luna Moth Returns, Re-Targeting Law Firms Through Access Tokens
results.description: The extortion group Luna Moth is re-targeting law firms that previously declined to pay ransom demands, employing a novel token-based exfiltration technique. Attackers impersonate IT support via video calls, convincing victims to extract Microsoft Graph access tokens from Microsoft 365 Copilot through browser developer tools. These stolen tokens bypass MFA and Conditional Access controls since validation occurs only at issuance, enabling bulk file downloads within approximately one hour. The group has simplified its attack chain from earlier campaigns that relied on multiple remote-management tools and manual exfiltration. This shift represents a broader trend toward identity-focused attacks that avoid malware and endpoint detection. Organizations should implement Continuous Access Evaluation with strict location enforcement to invalidate tokens used outside authorized networks.

results.name: Fake Zillow pages use ClickFix NetSupport RAT to target apartment hunters
results.description: A ClickFix campaign deployed NetSupport RAT through fraudulent Zillow apartment-review pages targeting Windows users. The attack leveraged social engineering by presenting fake verification checks that copied PowerShell commands to victims' clipboards. Users were instructed to execute these commands via Win+R, Ctrl+V, Enter key combinations, which fetched malicious scripts from decimal-encoded IP addresses. The scripts deployed NetSupport Manager remote administration software configured to hide windows and persist through startup folders. Targets primarily included apartment hunters and renters, with particular risk to those using work laptops. The campaign utilized short-lived domains with random numeric suffixes on .sbs TLD and wildcard subdomains, suggesting personalized targeting through direct messaging rather than search poisoning or malvertising. Attribution remains uncertain as NetSupport RAT is widely used across multiple threat actors.

results.name: 2026-11-12: SmartApeSG ClickFix campaign pushes CNCmachineRMS RAT
results.description: A malicious campaign utilizing SmartApeSG ClickFix (also known as BabaDeda) techniques has been observed distributing CNCmachineRMS RAT through fake CAPTCHA verification pages. The attack chain begins with compromised domains serving malicious JavaScript that injects ClickFix text for victims to paste into Windows Run windows. This retrieves an HTA file that subsequently downloads a ZIP archive containing a DLL side-loading package for deploying CNCmachineRMS RAT. The infection establishes command and control communication over TCP port 443 with encoded traffic. The campaign leverages social engineering through fraudulent CAPTCHA pages to trick users into executing malicious code, ultimately leading to RAT installation and persistent access.

results.name: Beware of Phishing Email Disguised as Purchase Order Confirmation Request (Xloader)
results.description: A phishing campaign distributes XLoader infostealer through emails disguised as purchase order confirmation requests. The attack chain begins with a malicious DOCX file that exploits Word's altChunk feature to execute an embedded RTF document. This RTF exploits CVE-2017-11882 through OLE objects to execute a VBS script, which drops encoded data and launches PowerShell scripts. The PowerShell scripts establish persistence through registry modifications and deploy a loader that decrypts and executes XLoader version 8.9 in memory. The final payload steals system information, browser credentials, and can download additional malware while communicating with its command and control server.

results.name: European Refrigeration Systems Cyber Sabotage
results.description: A series of cyberattacks targeting commercial refrigeration infrastructure across Europe exposed critical vulnerabilities in operational technology systems. Beginning October 2026 in France with approximately 700 affected supermarkets, the campaign expanded in November to Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Netherlands, Ireland, Estonia, Portugal, Italy, Finland, Germany, and Romania. Attackers manipulated refrigeration management interfaces, altering defrost cycles and temperature settings, causing product losses and business disruptions. France attributed the October attacks to Iran's IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh, while Russian-aligned groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed responsibility for the broader campaign. Technical analysis reveals the attacks exploited default configurations, weak passwords, and internet-exposed management systems rather than sophisticated malware. The incidents affected food retailers and attempted intrusions against meat-processing facilities and medical cold-storage systems, demonstr...

results.name: 2026 Q3 Linux SSH Server Targeted Malware Statistics Report
results.description: During Q3 2026, honeypot monitoring revealed attacks targeting poorly managed Linux SSH servers through brute force and dictionary attacks. Primary malware families included ShellBot (also known as PerlBot), a Perl-based DDoS bot with C&C infrastructure at specific IPs, and Fisieredoor, a backdoor capable of executing commands and deploying SSH dictionary attack tools. Attackers downloaded malware using wget or curl, then installed user-mode rootkits, XHide process masking tools, and XMRig cryptocurrency miners. The launcher malware utilized ld.so.preload to inject rootkits and disguised mining processes as legitimate bash sessions. Fisieredoor deployed additional tools including goauto and tsm for credential harvesting and lateral movement, transmitting successful authentication results to command servers.

results.name: Q3 2026 Statistical Report on Malware Targeting Windows Database Servers

Additional tools used included VShell for remote command execution, HackBrowserData for credential theft, Fscan for network reconnaissance, and Cloudflared for port exposure. Attackers created backdoor accounts for RDP access and operated SoftEther VPN servers in Cascade Connection mode as command and control infrastructure. The attacks primarily resulted from weak passwords, improper account management, and inadequate security measures on externally exposed database servers.

results.name: 2026 Third Quarter Windows Web Server Targeted Malware Statistics Report
results.description: This analysis examines attacks against Windows web servers during Q3 2026, focusing on Internet Information Services (IIS) and Apache Tomcat environments. Two prominent attack cases involving CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX are detailed. The first case deployed reverse shells connecting to 206.82.6.22, utilized Potato-family privilege escalation tools like SweetPotato and PrintSpoofer to obtain SYSTEM privileges, and installed Godzilla-style memory webshells. The second case leveraged the same vulnerability to deploy a Rust-based scanner that identified WordPress installations and reported findings via Telegram. Attackers subsequently conducted coin mining, established VPN servers, and maintained persistent remote access. Recommendations include applying current patches, minimizing exte...

results.name: Statistical Report on Malware Targeting Linux SSH Servers in the Third Quarter of 2026
results.description: During the third quarter of 2026, multiple attack campaigns targeted poorly managed Linux SSH servers using brute force, dictionary attacks, and vulnerability exploits. Threat actors deployed ShellBot, a Perl-based DDoS bot, utilizing C&C servers at specific IP addresses with capabilities including port scanning and UDP flooding. A sophisticated attack chain involved launcher malware that executed user-mode rootkit libSSL2.3.0.So via /etc/ld.so.preload, subsequently deploying XMRig cryptocurrency miner disguised as -bash using XHide process concealment tool. Additionally, Fisieredoor backdoor was deployed, capable of command execution and installing SSH brute-force tools including goauto and tsm-family, which systematically targeted systems using credential lists. Organizations must implement strong password policies, regular patching schedules, and access controls for externally exposed SSH infrastructure.

results.name: How AI Revived a Stalled Attack on a U.S. Retailer
results.description: In September 2026, attackers targeting a U.S. retail organization initially struggled with hand-typed commands that contained errors and were blocked by security software. The following day, their tactics dramatically shifted to using AI-generated PowerShell scripts characterized by error-free code, labeled output sections, and reasoning comments typical of large language models. This AI assistance enabled rapid exploitation within minutes, including credential harvesting from SolarWinds Orion software and lateral movement to additional servers. The attackers demonstrated financially motivated objectives by searching point-of-sale scripts for passwords and credentials. Infrastructure overlaps linked this intrusion to previous attacks in August and July 2026 that showed no AI assistance, suggesting AI capabilities were recently added to existing toolkits. Similar AI-assisted attacks proliferated across multiple sectors and countries throughout 2026, with activity significantly increasing in September.

results.name: PHP2Shell Exploitation on Check Point Gateway
results.description: In late October 2026, approximately one week after security fixes became available, attackers exploited vulnerable Mobile Access portals on Security Gateways, targeting Israeli organizations from IP address 130.94.19[.]204. The exploitation leveraged PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to gain initial access, followed by privilege escalation to root level. Attackers deployed PHP webshells for persistence, then installed TSGA malware and TSProxy backdoor components. The campaign expanded with lateral movement to VMware ESXi infrastructure, culminating in deployment of the destroy_v6 wiper and a politically-themed ransom rejection note. A second scanning wave on November 2nd targeted additional organizations worldwide without sector-specific focus, suggesting opportunistic access attempts. The toolset shows links to PhiliKit malware family and Chinese-nexus actors, though attribution remains ambiguous.

results.name: 0% GPU utilization: How SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining
results.description: Elastic Security Labs analyzes REF3364, a sophisticated Linux cryptomining intrusion combining custom malware with public miners. The toolkit features SANSAR, a Rust-based orchestrator managing CPU and GPU miners over Tor infrastructure. Attackers exploited an exposed Ray job agent to gain root access across three Linux GPU hosts. The operation deployed a kernel rootkit concealing processes and files, an NVIDIA Management Library wrapper falsifying GPU telemetry to show 0% utilization, and a backdoor named netns retrieving C2 addresses from Ethereum smart contracts. SANSAR supervises XMRig and SRBMiner-MULTI miners while maintaining command handlers for configuration management and interactive shells. The threat actor employed multiple stealth mechanisms including ftrace-based rootkit hooks, modified GPU monitoring libraries, and Tor-based communications with bridge support for enhanced anonymity.

results.name: ScreenConnect Attack: SCKit Turns Remote Support Into an Attack Platform

The investigation uncovered SCKit, a malicious toolkit designed to abuse ScreenConnect's remote management functionality. SCKit combines rogue remote access installations with attempts to compromise technicians through a Guest-to-Host file execution technique targeting CVE-2026-84869. The toolkit's RelayTrap component attempts to reverse normal support connections by replacing legitimate ScreenConnect Guest processes and sending malicious payloads to connecting technicians. Follow-on components seek to recover .ASPXAUTH cookies from technician browsers and reuse their management permissions to distribute commands across additional endpoints. Testing confirmed the attempt but found that current patched ScreenConnect Host clients successfully blocked the reverse execution. results.name: Crafty Microsoft Teams Booking Flow Disguises Device Code Phishing
results.description: A sophisticated device code phishing campaign was observed in mid-October targeting the construction industry. Attackers used a typosquatted domain and impersonated a senior vice president to deliver spear-phishing emails containing multi-stage redirects. The campaign featured a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler that disguised the device code authorization process within a booking workflow. When victims clicked through the booking interface, the site secretly initiated a Microsoft device-code sign-in and copied the generated code to the clipboard. The final step directed targets to Microsoft's legitimate device-login page to complete authorization. The encrypted phishing kit included fallbacks for MFA and used residential proxies to route traffic, making detection more challenging.

results.name: T-SQL Being Abused to Deliver Malware on Compromised MS SQL Servers
results.description: An active campaign discovered in October 2026 targets Internet-facing Microsoft SQL Server instances using T-SQL commands to deliver malicious payloads. Attackers scan IP ranges for exposed servers on TCP port 1433 and perform brute-force attacks using predefined credentials. Upon successful authentication, malicious T-SQL commands download and execute additional malware on compromised servers. The attack chain deploys a UPX-packed Go binary incorporating the Naabu scanner, which retrieves target IP ranges and performs port scanning. Compromised servers are infected with an XMRig cryptocurrency miner that hijacks CPU resources for Monero mining and Gh0st RAT providing remote access capabilities including keylogging, screen capture, file management, and over 30 control commands for complete system compromise.

results.name: Kimsuky attacks targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy
results.description: The Kimsuky threat group has launched spear phishing campaigns targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy through fraudulent international conference invitations and collaboration requests. This operation, dubbed GitPower, leverages legitimate development platforms like GitHub for malware distribution and data exfiltration. Attack vectors include malicious LNK files and fake Zoom installers, demonstrating links to previous CHM-based attack methodologies. The campaign appears to be state-sponsored cyber espionage focused on monitoring cooperation developments between South Korea and Ukraine. Organizations are advised to enhance EDR detection capabilities and implement threat hunting for suspicious LNK file execution, PowerShell abuse, and unauthorized GitHub communications.

results.name: The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar
results.description: A sophisticated command and control framework named Falcon (also known as XG or Xiàng Gē) has been identified operating entirely within browser contexts through malicious JavaScript. The framework compromises webmail portals and government web applications, enabling attackers to sideload malicious Chrome and Firefox extensions that steal passwords, emails, session cookies, and communications. Falcon also delivers an implant called Antino, which uses Microsoft OneDrive as a C2 channel. Between March and May 2026, government entities in one Middle Eastern country and four Southeast Asian countries were compromised, specifically targeting ministries of foreign affairs, defense, interior, and law enforcement agencies. The framework shares significant overlap with PeckBirdy and demonstrates advanced capabilities including browser proxy functionality, download interception, network traffic hijacking, and credential harvesting. The deployment suggests strategic intelligence collection objectives against governmen...

results.name: SCKit Worm Installs Rogue ScreenConnect Clients and Session Cookie Relays Across Hundreds of Endpoints
results.description: On November 11, 2026, operators exploited cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to deploy attacker-controlled clients and the SCKit toolkit across 288 hosts in 48 organizations. ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions as a precaution but had not identified the initial access vector. The attack involved two stages: spreading from infected endpoints to technician workstations via session cookie theft, then laterally to other accessible endpoints. SCKit consists of 16 PowerShell and batch scripts delivered as encrypted payloads, using system UUIDs as decryption keys. The toolkit installs rogue ScreenConnect clients, creates persistence mechanisms through scheduled tasks, and attempts console takeover. While endpoint infections succeeded, the technician workstation compromise functionality failed in all observed cases. The worm includes sophisticated features like browser cookie extraction, session replay, and automated payload distribution through ScreenConnect's Shared Toolbox.

results.name: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
results.description: Multiple threat actors have been deploying GSocket, an open source remote access tool, on compromised Linux servers to maintain persistent access even after initial vulnerabilities are patched. The activity increased 356.2% from March through August 2026, primarily targeting web applications and hosting environments, with education and research sectors representing 30.7% of affected organizations. GSocket relays traffic through a shared public network, eliminating traditional C2 infrastructure that defenders could block. Threat actors exploit internet-facing applications, deploy GSocket with renamed processes in memory-backed directories, establish persistence through cron and systemd, and in some cases escalate privileges using CVE-2026-43284. The tool's outbound-only connections and shared relay infrastructure make it particularly difficult to detect and remediate through conventional methods.

results.name: Beware of Phishing Email Disguised as Quotation Inquiry (SnakeKeylogger)
results.description: A phishing campaign disguised as quotation inquiry requests has been observed, where attackers impersonate purchasing team material management personnel requesting quote confirmations. The emails contain compressed attachments that, when extracted, reveal JavaScript files. These execute obfuscated PowerShell scripts that decrypt and run multi-stage payloads using AES-256-CBC encryption and XOR operations. The attack chain utilizes process hollowing techniques to inject the final payload into aspnet_compiler.exe. The ultimate malware is SnakeKeylogger, an infostealer that collects web browser credentials, system information, and keylogging data, exfiltrating it via SMTP or Telegram to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

results.name: The Rise of LLMjacking: How Attackers Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
results.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group identified multiple incidents where attackers hijacked enterprise Large Language Model (LLM) access in a tactic called LLMJacking. These intrusions affected organizations across financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific. Unlike cryptojacking's gradual resource consumption, LLMJacking can generate fraudulent cloud charges exceeding $100,000 per day within hours, with cumulative bills reaching $1 million before access revocation. Attackers obtain initial access through exposed cloud credentials, API keys, and service account tokens, then escalate privileges and deploy proxy infrastructure to resell stolen compute capacity through underground marketplaces operated by LLM Mixers, who aggregate and redistribute unauthorized model access to subscribers.

results.name: Off the Rails: Inside an Exposed Silent Lynx Server
results.description: An exposed open directory belonging to Silent Lynx, a Central Asia-focused espionage cluster, revealed the group's operations through October 2026. The directory contained tooling, data from active intrusions into government and critical infrastructure, and an AI agent used by the operator. The operator maintained persistent access to transport networks, collected government correspondence at scale including defence-related documents, and compromised a government geospatial platform. Implants matched known Laplas and Chvost families, alongside unreported variants. Lures impersonating Turkmenistan Railways were prepared for an upcoming campaign. A self-hosted AI agent running DeepSeek handled reconnaissance, collection and log cleanup. The operator worked in Russian with test traffic originating from residential Kazakhtelecom connections, supporting a Kazakhstan nexus assessment. Multiple OPSEC failures exposed the operation including storing everything on one server and leaving developer paths in binaries.

results.name: Citrus Ransomware: tactics, techniques, procedures, and links to Toy Ghouls
results.description: Citrus Ransomware represents a hybrid threat combining traditional infrastructure compromise techniques with modern evasion methods and AI-powered automation. The group gains initial access through compromised contractor accounts, using stolen credentials for VPN or RDP connections. Attackers employ VLESS tunnels disguised as HTTPS traffic and leverage large language models to generate commands and scripts. They exploit vulnerabilities like CVE-2026-54121 for privilege escalation, utilize tools including mimikatz and Snaffler for credential theft, and deploy the Sn00py ransomware via Group Policy Objects. The operation involves disabling security solutions, clearing event logs, and harvesting Telegram session data before encryption. The malware uses RSA-2048 and ChaCha20 algorithms, appending .citrus extensions to encrypted files. Links to Toy Ghouls suggest possible connections between Russian-speaking groups targeting Russian organizations exclusively.

results.name: From WhatsApp to SYSTEM: Inside the VulcanRAT207.A Intrusion Chain
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage intrusion chain begins with a WhatsApp-delivered financial document lure carrying Statement.exe. The malware employs NRV2E compression to conceal its true payload, which performs extensive host screening before attempting privilege elevation via COM-based techniques. Using PoolParty Variant 7 injection, the loader transfers execution into the Windows Task Scheduler process under LocalSystem authority. A downloader shellcode retrieves a compound bundle from a remote server, which deploys through a reflective loader. The deployment stage utilizes a signed GoFly driver to terminate Baidu security processes, establishes persistence via DLL side-loading with a legitimate Intel-signed VulkanInfo executable, and launches a WebSocket-based remote access trojan. The final VulcanRAT207.A payload provides extensive surveillance capabilities including shell access, keystroke capture, desktop control, network filtering, and process injection, while maintaining persistence through SYSTEM-leve...

results.name: From Endpoint to Funhouse: Changes in Ransomware Families and Kimsuky-Related Distribution Cases
results.description: A North Korean threat actor distributed Funhouse ransomware through malicious Korean-language documents disguised as resumes. Funhouse is a variant of the previously observed Endpoint ransomware. The attack chain involves multi-stage scripts including Batch, VBS, and PowerShell, leading to Quasar RAT installation before deploying the final ransomware payload. The campaign shares significant similarities with earlier Kimsuky Endpoint ransomware operations from early 2026, including identical mutex values, similar batch file structures, and comparable Quasar RAT configurations. The ransomware maintains key characteristics of the Endpoint family while updating encryption extensions, contact information, and C2 infrastructure. A notable shift involves using HWP documents instead of LNK files as initial infection vectors.

results.name: Analysis of Wpcdoor Attack Case Distributed Through Domestic DVR Management Software
results.description: A South Korean company's DVR management software (CMS) was exploited to distribute the Wpcdoor backdoor malware. The attack chain begins when CMS.exe installs rs.win32.exe along with a malicious IPHLPAPI.DLL file that loads via DLL side-loading. This first-stage downloader retrieves WpcMon.exe and samcli.dll, which acts as a second-stage downloader executing the Wpcdoor backdoor in memory. Wpcdoor exfiltrates system information including screenshots, clipboard data, browser credentials, wallet extension data, and supports various commands for remote control. The backdoor targets cryptocurrency wallets including MetaMask, Coinbase, and Phantom. The attacker, designated as Larva-26013, continues to deploy Wpcdoor through multiple attack vectors beyond the DVR software compromise.

results.name: A New ESXi Implant Linked to Settra Ransomware
results.description: GhostFrame is a previously undocumented post-exploitation framework enabling extensive control over compromised VMware ESXi environments. After root-level access is obtained, it provides a unified interface for accessing virtual machines, harvesting credentials, executing commands, and pivoting into victim networks. The framework operates from the virtualization layer, allowing attackers to control multiple VMs from a single compromised ESXi host. TAG-218, whose operations overlap with Settra ransomware, has been observed deploying GhostFrame following compromise of VPN appliances across the US and Europe.
