The implant establishes persistence, disables security controls, uses distinctive C2 communications across multiple ports, and integrates credential harvesting tools including VMkatz. This demonstrates how compromised hypervisors serve as centralized platforms for post-exploitation activities across virtualized environments.

results.name: Dark Web Profile: CyberXero
results.description: CyberXero is a Russian-speaking, financially motivated Initial Access Broker operating on Dark Web forums, conducting two parallel operations: a global mass-exploitation campaign targeting WordPress, Magento and e-commerce platforms, and a directed campaign focused on Ukrainian energy and utilities organizations. The actor distinguishes itself through AI augmentation, deploying 51 specialized Claude Code agents and PentAGI integrated with Cobalt Strike. Active since July 2026, CyberXero generates revenue through access brokering, payment data theft, and cryptocurrency payments. Over 40 organizations across Ukraine, Poland, China, Pakistan and the Netherlands have been affected, with more than 628,000 personal records exfiltrated and 429 WordPress administration panels compromised. The actor weaponizes vulnerabilities within 30 days and employs sophisticated techniques including SQL injection, PHP deserialization, and lateral movement tactics.

results.name: Not All That Glitters Is Gold: Tracking CopperDragon's Sparrow Framework Around the Globe
results.description: Over the past year, researchers investigated intrusion campaigns targeting high-profile organizations across Latin America, Asia, and Europe. These initially appeared independent but were linked through shared tools and infrastructure to the Sparrow malware ecosystem. CopperDragon is tracked as a digital quartermaster supporting China-nexus threat actors using the Sparrow cross-platform framework. Three distinct activity clusters were identified: SilentDelivery using watering-hole attacks with fake certificate warnings deploying SquadC backdoor; OceanGate targeting government and critical infrastructure with AnnobinDoor and SparrowShell backdoors; and DarkWire focusing on telecommunications and government entities using CopperDoor and CopperDNS backdoors. Operations employed sophisticated techniques including kernel rootkits, passive backdoors with packet interception, trojanized SSH tools, and extensive credential harvesting across Linux and Windows environments.

results.name: The Cold Chain on Fire: Unpatched Danfoss controllers exploited
results.description: Between October and November 2026, hundreds of supermarkets across France and over a dozen European countries suffered cyberattacks targeting unpatched Danfoss refrigeration controllers directly exposed to the internet. Attackers modified temperature settings and defrost cycles, causing food spoilage worth tens of millions of euros. The exploitation leveraged outdated firmware vulnerabilities, including authentication bypass flaws, without requiring sophisticated code execution capabilities. French authorities attributed the operations to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps unit "Shahid Kaveh," linked to CyberAveng3rs, known for previous attacks on U.S. critical infrastructure. The incidents demonstrate how exposed industrial control systems enable disruptive attacks and how generative AI can accelerate exploit development for ICS devices.

results.name: Inside an AhsayCBS Intrusion: Hidden Webshells, a CryptoMiner, and a C2 Implant
results.description: Between October 8 and 11, 2026, threat actors exploited authentication bypass and remote code execution vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS backup management software to compromise multiple servers. The intrusion involved deploying five distinct webshell families with varying capabilities, including command execution, file operations, and encrypted payload loaders hidden in PNG images. Attackers installed two XMRig cryptocurrency miners with scheduled task persistence, staged tunneling tools, and deployed a custom Python-based implant with environmental keying that communicated with command-and-control infrastructure. The operators created Microsoft Defender exclusions, accessed backup credentials through Veeam database queries, and specifically targeted backup infrastructure to potentially access stored credentials for hypervisors and domain accounts. The sophisticated multi-stage attack demonstrated significant operational patience beyond typical smash-and-grab cryptomining campaigns.

results.name: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild
results.description: A threat actor exploited IAM credentials from Qubole's AWS account (805246085872) to assume integration roles in customer environments between October 14 and October 26, 2026. The attacker used two IAM users and multiple VPN addresses to gain access, then conducted extensive reconnaissance across affected AWS accounts. Activities included enumerating storage, databases, and identity resources, harvesting credentials from Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store, and validating discovered credentials using TruffleHog. The actor exfiltrated data from S3 buckets opportunistically, downloading whatever each assumed role could access. A suspicious bootable Linux ISO image was also identified, designed for remote deployment and system reconnaissance. The campaign appears opportunistic rather than state-sponsored, exploiting trusted cross-account relationships that remained active despite many integrations being unused.

results.name: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
results.description: In October 2026, an AI-native penetration framework called ARTEX was observed conducting attacks against AWS environments, primarily targeting financial data. ARTEX operates through LLM agents that autonomously plan and execute attacks based on operator-defined objectives. Observed activity included exploitation of compromised long-term IAM access keys to search CloudWatch logs for financial information, file paths, and secrets. Additionally, attackers abused public Amazon Cognito user pools through anonymous sign-ups, token collection, and AWS account enumeration. Datadog identified hundreds of internet-exposed ARTEX consoles, often in Mandarin and hosted in Singapore and Hong Kong. The framework has been linked to China-aligned threat actor Storm-0940 and demonstrates sophisticated post-exploitation capabilities including automated resource discovery and credential harvesting across cloud environments.

results.name: Infostealer VOLTA That Has AI Assess Stolen Information
results.description: VOLTA is a Windows-based infostealer that incorporates an LLM assessment phase to evaluate stolen data. It operates through multiple phases: stealing credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets from browsers and applications; enriching data by querying external services with stolen tokens; sending bundled information to LLMs via OpenRouter to assess victim monetization value; and exfiltrating data through Telegram. The malware employs sophisticated techniques including Chrome App-Bound Encryption bypass, BIP-39 seed phrase validation, and automatic model switching when encountering refusals. Only one sample has been observed, submitted to VirusTotal in October 2026, with no confirmed in-the-wild usage.

results.name: Analyzing an Illegal Android Gambling App Built with Flutter
results.description: A Flutter-based Android malware campaign distributes an illegal online gambling application disguised as a Macau casino clone. The malware employs a sophisticated multi-tiered infrastructure with configuration servers, registration servers, and game servers. Victims engage in rigged casino games where mathematical odds favor cybercriminals, while the platform exploits gambling addiction through VIP recharges and referral schemes. The application exfiltrates sensitive data including geolocation coordinates, phone numbers, and device information through encrypted channels using AES encryption and HMAC-SHA256 authentication. Communication flows through multiple server tiers, with fallback mechanisms ensuring persistent connectivity. The malware represents professional-grade development with clean REST APIs and comprehensive backend ecosystem, though improved reverse engineering tools in 2026 have made analysis more feasible compared to 2024.

results.name: Malicious bee-js npm Release and Swarm Desktop Releases Deliver SleepyDuck Ethereum C2 Backdoor
results.description: On November 9, 2026, threat actors compromised Ethersphere's release pipeline through two compromised GitHub accounts, publishing malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 to npm and trojanized Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases. Both artifacts contained loaders fetching JavaScript from api[.]frameworkmetrics[.]xyz with full Node.js privileges. The infrastructure, including Ethereum smart contract 0xf8a900Db50b3331be6B768bA460BB59f3E40C344 for C2 addressing, matches SleepyDuck/EtherDuck operations from October 2026 targeting Open VSX extensions. The malicious npm package ran through legitimate trusted publishing workflows with valid SLSA provenance, while Swarm Desktop releases were signed with Apple Developer ID and notarized. Payloads exfiltrated Bee node passwords and wallet keys, then deployed Go backdoors on macOS/Linux and ScreenConnect remote access tools on Windows, specifically targeting developers working with Ethereum tooling.

results.name: Contagious Interview - One Interview Away From Infection
results.description: A sophisticated campaign targeting software developers through fake job interviews has been exposed, using a fraudulent company called AccuraSoftHire as a front. The operation lures developers through legitimate job platforms like Indeed and Glassdoor, with recruiters using identity-verified LinkedIn profiles. Candidates receive take-home coding assignments containing malicious npm packages disguised as Tailwind CSS plugins. When built, these packages deploy loaders that fetch additional payloads from remote servers using blockchain dead drops. The company's career site also serves a fake camera driver that delivers the same malware. This attack vector, linked to previous North Korean campaigns, has infected tens of thousands of machines globally and resulted in significant cryptocurrency theft, including the Binance breach exceeding six billion dollars.

results.name: The Industry Leader in Enterprise Brand Protection
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign has been identified targeting hospitality customers through fake hotel reservation pages impersonating Booking.com and other hotel services. The operation uses personalized reservation details including hotel names, dates, prices, guest information, and contact details to enhance credibility. Two main visual templates share the same underlying codebase: one closely mimics Booking.com while another uses generic Best Hotel Reservation branding. The kit employs advanced features including real-time card validation using Luhn checksums, interactive verification workflows, multi-language support spanning Japanese, Chinese, Korean, European languages and others, and three backend endpoints for tracking victim progression. Pages continue interaction after initial card submission through polling mechanisms that can present additional verification prompts. The campaign shows particular focus on Japanese hotels but is designed for global deployment across multiple countries and curr...

results.name: Shai-Hulud Descendant Surfaces in Malicious Ruby Gem That Steals Credentials and Poisons AI Tools
results.description: A malicious Ruby gem, strutil-core version 1.0.1, executes a 5.48 MB credential-stealing worm during installation. Published on November 1, 2026, by RubyGems account jamnajiea, the package was flagged 70 seconds after release and removed within five hours. The payload, a new build of the testmetest worm from the Miasma family descended from the Shai-Hulud toolkit, steals credentials from cloud services, CI systems, package registries, SSH, AI coding tools, and cryptocurrency wallets. It propagates through RubyGems, npm, PyPI, JFrog Artifactory, GitHub, GitLab, and SSH. The worm installs a Python backdoor controlled via signed GitHub commits, poisons AI tool configurations to maintain persistence, and includes a conditional wiper that deletes the user's home directory when a stolen GitHub token is revoked. The malware targets Linux and macOS systems on x86-64 and ARM64 architectures, excluding Russian-speaking locales.

results.name: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
results.description: In October 2026, the Cambodia-based threat actor Storm-3358 began leveraging the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX to target financial organizations primarily in Southeast Asia and select global institutions. The group combines ARTEX with conventional automated tools to scan internet-connected systems, exploit vulnerabilities including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery, and deploy open-source remote access trojans such as WISP, vshell, and AdaptixC2. ARTEX agents perform credential compromise, web shell deployment, lateral movement, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration at machine speed. This activity demonstrates an emerging trend of threat actors accelerating attack chains through agentic AI penetration testing frameworks, requiring defenders to similarly adopt AI-powered detection and response capabilities.

results.name: NEBULA: Seven Fake AI SDK Packages on npm Install a Windows RAT That Needs No DLL
results.description: In late September 2026, an actor deployed seven malicious npm packages masquerading as a NebulaAI software development kit to deliver a Windows remote-access trojan. The operation, tracked as NEBULA, spans four sequential burner accounts (nebulallms through nebulallms4), with api-nebula and llm-nebula remaining downloadable. Each package presents a convincing AI client facade while hiding an obfuscated installation hook executing malicious logic. The underlying RAT operates exclusively through direct NT and win32k syscalls, bypassing standard DLL imports with an empty Import Address Table. Features include hidden-desktop remote control (HVNC), Kernel Streaming for camera and microphone monitoring, and Winlogon Shell persistence. The payload is a customized KNTRAT variant communicating with 65.87.7.132 using user-agent kntrat/0xB15B00B6. The implant masquerades as conhost.exe and suppressed beaconing during analysis, consistent with embedded anti-analysis provisions.

results.name: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
results.description: An unidentified threat actor, likely Chinese-speaking and financially motivated, conducted targeted attacks against South Korean financial institutions between late September and early October 2026, successfully exfiltrating data. The adversary utilized ARTEX, a Chinese-developed open-source agentic penetration testing tool, combined with large language models including DeepSeek v4.1-flash, GLM-5.3, and Grok 4.6. Analysis of exposed directories revealed Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files, and operational details showing a two-server architecture involving Hong Kong-based infrastructure. The threat actor demonstrated sophisticated tradecraft by leveraging AI tooling to enhance operational tempo, enabling multiple intrusions within a compressed timeframe. Evidence suggests the attacker also researched Korean data breach marketplaces and Telegram channels for selling stolen information.

results.name: Threat Actors Exploit Critical AhsayCBS Flaws to Drop Webshells and XMRig Cryptominer
results.description: Beginning October 7, 2026, threat actors exploited two critical vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS backup utility (CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134) to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on exposed systems. The attackers chained these vulnerabilities together, first bypassing authentication and then executing code with SYSTEM privileges. Post-exploitation activities included deploying JSP webshells, installing XMRig cryptocurrency miners disguised as Microsoft Edge processes, and dropping an AI-assisted PowerShell script that monitors and terminates Task Manager to hide mining operations. The attackers established persistence through a fake Windows service named MicrosoftEdgeUpdateSvc and utilized a vulnerable WinRing0x64.sys kernel driver to enable kernel-level hardware access for optimized mining performance. All AhsayCBS versions through 10.3.4 are affected, with managed service providers being the primary targets.

results.name: MATCHBOIL: New tricks, same old evil intentions
results.description: ESET researchers documented the evolution of MATCHBOIL, a custom C# downloader used by Russia-aligned APT group UAC-0099. The malware downloads payloads from command-and-control servers, installs them, and establishes persistence on victim machines. Development traces back to April 2024, with continuous improvements through April 2026. Early versions used Unicode symbol obfuscation and custom string encryption, while later iterations employed the Eziriz .NET Reactor obfuscator. UAC-0099 progressively added sandbox detection methods, modified persistence mechanisms from registry keys to scheduled tasks, and introduced deceptive graphical interfaces. All observed victims were Ukrainian organizations across transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors. The group typically distributes MATCHBOIL through spearphishing emails containing malicious links that download VBScript files. MATCHBOIL often delivers MATCHWOK backdoor as its final payload.

results.name: Canto incognito: tracking the PoeLLM malware
results.description: Since April 2026, PoeLLM malware has been actively targeting exposed AI/LLM and open-source services including LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, and Gitea, with possible Ivanti Sentry targeting. The campaign employs an unusual command-and-control mechanism where infected systems derive C2 server addresses from keywords embedded in a poem hosted on GitHub. This financially-motivated operation deploys XMRig and Iron cryptocurrency miners, connecting victims to Kryptex mining infrastructure. Compromised hosts are repurposed as scanners and exploit servers to expand the botnet, which has impacted over 3,400 victim servers with peak activity exceeding 800 active servers daily. The campaign appears linked to an Italian-speaking threat actor and predominantly affects victims in the United States and Western Europe. Vulnerable routers are exploited to serve as C2 infrastructure.

results.name: RMM Tools Being Distributed Through Phishing Attacks (ScreenConnect, FleetDeck, Datto, SimpleHelp, JumpCloud, N-able)
results.description: Multiple Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools are being distributed through phishing campaigns involving video files and email attachments. Threat actors exploit legitimate RMM solutions like ScreenConnect, FleetDeck, Datto, SimpleHelp, JumpCloud, and N-able to gain remote access to compromised systems while evading security detection. These tools, typically used for legitimate IT administration purposes, are weaponized through various delivery methods including LNK files, BAT scripts, VBS files, and PDF documents disguised as business documents. The campaigns leverage social engineering tactics, presenting fake Adobe Acrobat updates, DocuSign viewers, and document access prompts to trick victims into installing these remote access tools. Each RMM tool contains configuration data linking back to attacker infrastructure, including deployment IDs, account identifiers, and command-and-control server addresses embedded within installation files.

results.name: DarkSword/Coruna Open Directory Finding
results.description: Five hosts exposed the complete DarkSword/Coruna iOS exploitation platform through open directories, revealing an active commercial exploitation-as-a-service operation. The platform targets cryptocurrency wallets across 18 different applications, extracting BIP39 recovery phrases and conducting automated theft. Analysis of the production server recovered 11 victim recovery phrases, 179 device loot directories, and a 75-account control-plane roster indicating an agent/reseller model. A separate China-based operator is deploying identical tooling through independent infrastructure at 66ds[.]lol, representing a distinct threat actor from previously documented DarkSword users. The infrastructure was operationally active during analysis, with beacon telemetry showing Chinese iOS devices polling every three seconds for hours. Development work targeting iOS 26 via CVE-2026-31001 was discovered but remains undeployed.

results.name: Armorsteal Unpacked: Breaking Down a Python Malware Kit That Steals Data and Mines Crypto
results.description: Armorsteal is a sophisticated Python-based malware kit that combines information stealing, cryptocurrency mining, and backdoor capabilities. Distributed through fake download pages for legitimate tools, it installs into C:\Windows\SystemHealth\Update with three scheduled tasks maintaining persistence. The malware uses PyArmor obfuscation and includes sandbox evasion by checking for cloud providers. Its modular architecture features a controller (SysMon.py) that functions as a backdoor accepting only RSA-signed code, a miner manager (xm_handler.py) running XMRig while detecting and evading monitoring tools, a spy module logging keystrokes and swapping clipboard cryptocurrency addresses, and a comprehensive stealer targeting browser credentials, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, and password manager vaults. The kit employs 11 failover C2 domains and adds Windows Defender exclusions to avoid detection.

results.name: Inside Help TDS: Hotejka, Cloudflare Pages and Predictive Detection
results.description: Infoblox attributes the Help Traffic Distribution System (TDS) to Hotejka, a small Russian-language affiliate program believed to be a rebrand of ROI777, which was exposed in 2018. Operating since April 2017, this TDS delivers tech support scams directing users to call centers where social engineering convinces victims to install remote desktop tools like UltraViewer, enabling persistent access for malicious activities. Hotejka's affiliates include Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay, who redirect traffic through compromised websites, malvertising, social media, and spam. Since April 2026, operations have leveraged free Cloudflare Pages infrastructure, creating approximately 300 new domains daily. Infoblox developed predictive detection capabilities that identify malicious domains seven days before deployment, successfully detecting over 16,000 domains and reducing customer exposure from 4% to 0.5%. The scam employs browser locks with alarming warnings impersonating Microsoft, ultimately leading vict...

results.name: Lookalike Domains Expose the iPhone Theft Economy
results.description: A thriving underground marketplace operating primarily through Telegram has emerged to unlock stolen iPhones, making phone theft profitable despite Apple's security features like Activation Lock. Thieves combine technical tools and social engineering through SMS phishing campaigns using lookalike domains to trick legitimate owners into surrendering their passcodes. These unlocking tools, sold on pay-as-you-go basis for $5-50, can jailbreak older phones and extract information for crafting credible phishing attacks. Analysis reveals over 10,000 domains associated with these operations, with DNS traffic increasing 350% in 2025. Sellers operate globally from countries including Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Venezuela, Mexico, and Brazil. The ecosystem prioritizes wiping devices for quick resale rather than data theft, with unlocked high-end phones fetching hundreds of dollars on black markets.

results.name: Remcos RAT
results.description: This intelligence analysis details a malicious campaign involving Remcos RAT, a commercially available remote access trojan. The attack chain begins with a weaponized Excel spreadsheet (Remittance Advice.xlsm) that executes VBA macros. Upon opening, PowerShell retrieves remote scripts (edi.vbs/firewall.vbs) from a malicious domain. The execution progresses through multiple stages, ultimately deploying the Remcos RAT payload. Command and control infrastructure utilizes domains at dvrlists[.]com and lbl[.]support. The threat demonstrates typical social engineering tactics using financial-themed lures to entice victims into enabling macros and initiating the infection chain.

results.name: FortiBleed Operations Continue Targeting Exposed Systems Leading to Reports of Lockouts
results.description: FortiBleed is an active global credential-compromise campaign targeting internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with over 86,644 compromised devices verified across 194 countries. The campaign exploits reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, enabling threat actors to harvest and crack authentication data at scale using distributed GPU clusters. Attackers scan for exposed FortiGate SSL VPN portals, collect credentials through stuffing and password spraying, and crack stolen password hashes offline. Once access is gained, they create new administrative accounts for persistence and conduct Active Directory enumeration to expand access. Affected organizations may experience lockouts as threat actors delete or modify existing accounts. The operation functions as an initial-access broker, with connections observed to INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates, representing a significant threat requiring immediate defensive action.

results.name: A Dish Served Lukewarm: The Refrigerator Botnet
results.description: Exposed Dixell/Copeland XWEB PRO refrigeration controllers are being exploited as abuse infrastructure. The STRIKE Team discovered a suspected SMTP botnet comprising nine IP addresses, with three confirmed as refrigeration controllers. These devices, used in supermarkets and cold storage facilities, remain exposed on the internet with unpatched vulnerabilities, particularly CVE-2026-25085. Attackers are repurposing these controllers as tunnel gateways, residential-proxy exits, and spam senders. Analysis revealed outbound-only SMTP traffic with significant target-list overlap among nodes, indicating coordinated operations. Of 1,041 mail targets, 508 were hit by multiple nodes, with the three most active sharing approximately 47% of their targets. The exposed controllers carry vulnerable firmware and lack security monitoring, making them ideal for prolonged malicious use without detection.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
results.description: ARTEX is an open-source, LLM-driven autonomous penetration testing framework released in July 2026 that integrates AI agents with reconnaissance and exploitation capabilities. As of November 2026, 1,465 hosts run exposed ARTEX consoles globally, with approximately 815 distinct deployments. CrowdStrike linked ARTEX usage to attacks against South Korean financial institutions, while Microsoft attributed its use to Storm-0940's ConnectWise supply chain compromise. The framework enables automated operations from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with minimal human intervention. Ten percent of ARTEX hosts also run other offensive tools including Cobalt Strike, Vshell, and additional AI attack frameworks. Operators frequently expose open directories containing exploit binaries, post-exploitation kits, and session histories. The tool's developer claimed it was intended for authorized testing and took the repository offline after public attribution, though archived copies remain circulating.

results.name: Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights
results.description: From July through September 2026, approximately 7.3 billion email-based phishing threats were detected, with September reaching nearly 3 billion attacks—a 41% increase from August. The quarter demonstrated significant shifts in attack techniques, including a sharp decline in QR code phishing, a recovery in CAPTCHA-gated attacks driven by SVG attachments, and persistent domain spoofing affecting 129 million messages impersonating business services. Credential theft remained the dominant objective across malicious attachments, while business contact impersonation declined and Teams-based threats increasingly used ordinary personal names rather than explicit help desk identities. Notable campaigns targeted legal organizations with personalized salary review lures leading to device code phishing, and Spanish-speaking users with purchase order and payroll themes delivering Agent Tesla malware. The disruption of Tycoon2FA phishing platform continued showing effectiveness with 99.8% volume reduction.

results.name: Iranian State-Aligned Threat Actor Masquerading as Dubai Airports IT Department Delivering Trojanized Coding Challenges - Blinder Tunnel Campaign Targeting Iraqi Critical Infrastructure
results.description: An Iranian state-aligned threat actor designated as CL-STA-1178 has been impersonating the Dubai Airports IT department to deliver trojanized coding challenges to high-value targets. The Blinder Tunnel campaign, active since November 2025 with attacks intensifying in March 2026, primarily targeted Iraqi critical infrastructure. The operation employs a three-step attack chain exploiting legitimate Windows developer files, AppDomainManager hijacking, and DLL sideloading to deploy ShelbyLoader V2 malware. Attackers abuse GitHub API infrastructure for command-and-control communications, utilizing repositories for decryption keys, payload downloads, and GitHub issues as fallback mechanisms. The campaign incorporates Peaky Blinders television show themes in its infrastructure naming and embeds the show's theme song in malware. Operational security failures exposed connections to a separate credential harvesting operation targeting Israeli entities using conflict-themed Google Drive lures during May-June 2026.

results.name: Akira Ransomware Attack Investigation
results.description: In September, an organization experienced an Akira ransomware attack, with investigation revealing the threat actor's tactics and tools. The attacker gained access through Remote Desktop Protocol, subsequently disabling antivirus protections on the compromised endpoint. The adversary deployed Rclone for data exfiltration purposes and utilized a GOST tunneling tool to maintain persistence within the network. Following these preparatory activities, the ransomware payload was executed. Forensic analysis of the impacted endpoints enabled investigators to identify key indicators of compromise, including command and control infrastructure and malicious executables. The investigation uncovered specific file paths and SHA256 hashes associated with the ransomware binary and GOST tunnel executable, along with the C2 server IP address used for tunnel communications.

results.name: Attackers Target AI Development Platform Langflow
results.description: In September 2026, F5 Labs detected 405 exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-0768, an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Langflow AI application-building platform, originating from 55 distinct IP addresses. This marks the first observation of an AI/ML development platform RCE in opportunistic internet-wide scanning. Captured payloads included capability probing with unique markers, timing-based execution checks, and environment harvesting attempts aimed at extracting cloud credentials, model API keys, and database secrets. Activity came primarily from two infrastructure clusters: Google Cloud hosts using environment-harvesting payloads with forged AI-crawler User-Agents, and European scanning subnets employing marker-based capability probing with spoofed localhost headers. The vulnerability, disclosed in January 2026, allows Python code injection through decorator and default-argument evaluation on the validation endpoint without authentication, enabling arbitrary code execution wit...

results.name: From Streaming to Stealing: Mirax and the Rise of Server-side Android Device Takeover in META
results.description: Between March and September 2026, thousands of Android devices in the META region were infected with Mirax malware, causing millions in estimated losses. The campaign uses malicious advertisements within low-reputation streaming apps on Google Play to distribute droppers installing the payload. Mirax impersonates Google Play Services using Cyrillic characters and coerces victims into granting Accessibility Service permissions, enabling complete device takeover. The malware employs server-side configuration with dual-WebSocket C2 infrastructure, DNS-over-HTTPS, and dynamically pushed phishing templates targeting over 20 regional banks and digital wallets. Attackers perform real-time remote control to execute unauthorized transactions appearing legitimate, with funds transferred to suspected mule accounts in India. Activity peaked during Eid holidays and remains ongoing.

results.name: CWPdoor: The Invisible Backdoor Living Inside Control Web Panel
results.description: A sophisticated passive backdoor named cwpdoor has been discovered targeting Control Web Panel (CWP), a free open-source server management control panel for Linux. The malware embeds malicious code directly into the legitimate cwpsrv binary and is triggered only by specially crafted HTTP requests containing cryptographic signatures. It executes commands remotely while suppressing access logs, leaving no forensic traces. With over 340,000 CWP instances exposed to the internet, the threat surface is substantial. First observed in June 2026 with deployment infrastructure at 136.0.141.71, the backdoor achieved zero detection rates across security vendors. A real-world victim was identified in Brazil in September 2026. The backdoor uses RSA signature verification and AES-256-CBC encryption for command and control communications through Unix domain sockets, making detection extremely difficult through conventional means.

results.name: New Lindnor Backdoor and Glut of Security Killers Used in Ransomware Attack on U.S. Org
results.description: Attackers leveraging Anubis ransomware targeted a U.S. organization in October 2026, deploying a previously undocumented custom backdoor named Lindnor. The backdoor masqueraded as Chrome and VMware components on Microsoft SQL Server machines. Within approximately one hour, threat actors dropped at least 13 executables designed to terminate security services, utilizing five publicly known vulnerable drivers through Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) techniques. The attackers installed AnyDesk remote access tool with Safe Mode persistence capabilities to maintain access when security software was not fully operational. Despite deploying numerous security evasion tools and establishing multiple persistence mechanisms, the file encryption payload was successfully blocked before execution. Anubis ransomware, operated by the Hawkmoth group as a ransomware-as-a-service operation, has claimed approximately 96 victims over the past year, with 52% located in the United States.

results.name: Inside Phexia: A macOS malware delivered through ClickFix
results.description: Phexia is a modular macOS backdoor and infostealer actively distributed through ClickFix campaigns since late 2025. The malware employs a multi-stage infection chain beginning with Terminal command execution that downloads shell scripts, establishes persistence via LaunchAgents, and deploys AppleScript-based loaders. A significant evolution occurred in May 2026 when operators began using Polygon blockchain smart contracts as command-and-control dead-drop resolvers, replacing earlier Telegram and Steam-based methods. Post-compromise activities include credential harvesting through fake password prompts, browser data theft, keychain extraction, password manager targeting, and XMRig cryptominer deployment. The malware collects login passwords, browser encryption keys, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet information. Multiple distinct builds communicate with rotating infrastructure, with reinfection potentially leaving concurrent installations active on compromised endpoints.

results.name: Supply chain attack: BO Team in a software developer's infrastructure
results.description: In June 2025, a software developer detected suspicious SMB connection attempts, revealing a sophisticated compromise by the Black Owl (BO Team) APT group. Attackers seized nearly all infrastructure components including domain controllers, servers, virtual environments, Ansible orchestration, backups, and security systems. They exploited CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) on VMware vCenter, compromised hypervisors using stolen SSH keys, and infiltrated both Windows and Linux infrastructures through credential theft and brute-force attacks. Evidence suggests attackers aimed to inject malicious code into the developer's software products to enable supply chain attacks against customers. The attackers maintained persistent access for several months using custom backdoors, but the operation was detected before completion, preventing potential widespread compromise of downstream organizations.

results.name: How to detect fileless attacks exploiting ToolShell: analyzing the Storm-2603 incident
results.description: In 2025, threat actors exploited CVE-2025-53770 and CVE-2025-53771 (ToolShell vulnerabilities) in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint to achieve remote code execution. Storm-2603 deployed ransomware following successful exploitation. Analysis of a December incident revealed attackers using the IIS worker process as an in-memory bridge, maintaining access entirely within w3wp.exe without writing to disk. The intrusion occurred in two stages: initial vulnerability fingerprinting on December 20, followed by full exploitation on December 24. The attackers deployed a fileless webshell framework with multiple modules for reconnaissance, privilege escalation via token impersonation, and persistence. Post-exploitation activities included deploying Velociraptor for command execution, establishing multiple tunneling mechanisms, attempting to kill EDR solutions using vulnerable drivers, and deploying Warlock ransomware.

results.name: Beyond valid credentials: How exposed AWS keys are tested for Amazon Bedrock access
results.description: Attackers who gain access to AWS credentials perform validation to determine their usefulness, particularly for Amazon Bedrock access. Multiple credential harvesting platforms, including KMON_NOC, have been identified that specifically test stolen AWS keys for LLM capabilities. These platforms validate credentials using GetCallerIdentity, then test Bedrock access through ListFoundationModels and Converse API calls. The validation process helps attackers assess credential value for resale in token-jacking markets, where stolen AI model access is sold below retail price. Scripts analyzed on VirusTotal demonstrate systematic testing across multiple regions, targeting Anthropic Claude models specifically, and enumerating promotional credits to assess financial value. This represents an evolution in credential validation similar to historical patterns observed with AWS SES/SNS services.

results.name: Grand Theft Auto VI Release Phishing Lures
results.description: Ahead of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI release on November 19, 2026, threat actors are exploiting consumer hype through phishing campaigns and fraudulent schemes. Analysis of 121 newly registered domains containing 'cyberleek' and other GTA VI-themed domains revealed four primary lure categories: fake downloads impersonating popular leaker CyberLeek, false early access offers, nonexistent mobile versions, and free game promises. These malicious sites distribute trojans, request cryptocurrency payments, employ content lockers that require survey completion for affiliate revenue, and harvest personal information. Tactics include fake storefronts impersonating developer Rockstar, fraudulent APK files requiring unsafe installation permissions, and giveaway scams using urgency counters. Post-launch threats are expected to shift toward in-game currency fraud, credential phishing for Rockstar and gaming platform accounts, and malware distribution through fake cheats and modifications.

results.name: SkyW4lker Phishing Kit: Microsoft 365 Threat to US Firms
results.description: SkyW4lker is an active device-code phishing kit targeting Microsoft 365 users primarily in the United States, Europe, and other regions. By exploiting Microsoft's legitimate authentication process, attackers gain access to corporate accounts without stealing passwords or bypassing MFA. Between June and October 2026, 618 sandbox analyses identified related activity, with submissions increasing from 20 in June to 200 in September. The United States accounts for 47% of submissions, with organizations in technology, manufacturing, and government sectors most affected. The kit uses phishing emails with password-protected attachments containing links that lead victims through CAPTCHA pages to Microsoft's authentication system. Technical analysis reveals obfuscated JavaScript, IP-based geolocation, and polling mechanisms. SkyW4lker shares infrastructure and code modules with the Gabagool credential phishing kit, suggesting both were developed by the same actor.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Binance heist: what we know, and what we see in TraderTraitor's toolkit
results.description: In October 2026, attackers stole approximately $6.34 billion from Binance in one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor operation. The multi-stage compromise involved malicious software delivered through a fake job interview, where engineers were tricked into downloading trojanized developer tools including a weaponized Terraform provider. ReversingLabs analysis uncovered malicious components in their telemetry 77 days before public disclosure and identified backdoor variants with earlier submission histories. The attack chain progressed from initial developer workstation compromise through lateral movement to ultimately reach Binance's wallet signing infrastructure. The trojanized tools included FLATROOF and ROOFDECK backdoors hidden within legitimate-looking developer software, demonstrating sophisticated supply chain compromise techniques targeting DevOps environments.

results.name: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
results.description: Hackers potentially linked to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service exploited previously patched iOS and Android vulnerabilities to target visitors of multiple websites. The operation included impersonating america250.org, a site celebrating American independence, and a luxury UK hotel website near sensitive government institutions where Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stayed. Attackers used JavaScript injection, proxy domains, and compromised a Ukrainian web analytics service to deliver three different zero-click exploit chains, including the DarkSword iOS exploit kit. The attacks aimed to steal browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords, and device data from diplomatic and high-profile targets related to Ukraine.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Summary of Malicious Program Distribution via Goddess of Victory: NIKKE PC Launcher
results.description: Level Infinite disclosed that the PC launcher for the game "Goddess of Victory: NIKKE" was compromised when four script files on the official CDN were tampered with between September 27 and November 4, 2026. The modified scripts downloaded a remote access agent (internally named K2F) that could execute arbitrary commands, steal credentials from browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, and cloud services. The malware persisted by injecting a DLL into Chrome and could intercept wallet recovery phrases. The compromise began with domain hijacking of insightjs.com on September 27, with script tampering occurring shortly after. Malicious payload distribution to users started October 30. Level Infinite detected the anomaly on November 4, replaced compromised files, and deployed automated detection and removal functionality on November 5. Users who launched the Windows PC launcher between September 27 and November 4 were potentially affected.

results.name: DarkBlinders: Active Espionage Campaign
results.description: A sophisticated cyberespionage operation targeting Israel and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq was conducted by DarkBlinders, the threat actor behind the Blinder Tunnel campaign. Active between August and October 2026, the campaign compromised a high-profile Israeli individual associated with the security sector and a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region. The operation employed government webmail, cloud-drive, and meeting-service lures, including phishing infrastructure impersonating the Gulf Cooperation Council Secretariat General and Kuwait's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. GitHub repositories under the PeakyBlindersTeam account served as command-and-control infrastructure. The attackers used selective activation, reviewing metadata from infected hosts before deploying a second-stage backdoor enabling PowerShell command execution. Post-compromise activity included credential theft and exfiltration of at least 1 GB of data from the government cloud environment. The activity demonstrates connectio...

results.name: ClingSTUN Linux Backdoor Abuses Public STUN Infrastructure
results.description: A Linux malware strain named ClingSTUN exploits unpatched vulnerabilities in Internet-facing devices to establish persistent footholds and functions as a back-connect proxy backdoor. The campaign targets IoT devices through multiple CVEs including command injection and code execution flaws in various vendors' products. ClingSTUN abuses legitimate public STUN infrastructure to discover externally mapped IP addresses, maintain NAT bindings, and improve connectivity between compromised hosts and operators. The malware employs sophisticated persistence mechanisms, terminates watchdog timers, kills competitor processes, and disguises itself as the init process. It maintains remote command execution capabilities and includes self-propagation exploits for seven additional vulnerabilities. The threat actor evolved their approach across three distinct periods, adjusting initial access strategies and expanding the list of targeted vulnerabilities from single-vendor exploits to multi-vendor command injection attacks ...

results.name: ARTEX Exposed: Infrastructure Behind the South Korea Bank Hack
results.description: Between late September and early October 2026, seven South Korean financial institutions experienced breaches affecting approximately 66,000 individuals and 2,200 corporations. The intrusions were attributed to ARTEX, an AI-driven autonomous penetration testing framework. Investigation revealed exposed infrastructure at 38.244.50[.]120 and 23.248.226[.]250, uncovering AI model-routing components, custom Claude Code skills, proxy management utilities, and exploitation tooling. The operation utilized DeepSeek, GLM, and Grok models through the xcai[.]pro reseller domain. Recovered artifacts included FOFA reconnaissance tools, JNDI/LDAP exploitation chains, Linux privilege escalation exploits, cryptocurrency-exchange access scripts, and mobile-device utilities. The infrastructure spanned multiple countries with 1,303 distinct IP addresses identified through certificate, malware classification, and HTTP title hunting methods.

results.name: Not Actually Suspended: How a Bank-Phishing Network Fakes Its Own Takedown
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign targets 189 US financial institutions through 248 live look-alike domains using a distinctive naming pattern combining urgency keywords with bank names. The operation employs an innovative cloaking mechanism that displays fake "account suspended" pages to returning visitors while serving actual phishing content to first-time visitors, effectively evading takedown efforts. The infrastructure focuses on business banking and treasury portals, which provide access to larger balances and transfer capabilities. All domains operate behind Cloudflare, with hosting traced to shared servers at two providers. Network analysis reveals connections to a centralized backend managing additional phishing operations targeting UK, Netherlands, Australian, and New Zealand institutions. The campaign is administered through a jump server accessed via Remote Desktop from a UK residential broadband connection, representing the strongest lead to the operator's identity.

results.name: KeyHunter Operation: Harvard Alumni Data, Stanford Applications and LLM Key Theft
results.description: A Chinese-speaking threat actor identified as leepsmarts conducted a multi-vector operation combining LLM API credential theft with academic fraud targeting 20 universities. The campaign harvested 2,233 API keys from misconfigured cloud infrastructure across platforms like Vercel, Netlify, and Railway, with 12 marked valid. The actor created fraudulent student accounts at institutions including NYU, UC Berkeley, and Oregon State, while processing 195 Harvard alumni records from a torrent-distributed dataset. The operation employed AI agent frameworks through Telegram bots for automated scanning, validation, and account creation. Parallel financial fraud activities included a Harmony ONE cryptocurrency drainer capturing victim seed phrases and credit card validation using stolen Stripe merchant keys. Infrastructure spanning China, South Korea, Malaysia, and the US was discovered through an exposed directory listing revealing tools, scripts, and operational logs dating back to January 2026.

results.name: From Business Emails to XLoader: An Order Lure That Led to In-Memory Injection
results.description: Morphisec has observed increased XLoader activity using business-themed email lures. The attack chain begins with order confirmation or payment request emails containing RAR archives that hold obfuscated JScript files. When executed, the JScript extracts an x86 LuaJIT interpreter and Lua loader to the user's Documents directory. The Lua loader attempts security interference, decodes an embedded packed PE, and manually maps it into LuaJIT memory. The packer then decrypts the XLoader core and executes it within the same thread. XLoader creates a clone of itself and uses shared-section injection to map into a selected x86 target process, redirecting thread execution context. The final payload implements credential stealing capabilities including Windows Vault enumeration and cookie extraction, while communicating with 16 configured C2 endpoints. Additional payloads delivered in this campaign include Agent Tesla, Remcos, and XWorm.

results.name: Poisoned Source: APT29 Watering Holes Targets Mobile Devices
results.description: Sekoia TDR identified a large-scale watering hole campaign employing three infection vectors: compromised legitimate websites, Adversary-in-the-Middle-like impersonating high-profile domains, and supply-chain compromise of Ukrainian Plerdy analytics service. The injected JavaScript code profiles browser and device attributes before delivering platform-specific n-day exploit chains targeting iOS or Android devices. Exploited vulnerabilities include CVE-2025-43529, CVE-2024-27834, CVE-2026-20700, CVE-2025-14174, CVE-2025-43510, CVE-2025-43520, CVE-2026-3910, and CVE-2025-27038. Final payloads exfiltrate browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords, and comprehensive device data without persistence, consistent with intelligence-gathering objectives enabling session hijacking and access to browser-based services. Based on technical overlaps, operational patterns, victimology and infrastructure analysis, this campaign is attributed with moderate-to-high confidence to APT29, a Russian nexus intrusion set widely linked to th...
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: VAPOR PANDA Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Grow Global Espionage Campaign
results.description: VAPOR PANDA conducted a sophisticated espionage campaign beginning October 17, 2026, using the ARTEX AI-driven framework alongside DeepSeek and commercial LLMs to orchestrate parallel intrusions against over 200 organizations worldwide. Targets included foreign ministries across Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, plus U.S.-based semiconductor, defense, pharmaceutical, nuclear, and telecommunications entities. The adversary deployed BLOODALCHEMY backdoor, conducted credential spraying, and explicitly instructed AI agents to identify systems without endpoint security sensors. This represents an escalation from single intrusions to multiple simultaneous engagements, with agents autonomously pursuing attack paths while human operators provided strategic direction in Chinese. The campaign demonstrated how threat actors combine open-source AI frameworks with commercial LLMs to dramatically scale intrusion operations beyond manual capabilities.

results.name: Caught in 4K: The Gentlemen Files
results.description: A Russian-speaking affiliate of the Gentlemen ransomware group, identifying as Azazel, compromised over two dozen organizations across six countries while simultaneously betraying the RaaS operator. The threat actor deployed independent leak site LEAKNED, keeping all extortion proceeds. Attack chains primarily exploited CI/CD secrets from GitLab instances, with one deep compromise involving an AI platform through SSRF, credential decryption, and continuous object storage exfiltration. Azazel operationalized MCP (Model Context Protocol) as a command-and-control channel, marking the first documented criminal use of AI assistant tooling for attack execution. Infrastructure consisted of three nodes totaling over 50TB storage capacity, with approximately 6TB of actively transferring victim data discovered during investigation. Victims spanned logistics, insurance, pharmaceutical, AI, medical devices, and government-adjacent sectors.

results.name: A STUNning Disguise: Cling Malware Masquerades as Google
results.description: A sophisticated IoT botnet dubbed Cling has been discovered exploiting vulnerable internet-exposed devices through CVE-2021-35394 and other command-injection flaws. The malware distinguishes itself by abusing STUN protocol traffic and public STUN infrastructure for command-and-control communications, making malicious activity appear as legitimate NAT-traversal behavior. Cling propagates through multiple CVE exploits targeting routers, DVRs and embedded appliances, establishes persistence via init scripts and wget binary replacement, then communicates with operators through STUN-like exchanges with public servers. The botnet operator uses IP spoofing to make commands appear as if originating from Google's STUN infrastructure. Capabilities include propagation scanning, DDoS flooding, TCP tunneling and proxy relay functions. The malware supports various attack commands hidden within STUN transaction ID fields while maintaining a low detection profile by blending into legitimate application traffic from collab...

results.name: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
results.description: A compromised version of the Claude Code extension (anthropic.claude-code, versions 2.1.313 and 2.1.312) was distributed through the Cursor extension marketplace from October 29, 2026, between 2:27 AM and 1:35 PM PDT. The malicious extension contained injected JavaScript that executed during module loading to establish persistent backdoor access. The loader collected host reconnaissance data, installed an attacker-controlled SSH key, enabled local SSH services, established reverse SSH tunneling to infrastructure at 134.209.82.225, and configured platform-specific persistence mechanisms including macOS LaunchAgents, Linux cron jobs, and Windows scheduled tasks. The attack leveraged built-in system tools to avoid detection while maintaining access. Microsoft confirmed the malicious packages were never distributed through Visual Studio Marketplace or npm, and Anthropic's systems were not compromised. The incident appears limited to Cursor marketplace.

results.name: Fake-download campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads
results.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified an evolving campaign targeting users searching for cracked commercial software, free games, activators, and unofficial utilities. The operation uses trojanized Inno Setup-style installers to distribute multiple monetized software payloads through a per-offer callback and status-tracking system. Three downstream monetization branches transform affected devices into monetized assets: routing third-party internet traffic through the device via WorldProxyPool, enrolling devices in distributed-computing platforms through CharityEngine and BOINC, or installing utility-style software such as Advanced Windows Manager. These components are silently installed through deceptive software bundles without informed user consent, introducing security and privacy risks. The campaign employs a four-stage attack chain progressing from deceptive lures through Inno-based staging, offer-controlled payload delivery, and installation of monetization branches using scheduled tasks for persi...

results.name: Free the Model, Sell the Gateway: Prompt Adware hidden in Jailbreak Bundles
results.description: Check Point Research discovered the Haiou jailbreak bundle, a prompt package targeting OpenAI Codex designed to weaken model guardrails for security-related tasks including hacking and software cracking. The bundle functions as prompt adware by modifying Codex configuration files to inject advertisements for the author's LLM gateway service into agent responses. The jailbreak employs various techniques including role-playing, context-reframing into CTF scenarios, and refusal suppression. Researchers found this bundle on a misconfigured webserver alongside Cobalt Strike, VulnClaw agent, and Ladon framework, indicating active use by cybercrime actors. The freely distributed jailbreak serves as an acquisition channel for a paid gateway service. The bundle installs security-focused skills for penetration testing, reverse engineering, and game security, while persistently injecting promotional content through encrypted payload files distributed via GitHub and Chinese platforms.

results.name: BOSSAI: Inside the AI attack mesh that targeted Taiwan's emergency services
results.description: Acronis Threat Research Unit identified a single operator utilizing a mesh of 12 AI agents called BOSSAI to conduct persistent campaigns across 11 countries. The attacker deployed both abliterated and commercial AI models working in specialized roles - infrastructure builders, vulnerability scanners, and active exploitation agents. Primary targets included emergency services, universities, financial institutions, and government systems in Taiwan, Thailand, and Mexico. Confirmed breaches involved exfiltration of medical records from Taipei emergency services, student data from Thai universities, and collection of over 200,000 Mexican residential phone records. Commercial AI models repeatedly refused malicious instructions despite jailbreak attempts, forcing the operator to rely on less effective abliterated local models. The investigation exposed complete operational infrastructure including command histories, agent conversations, and victim data, revealing both the power and limitations of AI-augmented off...
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Gorbag: Orcs at the border harvesting intelligence from Ukraine
results.description: A Russia-aligned threat actor named Gorbag has been operating since February 2025, conducting highly targeted cyberespionage operations against Ukrainian organizations. The group primarily focuses on law enforcement, justice entities, local administrations near the front line, and the defense sector. Rather than establishing long-term access, Gorbag employs simple infostealers for rapid intelligence collection, harvesting browser credentials, VPN configurations, and selected documents in single-pass operations. The group's toolset includes Prime ReverseShell (a PowerShell reverse shell) and BeautyStealer (a C++ browser-data and file stealer). Initial compromise occurs through spearphishing emails with malicious attachments. In early 2026, Gorbag updated its attack chain to exploit CVE-2025-8088, a WinRAR path traversal vulnerability. The operational focus on quick data collection suggests Gorbag may function as an initial access broker, sharing collected credentials with other Russia-aligned threat actors ...

results.name: XWorm Malware: Worming Its Way From Entry to Exploitation
results.description: XWorm is a versatile modular malware that poses a multifaceted threat through remote access, data theft, ransomware delivery, and botnet creation. Associated with the DDGroup cybercrime group, it rapidly gained notoriety for using advanced techniques. The malware employs diverse delivery methods including phishing emails with malicious attachments, drive-by downloads, exploit kits targeting browser vulnerabilities, USB drives, and Remote Desktop Protocol exploitation. Once established, XWorm steals sensitive data like passwords and credit card information, deploys additional malware strains including ransomware and spyware, and causes system crashes and denial-of-service attacks. Its modular nature and varied attack vectors make it a persistent threat requiring robust cybersecurity measures and continuous vigilance.

results.name: StyleSmuggler Exploitation Deploys PSK Agent RAT Against Magento Stores
results.description: Between September 9 and September 13, 2026, a coordinated campaign exploited Magento and Adobe Commerce stores across Western Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific using CVE-2026-75650 (StyleSmuggler). The attack chain delivered a shell-script dropper, PSK Agent RAT, and PHP webshell through the /paypal/transparent/response/ endpoint. The dropper achieved 0% detection on VirusTotal at time of analysis. The campaign deployed chi_down, a 10.5 MB obfuscated Go binary with remote access capabilities including command execution, SOCKS5 proxying, and encrypted communications. DNS exfiltration was used to track successful compromises. Chinese-language comments in the dropper and infrastructure naming suggest a likely Chinese-speaking operator, though attribution to a specific threat group is not supported. Multiple operators are exploiting the same vulnerability with distinct toolkits.

results.name: Yoba Malware Campaign Abuses Signed AI Applications to Evade Detection
results.description: A sophisticated campaign tracked as Yoba distributes cryptocurrency mining malware through fraudulent GitHub repositories impersonating ChatGPT and Claude AI applications. Attackers leverage legitimate, digitally signed executables from OpenAI and Anthropic alongside malicious DLLs to achieve DLL sideloading, evading detection through trusted software signatures. The multistage infection chain employs YobaDropper and YobaLoader components with anti-analysis techniques including process verification, execution delays, and regional language exclusions. C2 communication leverages Telegram profile imagery combined with domain generation algorithms, DNS over HTTPS via Google, and public hosting services like Catbox to retrieve encrypted payloads. While XMRig cryptocurrency miner deployment was observed, the loader architecture supports additional Windows executables and PowerShell payloads, suggesting potential expansion beyond cryptojacking operations.

results.name: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
results.description: Threat actors are hijacking enterprise access to Large Language Models through a tactic called LLMJacking, impacting organizations across North America, South America, and Asia Pacific in financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors. Unlike cryptojacking's gradual consumption, LLMJacking generates massive spikes in fraudulent cloud charges, with incidents exceeding $100,000 USD daily and reaching $1 million USD cumulatively. Actors establish initial access through exposed cloud identity tokens, IAM credentials, Service Account keys, and stolen API keys. They escalate privileges, conduct reconnaissance, and monetize compromised resources through LLM Mixers—illicit routing gateways that proxy and resell unauthorized LLM access. The ecosystem shows sophisticated specialization with distinct operational clusters coordinating compromises and downstream monetization infrastructure.

results.name: Exploitation Targeting Node-RED, a Tool Embedded in ICS Products
results.description: On October 30, 2026, exploitation activity was detected targeting CVE-2026-58115, an unauthenticated Node-RED admin API vulnerability. Attackers deployed malicious flows that automatically download and execute Linux bots through three layers of encoding. The exploit originated from IP 4.201.105.116 in Microsoft's network and utilized Node-RED's inject and exec nodes to execute commands without authentication. The dropper retrieved binaries from 85.215.73.250:8080, saving them to RAM-backed storage at /dev/shm/.b to avoid disk forensics. Multiple payload variants were observed, including staged shell scripts and persistent webshells. The activity demonstrates opportunistic mass scanning across multiple CVEs rather than targeted operations. Node-RED is embedded in critical infrastructure products including Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 devices, making this vulnerability particularly significant for industrial control systems environments.

results.name: BITTER Expands Its Arsenal with PapRAT
results.description: A cyberespionage group known as BITTER has been conducting campaigns targeting South Asian organizations using PowerShell scripts and a custom remote access trojan called PapRAT. Three distinct infection chains have been identified: one exploiting Windows ftp.exe with malicious LNK files, another using VHDX disk images containing MSI installers, and a third combining URL shortcuts with WebDAV to deploy PapRAT. The malware exists in both C++ and Rust implementations, with capabilities including command execution, file manipulation, directory enumeration, screenshot capture, and secondary payload delivery. PapRAT maintains persistent access through scheduled tasks and communicates with command-and-control servers over HTTP. The Rust variant introduces enhanced functionality including PowerShell execution and sleep commands. Targets are concentrated in South Asian government, energy, and engineering sectors.

results.name: The Internals of a Badbox Operation
results.description: Investigation reveals a massive supply chain compromise involving MECOOL Android set-top boxes manufactured by Videostrong Technology Co., Ltd. Over 1.3 million devices were pre-infected with the x.cpe backdoor, granting operators system-level access through MQTT infrastructure. The backdoor deploys multiple payloads including residential proxy SDKs and ad fraud modules like AdMoyu, Appsalt, APSolo, LinkFog, and Gaganode. Approximately 500,000 devices remain actively online, predominantly affecting Malaysia, Mexico, and Brazil. The operation functions as a pay-per-install campaign fueling ad fraud and proxy ecosystems. Google has permanently banned Videostrong from the Android ecosystem following these findings. Investigation conducted in partnership with Motion Picture Association, Google, Plume, Trend Micro, Lumen, and HUMAN Security.

results.name: SEO Poisoning Campaign Targets DeepSeek Users: Chinese Threat Actor Deploys Kong RAT via Multi-Stage Attacks
results.description: A sophisticated SEO poisoning campaign targets users searching for DeepSeek AI tools through malicious lookalike domains positioned on first-page search results. The attack employs a multi-stage infection chain beginning with weaponized MSI files disguised as legitimate DeepSeek software. The execution flow progresses through multiple stages involving shellcode, DLL side-loading via legitimate Cyglaunch software, and ultimately deploys Kong RAT. The threat actor registered domains mimicking DeepSeek and distributed ZIP archives containing code-signed fake installers to add legitimacy. Attribution points to a potential Chinese threat actor based on PDB paths referencing '52pojie', a Chinese cybersecurity forum. This campaign appears to be a continuation of previous operations from April 2026 targeting users of Chinese developer tools including FinalShell SSH client, Xshell, and Clash proxy. The final payload includes keylogger functionality and establishes persistence through registry modifications.

results.name: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
results.description: Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor that enrolled over 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet. The backdoor was intentionally developed and operated by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android OEM/ODM, who monetized it by selling access to criminal affiliates. These affiliates loaded malware modules conducting ad-fraud, enrolling devices into residential proxy networks, and installing additional malware. The disruption also severed access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices by taking down affiliate C2 domains. The malicious software was built directly into various device models over multiple years with dedicated infrastructure. Google has banned Videostrong from making certified Android devices and implemented improvements to firmware integrity reviews on Android TV devices.

results.name: Hackers Use Fake ChatGPT Plus Billing Emails to Steal Credit Card Details and OTP Codes
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign impersonates OpenAI by sending fraudulent ChatGPT Plus billing emails claiming failed subscription payments. Victims are directed to fake payment pages hosted on compromised WordPress instances under Nexcess's nxcli.io infrastructure. The operation features live attacker involvement, where operators monitor submitted credit card information and dynamically decide whether to request one-time passwords through a real-time polling mechanism. After victims submit payment details including card numbers, expiry dates, CVV codes, and cardholder names, the page maintains a loading animation while the browser polls a backend system approximately every 500 milliseconds. The attackers can then redirect victims to verification-code collection pages to complete fraudulent transactions. The campaign uses distinctive redirect domains and identical client-side code across multiple instances.

results.name: CyberStrikeAI attacks educational institutions
results.description: An open-source framework called CyberStrikeAI was used in real-world attacks against educational institutions across Africa and Latin America. The framework combines LLM-based orchestration with a traditional C2 server, where an AI model on the server plans actions and generates commands while an implant executes them on compromised hosts. Attackers initially gained access through compromised SQL Server infrastructure, then deployed the CyberStrikeAI agent which performed reconnaissance, privilege escalation, credential dumping, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. The AI orchestrator automated post-exploitation activities that traditionally require manual operator intervention, reducing the skill barrier for attackers. While the AI component operates server-side, the actual malicious activities on victim systems use standard techniques like Kerberoasting, AS-REP Roasting, LSASS dumps, DCSync, and Golden Ticket attacks, making them detectable through conventional security controls. Chinese-language art...

results.name: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
results.description: VOLTA is a sophisticated Windows infostealer that incorporates AI-powered victim profiling to prioritize targets based on monetization potential. After harvesting credentials, browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, sessions from various platforms, and personal information, it compiles a structured evidence bundle and submits it to OpenRouter using LLM models like Claude Opus, with fallback options to Kimi-K2 and Gemini. The LLM acts as a forensic intelligence analyst, ranking stolen assets by value and assessing victim security posture. VOLTA performs live enrichment by accessing victim Gmail, Uber Eats, DoorDash, Discord, and Roblox accounts using stolen tokens. The malware self-deletes and operates through third-party infrastructure without actor-owned servers, suggesting a builder-based distribution model where customers can deploy customized versions.

results.name: Hackers Impersonate IT Help Desk on Microsoft Teams to Hijack Active Directory Accounts and Steal Data
results.description: Attackers impersonated IT help desk personnel on Microsoft Teams to gain unauthorized access to Active Directory environments through social engineering and misconfigured certificate services. Two distinct intrusion campaigns leveraged Quick Assist remote support sessions after convincing users to share connection codes. Adversaries deployed portable Python, Bun, and Java runtimes to enumerate domain infrastructure and exploit vulnerable Active Directory Certificate Services configurations through ESC1 and ESC8 attack paths. In one incident, attackers obtained certificates for multiple privileged accounts and performed DCSync operations to harvest credentials. Data exfiltration was conducted using Rclone transferred to external SFTP destinations. The second intrusion used PetitPotam to coerce domain controller authentication and relay NTLM credentials to obtain unauthorized certificates. Neither attack exploited Teams vulnerabilities, but rather combined impersonation tactics, legitimate remote access tool...

results.name: North Korea's Crypto Heists Start on the Open Internet
results.description: North Korean operators execute cryptocurrency thefts by initially compromising developers through social engineering on the open internet before moving operations on-chain. The Bybit theft in February 2025 began when operators tricked a Safe{Wallet} engineer into running a malicious stock-trading project via getstockprice[.]com, later planting code in Bybit's wallet interface. Binance experienced similar compromise through a DevOps engineer's laptop. These operations rely on registering domains before targeting victims, with bybit-assessment[.]com registered hours before the Bybit theft. An investigation revealed three US-registered front companies (BlockNovas, Angeloper Agency, and SoftGlide) used to deliver malware through fake job interviews. Preemptive defense mechanisms identified 206 Binance-named domains with maximum risk scores, with 64 showing live activity, enabling defenders to block malicious infrastructure before deployment.

results.name: Fake Claude Code extension in Cursor: How to find the backdoor
results.description: On October 29, 2026, Cursor's VS Code extension marketplace served malicious Claude Code extensions (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) designed to plant SSH backdoors on developer machines. The fake extensions, not developed by Anthropic, operated for approximately 11 hours before removal. They installed attacker SSH keys, established reverse SSH tunnels to 134.209.82[.]225, and created persistence mechanisms disguised as legitimate system components. Expel investigated four incidents involving Mac computers, discovering that malicious activity occurred up to 8 hours after Cursor's stated exposure window closed. The backdoor survives extension uninstallation and requires separate removal. The attack collected system information including hostname, username, Git email, and environment variable names. Organizations relying solely on the 11-hour exposure window for scoping may miss compromised machines.

results.name: Black October for AI Developer Platforms
results.description: Throughout October 2026, at least nine AI Developer Platforms experienced security breaches involving credential theft and subsequent abuse of AI model access. The attacks targeted platforms including Fireworks AI, Andromeda, Zeabur, Lightning AI, OpenCode, Railway, Warp, CommandCode, and Northflank. Attackers exploited various vulnerabilities to access stored environment variables containing AI credentials, then monetized stolen access through LLM broker infrastructure. Follow-on activity included validation sweeps, quota enumeration, and large-scale token abuse resembling resold coding-agent traffic. Two documented cases show approximately 800,000 and 1.7 million unauthorized Bedrock calls respectively, generating over $100,000 in fraudulent usage. Multiple reseller operations were identified, including actors using infrastructure at llm-routing.com and xingjiabiapi.org, selling discounted access to frontier models using stolen credentials.

results.name: From help desk impersonation to AD CS abuse: Investigating ESC1 and ESC8 intrusion paths
results.description: Two human-operated intrusions leveraged Microsoft Teams messages and calls to impersonate IT personnel, socially engineering users into granting remote access through Quick Assist. Threat actors staged portable Python, Bun, or Java runtimes, performed network discovery, and assessed Active Directory Certificate Services for authentication paths. The incidents diverged at the certificate layer: one exploited an ESC1-vulnerable certificate template to obtain authentication certificates for privileged accounts and performed DCSync operations, while the other used PetitPotam to coerce domain-controller authentication and relayed it to AD CS Web Enrollment through ESC8, obtaining a domain-controller certificate for Kerberos authentication. Automated attack disruption limited progression in the first case except for an excluded privileged identity that enabled data exfiltration, while customer-led device isolation stopped progression in the second case following Defender alerts.

results.name: PHP2Shell One Week Later: Honeypot Shells on the Web, a Path to Root on Palo Alto Firewalls
results.description: PHP2Shell emerged from two critical PHP memory-safety vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, rated CVSS 9.2 and patched on October 21, 2026. Investigation of open directories uncovered 616 PHP2Shell-related files revealing widespread exploit development across multiple operators. While exploitation succeeded only on honeypots operated by watchTowr, 0x4D31, and GreyNoise for the open internet, the vulnerability has been successfully weaponized against Palo Alto PAN-OS firewalls. Attackers chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-46300) to obtain root access on 25 PAN-OS firewalls.
