The attacker demonstrated sophisticated capabilities including custom tool development possibly leveraging large language models, privilege escalation attempts, and systematic data exfiltration using PowerShell-based collection and staging techniques.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: TRUST#GRAFT : JavaScript-Compromised Sites Target WordPress Admin Browsers to Deploy a Persistent PHP Backdoor
results.description: TRUST#GRAFT is a sophisticated attack chain that exploits authenticated WordPress administrator browser sessions to deploy persistent PHP backdoors. The attack begins with JavaScript loaders that present fake Cloudflare-style verification screens while performing browser fingerprinting, credential harvesting from browser storage, and environment profiling. The critical pivot occurs when the script detects an active WordPress administrator session, automatically extracting CSRF tokens and uploading a malicious plugin disguised as 'Web Media Optimizer.' The PHP backdoor establishes persistence by copying itself to the must-use plugins directory, injects remote JavaScript into public pages, provides token-gated administrator access, and conceals itself from standard plugin management interfaces. The chain demonstrates coordinated infrastructure across multiple domains and requires no authentication bypass, instead leveraging existing trusted browser sessions to convert legitimate administrator workflows into ...

results.name: New BlackX UEFI bootkit exploiting Baton Drop
results.description: In early 2026, a sophisticated APT campaign targeting diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan deployed BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to the notorious BlackLotus. The bootkit exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to bypass Secure Boot and install malicious drivers into the Windows kernel. Despite patches being available since 2023, victims remained vulnerable because the mitigation requires manual activation by administrators. The campaign deploys cyberespionage payloads including a RAT using cloud storage for command and control, and OxiDLLRunner, a Rust-based payload. The attack demonstrates APT actors borrowing techniques from cybercrime operations, as BlackX appears to be reverse-engineered from BlackLotus code. Attribution points to APT41 based on code similarities and tactics matching previous campaigns.

results.name: LiteLLM PyPI Package and Docker Images Compromised to Steal Cloud and AI Credentials
results.description: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised through a supply chain attack affecting both PyPI packages and Docker images. The malicious release contains Python startup files that automatically execute upon Python initialization, stealing cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, and AI development tool authentication. Socket's AI scanner detected the compromise seven minutes after publication. Container build provenance reveals the attack used a lookalike repository (Berri-AI/litellm instead of BerriAI/litellm) in the release workflow. The payload targets AWS, Azure, Google Cloud credentials, GitHub CLI, SSH keys, npm/PyPI configuration, and AI tool credentials including Claude, Gemini, and Cursor. Stolen data is encrypted and exfiltrated to a command-and-control server. A separate loader mechanism enables remote Python code execution. The package receives approximately 23 million weekly downloads, making the impact significant.

results.name: The Science of Exploitability: Decoding BlueHammer
results.description: BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) is an eight-stage local privilege-escalation chain targeting Windows Defender Antimalware Platform before version 4.18.26030.3011. It requires initial code execution as a standard user and chains CloudFilter callbacks, batch oplocks, object-manager symlinks, Defender's update RPC, offline SAM parsing, and SAMR operations to achieve NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM access. The exploit leverages legitimate Windows mechanisms rather than memory corruption, freezing MsMpEng.exe through CloudFilter manipulation while staging malicious update files. In laboratory testing, it successfully escalated privileges, recovered domain-admin credentials from LSASS, and enabled lateral movement via pass-the-hash to compromise domain controllers. Runtime factors including pending signature updates, WinDefend state, filter drivers, VSS, and CloudFilter reachability determine actual exploitability beyond version-based detection.

results.name: The Tale of Two INC Ransom Notes: A Ransomware Timeline
results.description: In late August, an organization was compromised by INC ransomware across at least 175 endpoints. The attack timeline spanned from early to late August with a 17-day gap, suggesting involvement of an initial access broker and a separate ransomware affiliate. Early August activity included scheduled tasks with randomized names and lateral movement via RDP using a compromised account. After the lull, attackers deployed AnyDesk for remote access, used Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver tactics to disable security controls, and executed ransomware via Impacket tools. Uniquely, two ransom notes were discovered: the standard INC-README.txt and a subsequent DATALEAK_PRESS_RELEASE.txt containing detailed stolen file listings, threatening to contact media, employees, and partners within 48 hours to increase pressure on victims.

results.name: LiteLLM supply chain compromise
results.description: On October 21, 2026, attackers compromised litellm version 1.107.0, a popular Python proxy library for LLM providers with approximately 23 million weekly downloads. The malicious release was available on PyPI and official Docker images for about two hours. Attackers used stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens from three engineers to launch a private release workflow against a malicious fork. The payload installed a credential stealer targeting cloud, developer, AI-tool, browser and LiteLLM proxy credentials, plus a second-stage remote access trojan backdoor. The malware executes automatically whenever Python starts through dropped files in the site-packages directory. This represents the second supply chain compromise of LiteLLM in 2026, with no established connection to the previous incident linked to TeamPCP activity.

results.name: North Korea's Hangro Revisited
results.description: A deep technical analysis reveals updates to Hangro, North Korea's state VPN and mail product, operating on servers in Pyongyang and the Russian Far East. A new certificate hierarchy deployed in July 2026 differs significantly from the 2024 version, with both containing cryptographic anomalies where signatures fail verification. Investigation uncovered six network assignments in Chinese address space linked to a single registry contact associated with Silibank, plus infrastructure in Russian Far East networks designated KPOST. The service evolved from a commercial email gateway in 2001 to a certificate-bound VPN deployment issued to trade representatives through consulates. Technical evidence indicates structured infrastructure spanning North Korean, Russian, and Chinese address space, with mail systems configured for bulk transfers over intermittent connections using ten gigabyte message limits and ETRN capabilities.

results.name: PAYLOAD ransomware attacks through Active Directory GPO
results.description: In April 2026, a manufacturing organization in the Middle East suffered a ransomware attack where threat actors with domain admin privileges weaponized Active Directory Group Policy Objects to achieve domain-wide impact without deploying ransomware binaries on Windows endpoints. The attackers created malicious GPOs linked at the domain root, delivering ransom notes, hijacking wallpapers and lock screens, enforcing logon banners, and disabling local administrator accounts across all domain-joined workstations. No file encryption occurred on Windows systems; instead, the operation focused on encryptionless extortion through operational disruption and data exfiltration. Initial access was gained via compromised VPN credentials. The attack remained dormant for one day between GPO creation and detonation, evading file-based detection entirely by abusing trusted AD infrastructure.

results.name: Don't Call Us, We'll Call Your APIs | TraderTraitor Backdoors Resurface on Victim With No Crypto Ties
results.description: In 2026, the DPRK-sponsored Lazarus subgroup TraderTraitor continued campaigns targeting cryptocurrency entities, including a high-profile attack on LayerZero resulting in $292 million theft from KelpDAO. Following this disclosure, an additional victim was identified: a smaller IT services provider in India with no cryptocurrency connections. The compromise involved a DevOps engineer targeted through fake job interview lures containing weaponized Terraform coding projects. Malicious GitHub repositories used typosquatted provider domains to deliver macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK when victims executed terraform init. The backdoors enabled reconnaissance, credential theft, and cloud environment escalation. One day after LayerZero's public disclosure, attackers deployed an updated stripped version of ROOFDECK and removed earlier implants. Activity continued until June 2026, suggesting the threat actor ultimately abandoned the intrusion after determining insufficient value from the smaller target.

results.name: Midnight Mimosa Malware Campaign Exploits Android Firmware Supply Chain
results.description: Midnight Mimosa is a widespread Android malware campaign involving malicious applications preinstalled in firmware of low-cost MediaTek-based devices, with infections observed across more than 150 countries. The campaign leverages platform-signed system applications to silently deploy payloads, evade mobile security protections, execute remotely supplied code, and monetize compromised devices through advertising fraud and residential-proxy services. The malicious firmware components provide persistent system-level access before device activation, bypass conventional Android security controls by temporarily disabling Google Play Store protections, and maintain privileged positions while operators rotate payloads remotely. Affected devices include low-cost Android handsets, counterfeit flagship models, and devices associated with Doogee and Cubot products, with highest concentrations reported in Mexico, France, and Italy.

results.name: Inside Wazza: A Newly Observed Device Code Phishing Kit Targeting Microsoft 365 Accounts
results.description: A newly observed multi-stage phishing kit named Wazza has been actively targeting Microsoft 365 accounts since early July 2026. The campaign delivers phishing emails from compromised accounts containing PDF lures with business themes like invoices and contracts. These PDFs redirect victims through a complex infrastructure leveraging Google Sites, CloudFlare Workers, and various domains. Wazza features dynamic capabilities including 19 different phishing themes impersonating services like Adobe, DocuSign, and OneDrive, along with six corporate decoy websites. The kit employs sophisticated browser interrogation, anti-automation checks, and client-side protection mechanisms. The final stage abuses Microsoft OAuth device authorization, displaying a verification code and instructing victims to complete authentication on a separate page. Throughout the process, a backend session continuously monitors the authentication attempt, ultimately granting attackers access to victim accounts and cloud resources.

results.name: Dissection of Operation FlashHole, a complex attack by Lazarus
results.description: In January, Lazarus Group launched Operation FlashHole against South Korea, exploiting mandatory security software CrossWeb EX through watering hole strategies and targeted spear-phishing emails with fake portfolio and resume sites. The campaign began in July the previous year, targeting software, construction, and cable equipment manufacturing sectors. The attack chain combines old and new malware families including TechHub, Cubridge, TouchShift, TouchHub, ClientHub, and LPEClient. Notable techniques include in-memory execution, GitHub and Dropbox for command-and-control infrastructure, DLL side-loading, and the incorporation of post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-1024) and GOST encryption. The sophisticated modular framework demonstrates Lazarus's continuous evolution of tools and tactics specifically designed for South Korean targets.

results.name: Swallowtail: Russian Espionage Group Targets Defense Firms in Two NATO Countries
results.description: Russian espionage group Swallowtail targeted organizations across two NATO member states, including a law enforcement agency, naval shipbuilder, and military aircraft engine manufacturer. During a two-month intrusion at the naval shipbuilder, attackers deployed the Hookedge backdoor delivered through malicious Word documents. They conducted hands-on-keyboard operations, stealing credentials through two distinct techniques: deploying an SSH private key to establish a persistent tunnel into the internal network, and using a PowerShell script to capture NTLM handshakes. The attackers also deployed a previously undocumented reflective loader (ld.exe) that decrypts payloads in memory using runtime-supplied keys. All targets hold information of direct interest to foreign intelligence, consistent with a broad collection effort against European government and defense sectors.

results.name: CVE-2026-102764: Critical BeyondTrust Remote Support Authentication Bypass Exploited in the Wild
results.description: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support platform allows unauthenticated remote attackers to perform file operations without user interaction. Versions 26.2.3 and earlier are affected. BeyondTrust confirmed exploitation in the wild with two compromises dating to August 29, 2026, affecting one hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance. Mandiant investigation revealed arbitrary file uploads, deployment of SAWFLY web shell and BARECLAW tunneler, root escalation, credential-vault extraction attempts, persistence mechanisms, and log deletion. The activity is attributed to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor. CISA added this vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list on October 16, 2026. Organizations must apply emergency patches and investigate for compromise, as patching does not remove persistence.

results.name: AOMEI Backupper update servers hijacked to push malware: Check your PC
results.description: Between April and July 2026, attackers compromised AOMEI Technology's update and notification infrastructure to distribute malware to users of AOMEI Backupper, backup software used by over 100 million people worldwide. During three confirmed tampering windows lasting ten, six, and five minutes, attackers modified download instructions to deliver a malicious ZIP archive containing an initial downloader that installed a persistent remote-access backdoor. The compromised infrastructure also serves AnyViewer customers. The brief tampering periods made detection difficult while limiting infection opportunities. The backdoor enables attackers to execute commands and install additional malware, leaving infected systems vulnerable to further compromise. Users can check for infection by scanning with security software, examining Task Scheduler for RadminComponentRuntime tasks, searching for unsigned upgrade-now.exe files, or monitoring suspicious network traffic to specific domains and IP addresses.

results.name: QuartzLine: A working PDF viewer with a backdoor inside
results.description: QuartzLine, also tracked as CLOUDHAZE by Mandiant, is malicious software disguised as a functional Windows PDF viewer that conceals a backdoor enabling attackers to execute commands and deploy additional malware. The malware has appeared as paperline.exe and fielddesk.exe, signed with a legitimate but now-revoked EV code-signing certificate. Distribution occurs through malicious advertising, where users searching for unrelated content click ads and download the viewer from AWS S3 buckets. Once installed, QuartzLine establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and communicates with command-and-control infrastructure. Observed attack chains include Chrome data theft within one week of installation, followed by deployment of second-stage RATs like Caira and IronBark. The backdoor operates with user-level privileges and can execute arbitrary Windows commands.

results.name: An Analysis of Suo5-Based Tunneling and Pivoting Attack Techniques Through Case Studies
results.description: This analysis examines exploitation of Suo5, an HTTP/HTTPS-based tunneling tool, for pivoting attacks through compromised web servers to access internal networks. Suo5 relays TCP traffic and enables SOCKS5 proxy access to internal systems, supporting multiple transmission modes and environments including Java, PHP, IIS/.NET, and Nginx. Two deployment methods were observed: file upload exploitation on IIS servers through renamed ASPX files, and memory injection via Jenkins Script Console using Groovy scripts to register Suo5 as Servlet and Filter components. Key indicators include repeated POST requests in web logs, DLL files in Temporary ASP.NET Files directories, and PluginServletFilter chains in Java logs. Detection strategies recommend monitoring web request patterns, server-side behaviors, abnormal User-Agent headers, unauthorized URI access, and file modifications in web application paths, alongside restricting script execution capabilities and implementing network segmentation controls.

results.name: ChainScript: Tracing a Node.js RAT Through the Blockchain
results.description: Blackpoint's Adversary Pursuit Group identified ChainScript, a previously unnamed Node.js remote access trojan discovered during ClickFix investigation. The malware disguises itself as legitimate software including Spotify, Zoom Workplace, and Microsoft Teams through malicious Windows Installer packages. ChainScript employs an EtherHiding-style C2 discovery technique utilizing a Polygon smart contract to dynamically locate active WebSocket infrastructure, enabling operators to rotate backend services without rebuilding agents. The RAT provides comprehensive remote access capabilities including interactive shell sessions, file operations, screenshots, payload deployment, cryptocurrency wallet discovery, remote JavaScript execution, self-update mechanisms, and cleanup functions. Multiple builds appeared under different names (ComponentTask33, UpdateDigital, HostShared, OrchidViolet66) while maintaining consistent core agent architecture. Analysis revealed automated contract deployment integrated into the mal...

results.name: Lazarus luring employees with trojanized coding challenges: The case of a Spanish aerospace company
results.description: ESET researchers uncovered a Lazarus attack against a Spanish aerospace company where attackers masqueraded as Meta recruiters on LinkedIn, sending trojanized coding challenges to employees. The campaign deployed multiple tools including LightlessCan, a previously undocumented backdoor that mimics native Windows commands to evade detection. Initial access was achieved through spearphishing via LinkedIn Messaging, delivering malicious executables disguised as C++ programming tests. The attack chain involved DLL side-loading techniques delivering payloads including NickelLoader downloader, miniBlindingCan variant, and the sophisticated LightlessCan RAT supporting 68 commands. LightlessCan represents a significant advancement over its predecessor BlindingCan, implementing execution guardrails and enhanced stealth capabilities. The campaign targeted aerospace technology and know-how for cyberespionage purposes, consistent with North Korean strategic objectives in missile development.

results.name: WeaselBiscuit Strips BeaverTail and OtterCookie Down to Essentials
results.description: A new JavaScript infostealer dubbed WeaselBiscuit has been discovered hidden in 11 malicious npm packages. This lean malware shares operational similarities with DPRK-linked BeaverTail and OtterCookie families but features a stripped-down architecture. WeaselBiscuit deploys through npm imports, executes a detached Node process, retrieves its payload from Npoint URLs, and communicates with a C2 server at 103.170.217.184:8787. The malware profiles infected hosts, steals Chrome extension storage containing wallet signing states, captures clipboard contents, and logs Windows keystrokes when commanded. Unlike its predecessors, it lacks wallet-draining code, browser password decryption, Python second stages, screenshots, and remote shell capabilities. The operation uses numeric campaign identifiers embedded in package names for tracking. While technical overlap suggests DPRK attribution, particularly through Npoint dead-drop patterns and nested IP geolocation lookups, definitive attribution requires additional c...

results.name: PolinRider Spreads Through Compromised GitHub Accounts and Packagist
results.description: PolinRider operators compromised a GitHub account to insert malicious code into development versions of visanduma/nova-two-factor, a Packagist package with over 700,000 downloads. The campaign spreads through compromised developer accounts and Git repositories across multiple ecosystems including npm, PyPI, Go modules, Packagist, and Chrome extensions. The operators use Git history rewriting, payload concealment in configuration files and font files, automatic execution through IDE tasks, and staged payload delivery via dead-drop mechanisms like EtherHiding and NullReceiver. Primary infection occurs through Git-based collaboration rather than direct package registry compromise, with PHP projects targeted using obfuscated JavaScript executed through shell_exec. The campaign appears linked to North Korean operators focused on cryptocurrency theft.

results.name: LabubaRAT Threat Snapshot
results.description: LabubaRAT is a custom, unsigned 64-bit Rust-based remote access trojan identified by Blackpoint, designed to masquerade as legitimate NVIDIA software. It provides comprehensive remote access capabilities including command execution, file operations, screen capture, and SOCKS5 proxying. The malware features configurable enrollment fields and an internal ZM_ configuration namespace, suggesting it is built on a reusable, multi-tenant framework consistent with a malware-as-a-service offering. LabubaRAT is managed through an associated backend infrastructure called LabubaPanel, hosted on German providers. The delivery mechanism utilized the RAT's own JavaScript execution capability. First observed in July 2026, it targets Windows platforms and employs various evasion techniques including masquerading as NVIDIA components and abusing legitimate Microsoft build utilities.

results.name: The Odyssey and trojans again: MovieReaper attacks users in multiple countries via compromised torrents
results.description: A previously unknown modular multi-stage framework named MovieReaper has been discovered targeting users through compromised torrent files. Attackers compromised the public torrent repository itorrents[.]org, enabling them to distribute malicious loaders disguised as popular movies, including "The Odyssey." The campaign began in mid-August 2026 and affected hundreds of victims across multiple countries. The malware employs a sophisticated infection chain with fileless execution, utilizing blockchain network Solana for C2 infrastructure resilience. The framework includes multiple stages: an initial loader with anti-sandbox checks, shellcode that retrieves C2 addresses from Solana blockchain, UAC bypass with persistence mechanisms, and a final file manager module providing comprehensive file system access. The campaign demonstrates advanced evasion techniques including manual API resolution, vectored exception handling, and in-memory execution.

results.name: Beware the SparroWock: The backdoor that bites, the commands that catch
results.description: ESET researchers have documented SparroWocky, a sophisticated C++ backdoor deployed by the FamousSparrow APT group since August 2025. This China-aligned threat actor has shifted focus to extensively targeting governmental organizations across Latin America, likely in response to increased US interest in the region. SparroWocky replaced the group's previous SparrowDoor backdoor and demonstrates advanced capabilities including reflective loading, anti-analysis techniques like SilentMoonwalk for call stack spoofing, and the ability to execute Beacon Object Files. The modular backdoor incorporates open-source projects directly into its codebase, uses TLS-encrypted communications with RC4 encryption for data exfiltration, and employs sophisticated evasion methods including MinHook API hooking and custom PE loading with host process camouflage. The targeting pattern reflects China's strategic interest in monitoring Latin American governmental responses to current US pressures regarding investments and infrastruc...

results.name: Ready, Settra, Go: New Settra Ransomware Variant Deploys MeshAgent RMM
results.description: Settra is a ransomware variant first observed in June 2026 that targets organizations through VPNs or compromised credentials. Two incidents were investigated in July and September 2026, affecting the consumer services, retail, and manufacturing sectors. Attackers deployed MeshAgent RMM for persistence, naming ransomware executables after victim domain names. The malicious activity included file encryption with .locked or .locked_wip extensions, deployment of RESTORE_FILES.txt ransom notes, clearing Windows event logs, and disabling Windows recovery options using reagentc and diskpart utilities. One incident featured Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) tactics using gdrv.sys. A notable operational security failure occurred when attackers misspelled the Windows Defender Event Log path, preventing its deletion. Both attacks followed remarkably similar operational patterns, with MeshAgent installations pointing to different C2 IP addresses (45.13.122[.]7 and 193.5.65[.]114), and malicious workstation WIN...

results.name: VectraRAT: An Undocumented Full-Stack MaaS Built From Scratch
results.description: VectraRAT is a previously undocumented Malware-as-a-Service platform combining a Go-based control server (VectraHub) with a native C++ Windows implant, renting from $250 monthly. The developer, operating under the handle 'Vectra' (formerly 'Nyxel'), has been active since August 2022 without prior public documentation. The platform offers hidden desktop control, keylogging, clipboard hijacking with cryptocurrency address replacement, browser credential theft, and a UAC bypass achieving elevation without user prompts. Delivered through Amadey loader and ClickFix campaigns targeting tax-themed lures, 48% of observed victims run corporate Windows editions including Windows Server 2025. Infrastructure analysis revealed exposed directories and operational panels across multiple hosting providers, with victims spanning the United States, Russia, Germany, and other nations.

results.name: SilkParasite Infrastructure: SpiceRAT Servers Tied to Energy and Government Targets Across Central Asia
results.description: Infrastructure analysis reveals a cluster of SpiceRAT command and control servers active from late 2025 through August 2026, linked through shared TLS certificates, domain registrations, and a cloned RTX Corporation webpage. The infrastructure connects to multiple threat families including SpiceRAT, NodeEdgeRAT, NomadRAT, and BloodAlchemy, suggesting either a single operator managing multiple toolsets or shared support infrastructure. A TLS certificate impersonating Uzbekistan's railway authority was issued by TLC, a Chinese state-affiliated certificate authority. Domains spoof Central Asian government entities including Türkmengaz, the Galkynysh gas field, Tojiktelecom, and Turkmenistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Passive DNS analysis reveals subdomain infrastructure dating to mid-2022, indicating at least four years of ongoing operations. The infrastructure shares characteristics with previously documented China-nexus actors FamousSparrow and IndigoZebra, both known for targeting Central Asian governm...

results.name: Noodle RAT: A Recipe for Cross Platform Espionage
results.description: Noodle RAT, also known as ANGRYREBEL or Nood RAT, is a modular remote access trojan with dual versions for Windows and Linux, actively used by Chinese-speaking threat actors since at least mid-2016. Previously misclassified as variants of Gh0st RAT or Rekoobe, it is now recognized as a distinct backdoor family. The malware has been deployed in espionage and cybercrime campaigns targeting entities across the Asia-Pacific region, including Thailand, India, Japan, Malaysia, and Taiwan. Multiple threat groups including Iron Tiger, Calypso APT, Rocke, and Cloud Snooper have utilized this tool. Both variants feature shared command-and-control architecture, similar configuration structures, and modular capabilities. The Windows version operates as an in-memory backdoor with file management and proxy capabilities, while the Linux variant provides reverse shell, SOCKS tunneling, and task scheduling functionalities. Evidence suggests an actively maintained, possibly commercial malware toolkit.
results.adversary: Iron Tiger, Calypso APT, Rocke, Cloud Snooper

results.name: How Money Laundering, Scams, and Espionage Hide in a Web Full of Casino Garbage
results.description: Illegal online gambling infrastructure spans three distinct cybercrime categories that defenders often overlook. First, over 1.7 million Chinese-language casino domains facilitate illegal gambling and transnational money laundering, primarily operated by triad-aligned syndicates. Second, thousands of "scambling" websites target global audiences with rigged games and withdrawal fraud, using deposit bonuses to lure victims. Third, China-aligned APT groups deploy the PeckBirdy malware framework within fake casino and adult websites as command-and-control infrastructure, targeting education, government, finance and technology sectors across Asia. These operations exploit U.S. and European hosting providers through infrastructure laundering while maintaining bulletproof Asian hosting. The campaigns have escalated sharply since 2023, with PeckBirdy domains achieving zero detection rates on VirusTotal. All three types appear visually identical, creating detection challenges for security teams.

results.name: The banana stand: brokering and managing infections across Asia using MQTT
results.description: BambooToken is an emerging multiplatform malware family active since at least February 2023, utilizing the Message Queueing and Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol for covert command and control operations. The campaign targets Windows and Linux systems across Asia and South America, with infections observed on backend servers for mobile applications, legal and financial services, software companies, hotels, and GitLab instances. The malware leverages sideloading techniques through Tendyron's OnKey authentication software, commonly used in Chinese banking and government networks. Analysis reveals extensive host enumeration capabilities, plugins for antivirus detection, and potential keylogging and clipboard theft functions. Infrastructure analysis shows C2 domains ranking in Cloudflare's top 500,000, indicating widespread infections. The actor demonstrates sophisticated operational security, using MQTT's publish-subscribe architecture to hide infrastructure and employing Cloudflare proxies for additional o...

results.name: Fake MP4 File Carries Malicious Payload
results.description: A sophisticated infection chain leverages PowerShell loaders to deliver encrypted NetSupport client payloads concealed within fake MP4 files. The malicious MP4 containers appear valid to basic file-type checks but contain 6.5 MB of encrypted data in ISO Base Media File Format uuid extension boxes rather than playable video content. The attack begins with PowerShell delivered via Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure, performing environment checks before retrieving the carrier file. A secondary script parses the MP4 structure, extracts and decrypts an embedded 16.8 MB PowerShell payload, then deploys NetSupport Manager with silent operation configured. Infrastructure spans 40 live endpoints across six autonomous systems, primarily in Frankfurt and Los Angeles, with command-and-control gateways registered 77 seconds apart. The toolkit employs Russian-language business site decoys and rotates carriers frequently without backward compatibility.

results.name: skynox7: Proxyjacking Edge Devices Into Residential Proxies
results.description: A malicious cyber actor conducted a proxyjacking campaign, compromising at least 143 network edge devices across 34 countries to force them into residential proxy networks. The attacker exploited vulnerabilities in D-Link ShareCenter NAS devices, Ubiquiti UniFi Video NVR systems, and SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer, also targeting DVR/NVR devices from Hikvision and Dahua. The compromised devices were installed with Pawns.app software without owners' consent, monetizing victim bandwidth through IPRoyal's residential proxy network. The attacker configured SSH key authentication as a persistent access method. This activity was discovered when an organization identified suspicious authentication patterns showing multiple users logging in from the same residential proxy IP address, leading to confirmation of a serious intrusion.

results.name: Variola: From ClickFix to a Modular Implant
results.description: Blackpoint's Adversary Pursuit Group traced a ClickFix intrusion to a previously unclassified modular Windows implant designated Variola. The malware establishes persistent host identity through encrypted storage, maintains configuration and controller information across executions, and employs authenticated command-and-control with controller rotation capabilities. Variola's modular architecture enables operators to dynamically load additional components for credential theft, browser manipulation, and session hijacking. The framework demonstrates capabilities typical of banking trojans, including Chromium browser process injection, live cookie database access, and VNC-style remote access. Multiple related builds discovered in the same GitHub repository suggest active development and experimentation. The implant uses XSalsa20 encryption, secp256k1 key exchange, and Ed25519 signatures for secure communications. Its ability to preserve context, migrate between processes, and expand capabilities on demand tra...

results.name: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits BeyondTrust
results.description: On October 15, BeyondTrust disclosed CVE-2026-102764, a vulnerability affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances that enables arbitrary file upload. Mandiant identified ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor, exploiting this as a zero-day in late August 2026. Following exploitation, the actor deployed SAWFLY webshell and BARECLAW tunneler, escalated privileges using SUID bit manipulation, harvested credentials from the BeyondTrust vault, and established persistent access by modifying sudoers templates and HAProxy configurations. The actor demonstrated deep knowledge of BeyondTrust internals, abusing proprietary CLI utilities and reverse-proxy routing. They systematically deleted logs to evade detection and leveraged compromised administrator credentials to pivot laterally and exfiltrate sensitive documents. Organizations face potential widespread exploitation as ARMORY CASTLE historically conducts opportunistic campaigns following vulnerability disclosure. Immediate patching and comprehe...

results.name: Aoki: Infostealer Targets AI Coding Assistant Credentials
results.description: The Aoki infostealer has evolved to target credentials from AI coding assistants including Claude, OpenAI's Codex, Cursor, Codeium and Gemini. This capability represents a recent addition, as earlier versions did not target AI-related files. The malware steals API keys, tokens and session files that could enable attackers to conduct activities under legitimate user identities, access connected repositories, cloud services and CI/CD pipelines. Beyond AI credentials, Aoki harvests data from dozens of browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, password managers, messaging applications, gaming platforms, VPN and FTP clients. The malware collects available data and transmits it to command-and-control servers. This development suggests AI credentials are becoming as valuable as traditional targets like payment card data and cryptocurrency wallets for cybercriminals.

results.name: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware
results.description: This investigation reveals the first public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted advertisements, termed AdFection. Devices at Al Jazeera were infected with Candiru spyware through malicious ads purchased by Israeli company Discover-Tech, which operates as a facilitator for mercenary spyware partners. Discover-Tech's Controlium platform enables partners to de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices when advertisements render. Analysis of four billion bidding records shows ads were displayed across nearly 200,000 websites and apps in dozens of countries. The company appeared on Google and IAB Europe vendor lists from 2020-2026, serving ads via major networks. Discover-Tech is linked to multiple mercenary surveillance actors including Candiru, Intelos, and Bindecy, and supports mass-deanonymization through mobile carrier vulnerability exploitation. The infrastructure also covertly directed millions of devices to contact Candiru servers for tracking and reconnais...

results.name: Fake Calendly "Meta Careers" pages steal Facebook and Google logins
results.description: A wave of fraudulent websites mimicking Calendly booking pages for Meta job interviews has been identified, targeting job seekers to steal credentials. Victims select interview time slots, provide personal information, and complete fake CAPTCHA verifications before being prompted to log into Facebook and Google accounts. The sophisticated phishing kit captures login credentials and bypasses two-factor authentication by relaying authentication codes in real-time to attackers. The pages use convincing replicas of legitimate login screens with fake address bars displaying authentic URLs. Eleven domains following similar naming patterns have been identified, utilizing generic recruiting-related terms. The collection infrastructure operates through Amazon API Gateway in Singapore, with code comments in Vietnamese suggesting the operation's possible origins.

results.name: Disruption Targets Major Chinese-Language Phishing Kits with Japanese Focus
results.description: A coordinated disruption action targeted Chinese-speaking cybercriminals operating three major phishing kits: CoGUI, CoAceV, and CoFish_Ws, which collectively distributed hundreds of millions of credential phishing messages primarily targeting Japanese organizations. These operations impersonated 66 well-known brands, mainly consumer and finance companies, to steal usernames, passwords, and payment data. The threat actors demonstrated sophisticated capabilities, utilizing approximately 17,000 unique domains with frequent rotation and evasion techniques. The ecosystem enablers YAM Store and Iron Man were also targeted through a civil lawsuit and domain seizures, conducted in collaboration between Microsoft, Health-ISAC, and multiple security partners. This coordinated action is expected to significantly impact the Chinese phishing ecosystem and cause substantial operational disruption to multiple threat groups conducting financial fraud.

results.name: Iron Man & YamStore: Powering a Global Phishing-as-a-Service Ecosystem
results.description: Resecurity identified and mapped infrastructure supporting a commercial Phishing-as-a-Service operation marketed as 'Iron Man System.' The kit is sold to criminal buyers as a self-hosted package deploying pre-built lure pages impersonating postal services, banks, government agencies, and other trusted entities. Through infiltration of Chinese threat actor communities and acquisition of a license, Resecurity traced the back-end infrastructure and found 2,360 phishing templates targeting 130 countries. The operation features a self-hosted build registry with 911 published versions, bilingual Chinese-English interface, and subscription-based licensing tied to vendor-controlled authorization servers. Working with Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit and industry partners, the cybercriminal infrastructure was mapped and disrupted. The kit captured approximately 17.4GB of telemetry data targeting 75,000 organizations through an estimated 1 billion phishing emails.

results.name: Thai Broadband Provider Targeted via FortiGate SSL-VPN and MeshCentral Persistence
results.description: An exposed directory on a Thai server revealed an active intrusion campaign targeting 3BB (Triple T Broadband), one of Thailand's largest broadband providers. The attacker exploited CVE-2024-21762 in a FortiGate 60F SSL-VPN appliance to gain initial access, then deployed MeshCentral remote management software for persistent command-and-control. The operation involved extensive reconnaissance, credential harvesting targeting RADIUS authentication databases, privilege escalation using PwnKit and Dirty COW exploits, lateral movement via SSH brute-forcing across 55+ internal hosts, and anti-forensic cleanup procedures. Multiple devices were already enrolled under attacker control at discovery, with additional targeting of Jasmine International infrastructure. The attacker's toolkit included web application exploitation scripts, database credential extraction tools, and persistence mechanisms designed to maintain long-term access to subscriber authentication systems.

results.name: Case of AgentTesla Malware Distribution Disguised as a Business Proposal Email
results.description: A phishing campaign has been observed distributing AgentTesla infostealer through emails masquerading as business proposal requests. Recipients are asked to review an attached product list, but the ZIP file contains an executable file instead of a document. The malicious EXE disguises itself as a café management program using Chinese-language descriptions and UI elements. Through multiple stages of obfuscation, the malware extracts encrypted data from bitmap resources, performs XOR decryption, and loads successive .NET payloads into memory. The final payload is AgentTesla, which steals credentials, cookies, and contact information from browsers, email clients, FTP and VPN applications. Stolen data is exfiltrated via FTP to a compromised server. The attack demonstrates sophisticated multi-stage loading techniques and social engineering tactics targeting business users.

results.name: RSVP to Disaster: How One Click Installs a RAT
results.description: Cybercriminals are exploiting digital event invitations to distribute remote access trojans. Victims receive legitimate-looking emails with generic subject lines about special gatherings and celebrations. The messages contain download buttons that redirect users through fake CAPTCHA verification pages hosted on recently created domains. After verification, users encounter another generic invitation page prompting them to download an eInvite file. This delivers a zipped folder containing ScreenConnect.exe, a legitimate ConnectWise Screen Connect installer weaponized as a RAT. Once executed, attackers gain full remote access to compromised devices through an unassuming taskbar icon that reveals an active connection. The campaign leverages user curiosity rather than sophisticated techniques, making it particularly effective during holiday seasons when event invitations are common.

results.name: Clean Install, Stolen Creds: Fake WatchGuard VPN Site Serves Genuine Signed Client
results.description: In early October, a sophisticated credential phishing campaign targeted WatchGuard Mobile VPN users through a fake download site at watchguard-vpn[.]net. The attack used SEO poisoning to appear in search results and deployed a unique technique: after collecting victim credentials twice through browser pop-ups, it downloaded the genuine, validly signed WatchGuard installer directly from WatchGuard's official CDN. This eliminated malicious files that security tools could detect. The first credential submission was deliberately rejected as incorrect to collect multiple passwords. The credential collection endpoint at watchguard-ssl[.]online received server addresses, usernames, and passwords, providing attackers network access. This domain was previously reported in January with no backend functionality but was re-registered in August with full phishing capabilities implemented by September.

results.name: The phone was compromised before the user turned it on: the rise of Midnight Mimosa
results.description: A sophisticated malware campaign targets low-cost Android devices built on MediaTek platforms, with malicious code preinstalled in device firmware before users receive them. The platform-signed system application operates with elevated privileges, enabling operators to silently install applications, grant permissions, and load remote code. The scheme primarily generates revenue through ad fraud, click fraud, device information collection, and converting infected devices into residential-proxy botnet nodes. The malicious system application ships under various system-sounding names including com.android.system.lite, com.android.sys.prot, and com.android.sys.gmsprot. Operators deploy at least 32 disguised applications including fake weather, app-lock, and OCR tools. The malware disables Google Play Store during payload installation to evade detection, then re-enables it afterward. Thirteen related applications were also discovered on Google Play, communicating with identical command-and-control infrastructure...

results.name: Inside a brand deal scam targeting YouTube creators
results.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign targets YouTube content creators through personalized sponsorship emails impersonating legitimate brands like Hollyland, Nike, and Spotify. Attackers send customized collaboration offers referencing specific videos from targets' channels, then direct them to fraudulent platforms that appear legitimate with campaign metrics and income calculators. The scheme culminates in a Google sign-in request that either captures credentials directly or requests excessive account permissions. Once compromised, attackers lock victims out by changing recovery methods and can misuse the account to spread scams to followers. The modular campaign operates globally, targeting creators in Peru, Japan, and English-speaking regions, using multiple domains while maintaining similar functionality and design patterns across variants.

results.name: Threat Overview: NetScaler Zero Days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 Being Exploited in Production Environments (Updated September 30)
results.description: Two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway systems are being actively exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-88771 is a remote code execution vulnerability allowing unauthenticated command injection, while CVE-2026-88772 is a DTLS memory overflow flaw enabling RCE or DoS attacks. Threat actors deployed webshells through these vulnerabilities to establish initial access and persistence. The CVE-2026-88771 exploitation involves a three-stage command injection chain poisoning log files, while CVE-2026-88772 exploitation drops .deb webshell files. Attackers used PHP webshells with RC4 encryption for command and control communications, targeting custom directories within NetScaler Gateway interfaces. Cortex Xpanse identified over 50,000 potentially vulnerable exposed instances.

results.name: DNS as C2 in Noir, An AI-Developed Crypto Wallet Drainer
results.description: A cryptocurrency wallet-drainer kit called Noir uses DNS TXT records and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) as a dynamic command-and-control mechanism. The loader queries public DoH services to discover active infrastructure hosted on Cloudflare Pages, allowing operators to redirect deployed lures by changing a single DNS record. The drainer does not require victims to enter seed phrases or private keys; instead, it requests wallet connection permissions and obtains spending approvals that appear less suspicious than direct transfers. The architecture separates long-lived phishing lures from short-lived operational infrastructure, with 60-second DNS caching and self-healing retry logic. Extensive plain-English code comments suggest AI-assisted development, documenting bugs, fixes, and design decisions. The kit serves as a shared service across multiple cryptocurrency-themed phishing campaigns.

results.name: The Scalpel vs. The Sledgehammer: Lessons in Precision Triage from the .conf26 SOC
results.description: During a live Security Operations Center shift at .conf26 in Denver, analysts investigated Incident ES_00244 involving an exploit link detected by Cisco Secure Firewall. The challenge arose when 15 devices were found communicating with a single IP address (13.226.251.40) flagged for hosting malicious domains moonlighthathel[.]org and ukankingwithea[.]com. Investigation revealed the IP was an Amazon CloudFront CDN node simultaneously serving legitimate services including Samsung Health, Mindtickle learning platform, and Amazon Video. Using AI-assisted analysis, firewall logs, and packet forensics through Endace, analysts isolated one unmanaged Intel laptop generating malicious traffic among 14 benign connections. Instead of blocking the shared IP and disrupting legitimate services, analysts implemented precise DNS object blocks targeting only the malicious domains at the Cisco Firepower Threat Defense perimeter, successfully neutralizing the threat while maintaining normal operations for all other attendees.

results.name: Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Exposes 30,000 Users' OAuth Tokens to Russian Bot Service
results.description: A malicious browser extension called 'Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot' distributed on Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons captures and forwards users' live Twitch OAuth session tokens to Russian-controlled proxy servers. The extension, with approximately 30,000 Chrome users and 552 Firefox users, markets itself as a quality-of-life tool for blocking ads and unlocking streams. While delivering these features, it secretly extracts users' account-scoped OAuth tokens and forwards them as query parameters to operator-controlled infrastructure. Current versions append tokens inline during video playlist redirects, while earlier builds explicitly POSTed tokens to dedicated collection endpoints. The operator is identified as a commercial Russian bot service called JeetBot, with infrastructure hosted across German and cloud providers.

results.name: KATARU: IoT Malware Adopts Public LPE Exploits
results.description: KATARU is an IoT malware variant discovered in August 2026 through Telnet credential brute-forcing against a honeypot from Vietnam. While maintaining traditional Mirai-style botnet capabilities, it distinguishes itself through an extensive feature set including multiple Linux local privilege escalation exploits, comprehensive persistence mechanisms across Linux and embedded platforms, encrypted C2 communications using X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, anti-analysis techniques, and decoy traffic generation. Implementation artifacts strongly suggest AI-assisted development, evidenced by architecture-mismatched x86 shellcode in ARM binaries, RFC test vectors as configuration values, and untested cross-platform persistence logic. The malware attempts various privilege escalation paths through system misconfigurations and public exploits, establishes persistence across numerous startup mechanisms, and supports multiple DDoS attack vectors alongside SSH brute-forcing capabilities.

results.name: Artifactory Under Attack: In-the-Wild Exploitation of CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-42018 & CVE-2026-82329
results.description: Active exploitation of three critical vulnerabilities in JFrog Artifactory has been identified, with attackers chaining CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-42018, and CVE-2026-82329 to bypass authentication and gain administrative control. CVE-2026-42018 exposes internal anonymous-user tokens, CVE-2026-42016 enables privilege escalation through insufficient token validation, and CVE-2026-82329 allows unauthenticated access to administrative privileges. Post-exploitation activities include creating persistent administrator accounts, deploying malicious Groovy plugins for code execution, and installing Rust-based backdoors. Exploitation was observed between August 15 and September 8, 2026, affecting multiple organizations. Data indicates 67-69% of organizations running Artifactory had vulnerable instances at initial publication, with slow patching velocity for lower-severity CVEs despite active exploitation across environments.

results.name: Melofee: a look back at a Linux implant and its new variants
results.description: Three years after its initial discovery, the Melofee Linux implant has evolved with sophisticated new capabilities. The malware now features modularized architecture with hot-loadable components for shell functionality, file management, and command execution. New versions incorporate remote C2 infrastructure reconfiguration and enhanced stealth through a kernel rootkit based on the Reptile project. The implant uses RC4 encryption and supports multiple communication protocols including TCP, HTTP, HTTPS, and TLS. Analysis reveals two infrastructure clusters utilizing fake certificates impersonating Symantec and other entities. Code similarities establish links with Windows-targeting implants including CrowDoor, Hemigate, and RatelS, suggesting tool sharing among multiple Chinese state-linked threat groups. The modular design allows dynamic loading of up to eleven specialized modules via a common plugin interface.

results.name: Casbaneiro: A Banking Trojan with Distributed Data-Receiving Servers
results.description: In August 2026, a Casbaneiro campaign targeted Latin American users through phishing emails and PDFs themed as fake invoices and legal notices. The multi-stage infection chain includes HTA downloaders and AutoIt loaders, employing geofencing to filter victims by IP address location. The malware exhibits sophisticated evasion techniques, including distributed data-receiving servers, deliberate HTTP 403 responses, and activation only when victims access targeted banking websites. Casbaneiro steals email data, performs clipboard injection, and creates fake windows for fraudulent activities. The campaign specifically targets Argentina, Peru, Colombia, and Mexico while avoiding German, French, and English language systems. The malware splits stolen data across multiple servers and uses malformed HTTP packets to complicate detection and analysis efforts.

results.name: Threat Snapshot: Djinn Stealer
results.description: Djinn Stealer is a cross-platform information stealer delivered as a second-stage payload by the TaskWeaver Node.js loader. It employs a rules-based collection engine to harvest credentials and configuration data from cloud platforms, source control systems, package registries, infrastructure tooling, AI development assistants, browsers, SSH, and cryptocurrency wallets. The stolen data is archived, encrypted, and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This threat has been observed following exploitation of the SimpleHelp vulnerability CVE-2026-48558. The stealer executes within a Node.js runtime context and communicates with command-and-control servers using encrypted channels for data exfiltration.

results.name: Mantax Otax: Indonesian Mobile Ransomware with Spyware Integration
results.description: A sophisticated mobile threat linked to Indonesian actors combines ransomware and spyware capabilities in a single attack vector. The malware is distributed via third-party file-sharing platforms through social engineering, targeting Android devices. It requests extensive permissions including device administrator, SMS, contacts, and accessibility access. The threat encrypts files using AES on Android 9 and earlier, appending .enc extensions, while stealing sensitive data including screen recordings, browser history, PINs, contacts, call logs, SMS messages, WhatsApp and Telegram chats. It establishes C2 communication via HTTPS and WebSockets using dynamic domain resolution through GitHub. Version 2 introduces UI hijacking, screen blocking, touch input interception, harassment features, and remote text-to-speech capabilities. The malware exfiltrates data through Firebase and Catbox services, enabling double-extortion through an interactive chat portal for ransom demands.

results.name: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
results.description: In September 2026, two Chinese threat actors, UTA0560 and JungleBamboo, were observed exploiting an identical Chrome zero-day vulnerability chain targeting NGOs and other organizations. The exploitation leveraged CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491 in Chrome alongside CVE-2026-85880 in Windows kernel. These vulnerabilities had been patched in Chromium source code but not yet released to Chrome users, creating a patch-gap exploitation window. UTA0560 conducted spear-phishing campaigns using financial lures to deliver GRIMWEDGE JScript backdoor for reconnaissance and command execution. JungleBamboo employed generic phishing themes to deploy SUPERSTOMP loader, which installed the LONGTALE Chrome extension designed for credential theft, keylogging, and surveillance. Both actors used byte-for-byte identical shellcode, suggesting a shared exploit supply chain while deploying distinct post-exploitation tools tailored to their operational objectives.

results.name: Active exploitation of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center vulnerabilities
results.description: Cisco Talos is tracking active exploitation of two vulnerabilities in Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Software. CVE-2026-20079 is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability allowing remote attackers to execute scripts and obtain root access. CVE-2026-20316 enables remote login using low-privileged accounts and can be chained with other vulnerabilities for privilege escalation. Three distinct threat actor clusters have been identified conducting post-compromise activities: UAT-12197 deployed web shells and credential theft tools; UAT-11823, overlapping with Russian APT Sandworm, deployed Cyclops Blink malware and established reverse shells; UAT-11988, a Qilin ransomware operator, conducted extensive reconnaissance, credential harvesting, and deployed ransomware after establishing persistent network access through tunneling tools. Customers are strongly advised to apply available hotfixes immediately.

results.name: Agents Gone Wild: An AI-Orchestrated Global Campaign Against PaperCut NG/MF
results.description: A likely Russian-speaking malicious cyber actor leveraged artificial intelligence to orchestrate a global campaign exploiting PaperCut NG/MF print management software via CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078. Using AI agents powered by DeepSeek models and OpenAI's Codex, the adversary moved from empty workspace to first remote code execution in under four hours, compromising at least 440 PaperCut instances across 395 organizations in 48 countries. The campaign originated from IP 45.142.193.132, which had been tracked since July 2026 for attacks against various technologies. The adversary developed and tested exploits in a self-hosted lab environment before launching coordinated attacks using AI agents to achieve rapid compromise, with the fastest domain admin access achieved in just five minutes. Domain administrator access was confirmed in 12 organizations, primarily affecting educational institutions in the United States.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: Warden Stealer: The Rapid Rise of an Infostealer with an Appetite for AI Agent Data
results.description: Warden Stealer is an emerging Rust-based infostealer-as-a-service that has rapidly become one of the most prevalent threats, distributed via malware-as-a-service model since August 2026. Unlike most competitors, it includes a dedicated loader and built-in cryptocurrency clipper. The malware targets over 200 cryptocurrency wallet extensions, 360+ applications across 13 categories, and is notably one of the first infostealers specifically collecting AI assistant and agentic coding tool data, including tokens, credentials, and prompt histories from Claude, Codex, Grok, and Cursor. Operating through tiered subscriptions ranging from $149 for three days to $1,500 monthly, Warden Stealer employs sophisticated obfuscation techniques, morphing capabilities, and bypasses Application-Bound Encryption to steal browser data. The malware avoids CIS and Baltic countries and is distributed through cracked software, game cheats, malvertising, and ClickFix campaigns.

results.name: US disrupts Chinese hacking tools as 7 govts warn of PRC spies stealing sensitive data worldwide
results.description: The FBI seized seven web domains linked to Integrity Technology Group, a Chinese security firm allegedly providing hacking tools to Beijing-backed operatives. These tools enabled attacks on critical infrastructure, including a South Carolina power company and universities in Taiwan. The Flax Typhoon group utilized a Mirai-based botnet from 2021 to infect internet-connected devices, scan networks, and launch cyberattacks while concealing Chinese government hackers' locations. The malicious activity involved vulnerability scanning via Microscan tool, cross-site scripting, password spraying on Microsoft Exchange servers, and data exfiltration using FishHub malware. A joint advisory from US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain warned that Chinese state-sponsored actors continue targeting organizations worldwide to steal sensitive information from critical infrastructure networks.

results.name: Suspected TraderTraitor Group Uses Trojanized Terraform Provider to Deliver Cross-Platform Malware
results.description: In July 2026, Zscaler ThreatLabz uncovered a sophisticated campaign utilizing a trojanized Terraform provider to deliver cross-platform malware targeting cryptocurrency and Web3 developers. The attack begins with a malicious Terraform provider that downloads a Bash loader from a HashiCorp-themed lookalike domain, which then selects and deploys payloads tailored to the victim's operating system (macOS, Linux, or Windows). Encrypted executables are concealed within fake font files and extracted using marker-based techniques and AES-256-CBC decryption. The campaign delivers FLATROOF, a Rust-based backdoor with platform-specific persistence mechanisms and multiple C2 channels including Telegram Bot API and GitHub. Python-based information stealers target browser credentials, cookies, cryptocurrency wallet extensions, and system information. The attack culminates with ROOFDECK backdoor deployment, featuring resilient C2 discovery through cryptographically signed Pastebin dead drops and Nostr profile metadata, p...

results.name: From Guest Complaints to Malware: Blockchain Abuse Targets Hotels
results.description: Threat actors are conducting email campaigns targeting the accommodation industry using fake guest complaints, reviews, and inquiries. These emails deliver malicious LNK shortcut files disguised as images, which ultimately deploy blockchain-abusing malware families known as EtherRAT and TONResolver. Both malware types resolve command and control infrastructure by querying public blockchain APIs (Ethereum and TON respectively) instead of using hardcoded domains. This technique allows operators to rotate infrastructure cheaply through small blockchain transactions while making traditional takedown efforts ineffective. The campaigns represent an evolution from earlier Booking.com-spoofing operations that used ClickFix fake CAPTCHAs to deliver remote access trojans. The threat actors likely employ generative AI to create unique email variants, making detection more challenging.

results.name: Bypassing the Gatekeepers: How a Global Phishing Campaign Turns Google's Infrastructure into a Trust Proxy
results.description: Cybercriminals are exploiting legitimate Google infrastructure in a sophisticated phishing operation that bypasses email security gateways and enterprise firewalls. The attack chains together six distinct Google properties including Meet, Search, DoubleClick, Custom Search, Tag Manager and Analytics to proxy malicious traffic through trusted domains. Victims' email addresses are encoded in URL fragments and stripped before server-side logging. Landing pages dynamically impersonate target organizations by pulling live logos from Clearbit, capturing real-time website screenshots, and validating domains via Google's DNS API. The operation includes multilingual support for 16 languages and dual execution tracks: credential harvesting with immediate Telegram exfiltration, or silent ScreenConnect remote access tool installation. Lures span document reviews, credential expiry notices, package delivery, payment notifications, government benefits and voicemail themes targeting manufacturing, government, finance and...

results.name: Redis Cryptomining Botnet Compromised 3,562 Servers, Exposed by the Operator's Own Files
results.description: An exposed directory at 188.245.99.156 revealed a comprehensive cryptomining toolkit containing 147 files including Python exploit source code, campaign logs, and Windows registry hives. Analysis confirms 3,562 Redis servers were compromised across two campaign runs targeting 12,966 hosts. The operation exploited unauthenticated Redis instances using rogue replication techniques to inject cron jobs that deployed XMRig miners. Victims spanned Redis versions 2.8.17 through 7.2.0 across outdated and current Linux distributions, indicating misconfiguration rather than version-specific vulnerabilities. The toolkit also targeted WordPress, MongoDB, and SSH but achieved zero confirmed compromises through those vectors. A separate February 2026 open directory linked by wallet reuse revealed Meterpreter deployment capabilities, extending the operator's known activity timeline by five months. The operation mined Monero through pool.moneroocean.stream with the same wallet used on the operator's own Windows-based work...

results.name: Inside a Packed Android RAT Loader
results.description: Hagaseca is an Android malware cluster linked to exposed Android Debug Bridge (ADB) services, focusing on the THost9 RAT loader variant. The malware conceals executable code within an APK that loads tc9.dex, a stage providing shell access, file transfer, and ADB propagation capabilities. Public incidents connect THost4 and THost9 to exposed Android and Redroid systems from October 2024 through 2026. The loader uses XOR and gzip packing, establishes persistence through foreground services, exploits accessibility features for device control, and downloads additional stages from test.hagaseca.com. The tc9.dex stage implements remote administration, discovers ADB endpoints via mDNS, scans entire /16 networks, authenticates with prepared keys, and installs itself on vulnerable systems. The malware exhibits worm-like behavior, spreading opportunistically through unsecured ADB services exposed to the internet, particularly affecting Redroid container deployments and devices with public ADB over Wi-Fi.

results.name: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware
results.description: Malware authors are developing techniques to obstruct automated AI analysis by embedding natural-language instructions within their code. This 'AI-analysis evasion' targets the pipeline that extracts text from samples and submits it to language models for triage or classification. Analysis of 84 samples across four malware families (FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, and MANTLEMAZE) from January 2025 through July 2026 reveals progression from simple comments claiming benign functionality to template spraying across multiple LLM formats and intimidation tactics invoking copyright, government contracts, and security certifications. The cheapest technique—direct instructions to ignore samples—proved most effective, steering outcomes favorably for attackers in approximately 35% of test runs. However, these techniques must remain in plaintext, making them consistently detectable. The fundamental defense requires treating extracted text as evidence rather than instruction, ensuring analysis pipelines maintain exp...

results.name: ClearFake WebDAV infection chain delivers Amatera stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
results.description: An investigation revealed a sophisticated cryptocurrency and credential-stealing operation using Amatera stealer as the primary payload. The attack chain leverages Cloudflare Workers to inject JavaScript stored on BNB Smart Chain, presenting fake Google CAPTCHA prompts that lead to WebDAV-based DLL execution. Two parallel infection chains were identified, one loading through a DLL named 'pf.ch' and another through 'verification.google', both delivering Amatera stealer with different secondary payloads. The 'pf.ch' variant deployed ZigCryptoStealer via NativeAOT loader and a Go-based reverse proxy, while the 'verification.google' variant installed NetSupport Manager with C2 infrastructure in Russia. The operation affects numerous countries with primary focus on stealing cryptocurrency wallets, credentials from password managers, and various authentication data through extensive collection rules targeting over 400 applications.

results.name: Phishing Campaign Abuses Microsoft Power BI to Deploy Rogue RMMs
results.description: In September, a phishing campaign exploited legitimate Microsoft Power BI domains to distribute rogue ScreenConnect remote monitoring tools. Attackers sent phishing emails with embedded links redirecting victims to fake reference documents hosted on Power BI infrastructure. Clicking 'Download Reference' opened attacker-controlled websites that fingerprinted victims' systems and browsers before triggering malicious ScreenConnect installer downloads. The attack deployed multiple ScreenConnect instances for persistent remote access, with the second client connected to attacker infrastructure. Following deployment, threat actors executed defense evasion tools and created scheduled tasks running persistence scripts every two minutes. The campaign used browser fingerprinting and Telegram bots to filter victims and track infections, while abusing trusted Microsoft domains to bypass email security controls and increase attack credibility.

results.name: 16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Steal Cryptocurrency Wallet Credentials
results.description: A coordinated campaign of 16 malicious Firefox extensions has been identified targeting cryptocurrency wallet users. The extensions masquerade as wallet portals, desktop utilities, and browser tools while intercepting recovery phrases and private keys during wallet import flows. Four large extensions clone Rabby Wallet (misspelled as Raabby WaIIet), while twelve smaller extensions impersonate OKX Wallet. All variants capture 12- or 24-word mnemonics and private keys, transmitting stolen credentials to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers endpoints. Fifteen extensions communicate with icy-star-f45c.workers.dev infrastructure. The campaign reuses code markers, network infrastructure, and credential-handling logic, indicating connection to crypto-theft operations identified in August 2026. Mozilla has unpublished these extensions. Users who entered credentials should immediately create new wallets and transfer assets.

results.name: Inside PhantomPolia: Remus Stealer Delivery via Donut Shellcode in ClickFix Campaign
results.description: LevelBlue observed a ClickFix campaign delivering Remus Stealer through compromised websites using PhantomPolia, a JavaScript loader that retrieves encrypted configurations from Ethereum Sepolia smart contracts via public RPC endpoints. The loader decrypts configurations locally using PBKDF2 and AES-GCM to obtain C2 domains. Victims are tricked into executing PowerShell commands that retrieve and decrypt additional configurations using AES-CBC before downloading bundled installers containing AutoIt executables. The AutoIt script decrypts embedded Donut-packed shellcode and executes it from allocated memory, ultimately loading Remus Stealer. This information-stealing malware collects system data, credentials, browser information, password managers, and cryptocurrency wallets. Stolen data is compressed using custom methods and encrypted with ChaCha20 before exfiltration to attacker-controlled servers.

results.name: TensorLake npm SDK Compromised in ChainDrop Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Attack
results.description: The Tensorlake npm SDK version 0.5.144 was compromised in a ChainDrop/Shai-Hulud supply chain attack, affecting a package with approximately 12,000 weekly downloads. The malicious release contains obfuscated code that harvests credentials from multiple sources including npm tokens, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes configurations, SSH keys, and AI development tools. A preinstall hook executes the payload during installation, establishing persistence through scheduled tasks and supporting remote code execution. The attack uses an Ethereum contract to resolve command-and-control endpoints and implements a dead-man switch that monitors stolen GitHub tokens, triggering destructive actions if revoked. The malicious code can self-propagate by republishing compromised versions to other packages associated with the victim's publishing identity, extending the worm's reach across the npm ecosystem.

results.name: StyleSmuggler: Magento and Adobe Commerce 0-day RCE under active attack
results.description: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability dubbed StyleSmuggler affects all current versions of Magento and Adobe Commerce, including 2.4.9, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Active exploitation began on September 4th, 2026. The attack operates in two stages: injecting malicious PHP code into Magento's template system using styles properties to evade safeguards, then executing the poisoned code via failed payment emails. Upon successful compromise, attackers deploy a Rust-based backdoor disguised as legitimate system processes (kworker, fc-cache, or chronyd) that connects to command and control servers. The backdoor uses NTP-shaped UDP traffic for C2 communication to evade detection. A second unrelated attacker has also been observed exploiting the same vulnerability to deploy PHP web shells. Affected merchants should deploy immediate mitigation measures, scan for compromise, and temporarily disable GraphQL until an official patch is released.

results.name: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign
results.description: In June 2026, researchers uncovered BigBear 2.0, a rebranded Evilginx2-based phishing-as-a-service framework targeting Microsoft 365 credentials globally. The operation, managed by operator 'General Boss', deployed 42 VPS nodes primarily hosted on Vultr infrastructure, utilizing the 'offy' phishlet configuration. The platform employed adversary-in-the-middle techniques with geo-matched residential proxy pools across 69 countries, real-time Telegram exfiltration, and automated cookie replay to bypass MFA. The campaign exfiltrated 5,137 credential records including 474 complete MFA-bypassed authentications, 1,032 plaintext passwords, and 4,148 session cookies, affecting 3,331 unique victim IPs across 40+ countries. The multi-user PhaaS panel was leased to at least five identified affiliate operators. Custom JavaScript injections disabled FIDO2/WebAuthn MFA while residential proxies bypassed anti-bot detection, enabling persistent access to compromised Microsoft 365 environments.

results.name: Behind the Connect Button: The Fake AI Ads Campaign
results.description: Security researchers uncovered a sophisticated human-operated phishing platform disguising itself as AI advertising products for major platforms including Muse, Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity. The campaign uses a Browser-in-the-Browser technique, creating fake authentication windows that appear legitimate while remaining on phishing domains. When victims click 'Connect' buttons, operators intercept credentials and MFA challenges in real-time through a state machine that can retry passwords and adapt to different authentication methods. The platform targets advertising account managers and recruiters, with infrastructure built on Next.js and Socket.IO, reusing the same codebase across multiple brand impersonations. The operation extends beyond AI products to include refund scams and fake recruitment sites, all connected through shared backend infrastructure on Railway and Render hosting services.

results.name: Lunex Uses BYOVD to Disable Security Monitoring and Deploy Persistent Stealer
results.description: The Lunex Malware-as-a-Service platform targets Ukrainian users through fake CAPTCHA lures, deploying a sophisticated loader that exploits AMD's vulnerable PDFWKRNL.sys driver (CVE-2023-20598) to disable endpoint security products. The loader retrieves Windows kernel debugging symbols from Microsoft's Symbol Server to dynamically identify and zero security-related kernel callbacks, making the technique version-agnostic. After manipulating security controls, LunexStealer is deployed to harvest credentials from seven Chromium-based browsers and multiple cryptocurrency wallets while establishing persistent C2 access through registry keys, scheduled tasks, and Native Messaging Host registrations. This mechanism survives deletion of the primary executable and provides continued filesystem access and remote execution capabilities, demonstrating advanced evasion techniques that leave security products running while disrupting their operational visibility.

results.name: StyleSmuggler: Magento and Adobe Commerce 0-day RCE under active attack
results.description: StyleSmuggler is an unpatched zero-day vulnerability affecting all current versions of Magento and Adobe Commerce, including version 2.4.9, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Active exploitation began on September 4th, 2026. The attack operates in two stages: injecting malicious PHP code through the styles properties to evade safeguards, then executing it via failed payment email templates. The vulnerability exploits Magento's GraphQL endpoint and template system. Attackers deploy backdoors disguised as legitimate system processes, establish command and control through multiple domains using WebSocket over TLS and custom NTP-shaped traffic.
